tools.description:
Accept a claimed delivery: commits a permanent receipt. {disposition.kind} is 'work' (you will do the work, then ack_role_message) or 'no_work' (acceptance records why no work was spawned). Role work lives in this receipt and ack_role_message; it is not mirrored into wv_queue. Idempotent on same (delivery, instance, generation, kind) — a replay returns the same receiptId; a different kind returns status='conflict'. Returns {receiptId}.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

kind.description:
`"work"` records that the acceptor will do the work (then
`ack_role_message`); `"no_work"` records the `noteOrReason` and spawns
no work. Neither value writes a `wv_queue` row — role work lives only
in the acceptance receipt.

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: accept_role_message

tools.description:
Acknowledge a delivery previously accepted by this instance. Pass the {receiptId} accept_role_message returned. Idempotent: a re-ack with the same receiptId succeeds. A different receiptId or a stale (expired / released) claim fails with StaleAck. Returns {}. Acknowledgement is distinct from completing the underlying work — a work item in wv_queue remains governed by the queue state machine.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: ack_role_message

tools.description:
Add a source repo to a team. Pass `org` (owner/repo) and `team`, plus exactly one of `url` (a remote — https://…, git@…, host/owner/repo, or GitHub shorthand owner/repo — tracked on the team) or `path` (the absolute path of a folder on this machine, which is then bound as the repo's local clone). A folder is tracked as the repo its `upstream` remote names when it has one (the canonical repo in a fork workflow), else its `origin`, else `local/<folder>`; the result's `remoteName` says which remote was used. A folder inside a git repository must be that repository's root. CodeSense never clones: clone with git yourself, then pass `path` (or add by `url` and bind the clone later with attach_source_repo_path). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ owner, repo, provider, host, remoteKey, localPath, remoteName, remoteUrl } }; an unknown or archived team returns { status:"unauthorizedTeam" }; a bad URL or folder, a duplicate, or invalid source identity returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

org.description: The context-repo org slug (`owner/repo`).

path.description:
An absolute path to a folder on this machine: tracked as the repo its
git `origin` names (`local/<folder>` without one) and bound as that
repo's local clone. Pass this or `url`, not both.

team.description: The team to add the repo to.

url.description:
A remote to track: `https://…`, `git@…`, `host/owner/repo`, or GitHub
shorthand `owner/repo`. Pass this or `path`, not both.

tools.name: add_source_repo

tools.description:
`agent_create {name, runtime}` is a complete agent. Required: `name`; `runtime` (`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`: the built-in CLI; it may be omitted when your verified session has a recorded CLI, which supplies the default). Optional: `id`, `description`, `args`, `env`, `launch`, `mcpServers`, `mcpBridgeTools`, `startup`, `context`, `repoOverrides`, `permissions`, `defaultPrompt`, `scope`, `dryRun`, `sessionId`. `env` is environment variables every launch sets on the CLI (e.g. `{"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY":"1"}`), for what the CLI reads only from its environment; values are strings. CodeSense's own launch variables (its session id, API port, MCP config, activity bindings, `PATH` and `SHELL`) are always CodeSense's, and any other variable CodeSense sets for the launch wins over one of the same name. Visible to anyone who can read the agent (stored in agent.yaml); not for secrets. A prompt or routine task starting with `/name` needs `.claude/commands/name.md` or `.claude/skills/name/` (codex: `.agents/skills/name/`) in `startup`. `permissions` is the runtime's own native config, passed through verbatim and enforced by the CLI, never by CodeSense: `{claude: {allow, ask, deny, additionalDirectories, defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode}}` with Claude's own rule strings (`Bash(npm test:*)`, `mcp__slack__*`), `{codex: {approvalPolicy, sandboxMode}}`, or `{opencode: {permission}}`. Each launch gets them in its own settings, so agents in one folder never share rules; CodeSense only adds the allows its own tools need. Examples: read-only plus Slack `{"name":"Slack triage","runtime":"claude","mcpServers":["slack"],"permissions":{"claude":{"allow":["Read","Grep","Glob","mcp__slack__*"],"deny":["Edit","Write","Bash"]}}}`; build and test but never force-push `{"name":"Dev","runtime":"claude","permissions":{"claude":{"allow":["Bash(npm test:*)","Edit"],"deny":["Bash(git push --force:*)"]}}}`; codex `{"name":"Dev (codex)","runtime":"codex","permissions":{"codex":{"approvalPolicy":"on-request","sandboxMode":"workspace-write"}}}`. CodeSense sets no limits: a big startup list or broad permissions are saved as given and only reported in `warnings`. Before creating, call agent_list and prefer an agent that already fits; agent_preview takes these same fields and writes nothing, so check its `manifest.errors`, `warnings` and that `provides` has every `/name` the prompts use. The starters `builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex`, `builtin/opencode` and their `-unattended` twins are read-only: copy one to customize it. The account is not part of an agent and never goes in agent.yaml: each user runs it with their own Claude, Codex or OpenCode CLI login, chosen on their own Mac. The agent is a local file in the context repo (`config/agents/<id>/agent.yaml`, revisioned), shared with the team by the user's own git push; CodeSense never commits, pushes or tells anyone. Returns { ok:true, data:{ id, revision, context ([{path, dest?}] as stored, or null while the runtime default applies, as agent_get reports it), repo_overrides:[{repo, add, remove}], preview: the agent_get `resolved` shape (or `preview_error` when the saved agent cannot be resolved; the save stands) } }, or { ok:false, error:{code:"invalid", message, field} } (`field` names the input, e.g. `runtime`, `startup`, `permissions.claude.foo`, or an input key this tool does not take); nothing is written on an error. Read the Docs page before creating a team. Optional budgetUsd {perDay?, perWeek?}: positive finite USD for local calendar day and Monday-start week. A first cap tightens immediately. At the cap or with unpriced usage, new launches and automatic wakes are refused; a running turn finishes. Through CodeSense surfaces this approval boundary is enforced; unrestricted same-user shell agents are trusted not to edit private engine files. Use sandboxed permissions for untrusted agents. `mcpBridgeTools` scopes Codex bridge calls; see its input schema. Identity: verified connection; sessionId must match; unbound refused.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

allowWake.description:
`true` lets a routine wake a running session of this agent even while it
skips permission checks (bypass or unattended). Default false.

args.description: Extra argv words for the CLI, each its own string (never a command line).

avatar.description:
The face its sessions wear in the agents list when a launch names none:
`pack:id` from `avatar_list` (e.g. `builtin-funny:hardhat-raccoon`), or
a colour or emoji. Display only.

context.description:
The bulk content sets a workspace gets for the agent: `[{path,
dest?}]` (or bare paths), at most 32 relative prefixes, `dest` remapping
one. Omitted or `null`: the runtime's default (claude: `CLAUDE.md` +
`.claude/{commands,hooks,agents,skills}`; codex: `AGENTS.md` +
`.agents/skills`); `[]`: none. A missing prefix is a warning, never an
error; anything else is fetched at run time with hydrate_worktree.

anyOf.description: A content-relative file or directory, e.g. `docs` or `.claude/skills`.

dest.description: Where the prefix lands in the workspace instead, e.g. `plans`.

defaultPrompt.description: The prompt a launch starts with when the launcher gives none.

dryRun.description: Check everything and return the reply a create would, writing nothing.

env.description:
Environment variables every launch sets on the CLI's process, by name:
`{"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY": "1"}`. Use it for what the CLI only
reads from its environment, e.g. to run the agent on its own context
alone. Values are strings; names are letters, digits and `_`, not
starting with a digit; at most 64 variables, each value at most 4096
bytes. CodeSense's own launch variables (its session id, API port, MCP
config, activity bindings, `PATH` and `SHELL`) are always CodeSense's,
and any other variable CodeSense sets for the launch (account, MCP
scope, inbox) wins over one here of the same name. Visible to anyone
who can read the agent (stored in agent.yaml); not for secrets. Default
none.

id.description:
The agent id within its team: 1-64 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`. Default:
derived from `name`. It never changes once created.

mcpBridgeTools.description:
Codex bridge tool names (unqualified, exact); null/omitted grants all,
[] grants none. Local Codex only; remote preparation refuses explicit lists.
The generated CodeSense alias always auto-approves, including on-request
and untrusted agents. Shell/filesystem sandbox settings and other MCP
servers are unchanged. Native enabled_tools and the captured relay grant
both enforce this list; codesense_call_tool needs wrapper and target enabled.
Unknown names warn and grant nothing; excluded signal_done/read_messages/reply
warn. The bridge runs in CodeSense outside the CLI shell/filesystem sandbox;
permitted bridge tools can mutate CodeSense data.

mcpServers.description:
MCP server keys from the team's MCP config (`.mcp.json` /
`.codex/config.toml`). Default none beyond the CodeSense bridge, which is
always there.

name.description: What the agent is called, e.g. "Slack triage".

permissions.description:
The runtime's own permission config, passed to the CLI verbatim (default
none: the CLI's own defaults): `{claude: {allow, ask, deny,
additionalDirectories, defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode}}` with
Claude's own rule strings, or `{codex: {approvalPolicy, sandboxMode}}`.

repoOverrides.description:
Per-repo overrides of `context`: `[{repo: "owner/repo", add?: [path or
{path, dest?}], remove?: [globs]}]`, stored beside the agent as
`config/agents/<id>/repos/<host>/<owner>/<repo>.yaml` and part of its
revision. A `dest` may not be VCS data, a managed file such as
`.claude/settings.json`, or collide with another entry's.

items.description:
One per-repo override as the tools take it. Naming a repo replaces its
override; one with neither `add` nor `remove` removes it.

add.description: Extra context sets this repo's workspace gets.

anyOf.description: A content-relative file or directory, e.g. `docs` or `.claude/skills`.

dest.description: Where the prefix lands in the workspace instead, e.g. `plans`.

remove.description:
Globs over content paths this repo's workspace never gets, e.g.
`.claude/skills/legacy-*`.

repo.description:
`host/owner/repo`, or `owner/repo` (always github.com); a clone URL
also works.

resumeAfterRestart.description:
`true` relaunches its sessions as this Agent, with a resume brief,
after a terminal server update ends them. Default false.

role.description: Default team queue to join on launch; null means no role.

runtime.description:
`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`. Required unless CodeSense launched you and you
pass your `sessionId`, when it defaults to your own CLI.

scope.description:
`team` (default: in `org`+`team`, else the active team, where any
teammate can use and edit it) or `personal` (Only me, only when the user
asks for it: filed in your private space for `org`, which is then
required and must be an org synced on this Mac).

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

startup.description:
Ordered plain content-relative paths the agent starts with (default none: only
what CodeSense itself needs): each a file, or a directory that brings
everything under it, e.g. `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/bmad-build/`,
`.claude/commands/bmad-help.md`; never `skill:`/`command:` keys, absolute
paths, `..`, globs, reserved top-level dirs such as `.git`, duplicates or
an entry inside another. A file may list more content paths it needs in
`requires:` frontmatter, and they come along. A path no content layer has
is a manifest error, except the runtime's root instructions file
(`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`), skipped where the team has none.

startupSettings.description: Non-secret native settings saved with this agent; no global model or credential store.

tools.name: agent_create

tools.description:
Agent delete — archive any agent you can see: it leaves agent_list and pickers, its own routines (the ones that live under it) are archived with it, launches and routines that only wait on it keep resolving, and agent_unarchive brings it back (offering its routines). Required: `id`. Optional: `hard` (true removes its definition and history for good, keeping its archived routines' history; refused with `in_use` while it has active routines (archive them first) or routines wait on it finishing (change their trigger first)), `archiveRoutines` (archiving archives its routines too: with active routines the archive is refused with code `needs_confirm`, listing them in `referrers`, until you confirm with the user and pass true), `sessionId` (optional). A local edit to the context repo; tells no one. `used_by` and `in_use` list only routines you can see: a teammate's Only me routine that runs a team agent is invisible to you, so a hard delete of a team agent may still strand hidden routines, whose runs then fail `agent_unavailable`; archive a team agent unless the user is sure. Returns { ok:true, data:{ id, archived:true, revision, used_by:[routine keys], archived_routines?:[{id, name}] } }, with `hard` { ok:true, data:{ id, deleted:true } }; { ok:false, error:{code:"in_use", referrers} } (archive it instead), `read_only` for a starter (`builtin/…`, which can never be archived or deleted), or `not_found`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

archiveRoutines.description:
Archive its routines with it. Required (after the user agreed) when it
has active routines: without it the archive is refused, listing them.

hard.description:
Remove it and its history for good instead of archiving it. Refused
while anything references it.

id.description: The agent's `id` as `agent_list` returns it.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: agent_delete

tools.description:
Agent get — one agent in full, archived or not. Required: `id` (from agent_list). Returns { ok:true, data:{ id, scope, created_by, revision, archived, context ([{path, dest?}] as stored, or null while the runtime default applies; only `path`/`dest`: keys a newer build stored on an entry are in `definition` and agent_update keeps them by itself, so this list can be passed back to agent_update as it is), effective_context ([{path, dest?}]: what a launch into a repo workspace gets — `context`, else the runtime default (claude: `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/{commands,hooks,agents,skills}`, codex: `AGENTS.md` + `.agents/skills`); `[]` is none), effective_context_team_workspace ([{path, dest?}]: what a launch into the team workspace gets — `context`, else the runtime's native discovery defaults; a context worktree already has its team files, and only inherited native instructions (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/commands`, `.claude/skills`) are layered at its CWD), context_defaulted (true while `context` is null), definition (agent.yaml as stored), repo_overrides:[{repo, add, remove}] (its per-repo context overrides, applied on top of effective_context in that repo; `add` is `{path, dest?}` only, like `context`; an override holding only keys a newer build stored is not listed, so passing this list back never removes it), revisions:[{n, author, at}], resolved:{ agent:{key, revision, definition_hash}, launch (the CLI, argv, env and MCP server allowlist, bridge_tools restriction and effective_bridge_tools a launch runs), account (which of YOUR CLI logins it would use: `source` binding|runtime_default, `reason`, `spawn_eligible`), manifest (the startup manifest: entries with file hashes, generated per-launch permission settings, totals, errors), provides (`{commands, skills}`: every `/name` its startup paths bring, as a command file or a directory under `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/`), warnings, manifest_applies_at_launch, archived }, instances:[the sessions running this agent now, each a list_sessions row: {handle, displayName, state, launchedBy, unread, oldestUnreadAt, story?, workspace?, machine?, role?, avatar?, agent}], routines:[its non-archived routines: {id, name, mode (what a fire does), nextRunAt (RFC3339 or null), enabled (this Mac)}], routines_error? (why its routines could not be read; the agent still reads), context_suggestion? ({source:"projections.yml", entries:[{path, dest?}], fingerprint}: the team's retired projections.yml entries this agent's `context` lacks; offer them to the user, add them only with agent_update if they accept) } }, or { ok:false, error:{code:"not_found"} }. A launch's workspace gets the `startup` paths first, then the effective context (each file goes to the first entry that claims it); agent_preview {agent: id} shows the full resolved list for a repo workspace (with `repo`) and agent_preview {agent: id, teamWorkspace: true} for the team workspace. Its role inbox (messages to `id`) is in role_state {role: id} and inbox_list {agentId: id}. To copy an agent (a starter included: that is how one is customized), pass its `definition` to agent_create minus `created_by`, `revision` and `archived_at`, with `mcp.servers` as `mcpServers` and `mcp.bridge_tools` as `mcpBridgeTools`, the top-level `context` in place of the definition's, and your changes applied. `manifest_applies_at_launch` remains false because startup is not universal: named local product/story launches and saved-Agent launches into verified prepared remote workspaces apply selected manifests; raw runtimes and arbitrary terminal paths do not. Also returns budgetUsd {perDay?, perWeek?}, budgetPending, and spend {today, week, state: ok|warn|reached|unpriced}. Raising or removing a cap stays pending until a person accepts it in the native app. Through CodeSense surfaces this approval boundary is enforced; unrestricted same-user shell agents are trusted not to edit private engine files. Use sandboxed permissions for untrusted agents. Read the Docs page before creating a team.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

id.description: The agent's `id` as `agent_list` returns it.

tools.name: agent_get

tools.description:
List every agent you can see: your Only-me agents (private, per-org), team agents on teams synced on this Mac, and the shipped starters — `builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex` (each runtime's defaults with your own CLI login), and their `*-unattended` twins (permission checks skipped — what a background launch naming no agent runs). Starters are read-only (copy one to customize). Optional: {scope} `all` (default) | `mine` | `team` | `builtin` (view filter, not permission). {includeArchived} default false. {includeManifest} default false — resolves each agent's startup manifest (reads every startup file). Returns `{ok:true, data:[{id, name, description, runtime, launch, mcp_servers, startup_count, created_by, scope, org, team, archived, revision, manifest?:{files, bytes, error_count}}]}`. `id` is what every agent_* tool takes; `revision` is agent_update's `baseRevision`. To fork any listed agent ("Copy to Mine"), including a starter: agent_get it, then agent_create its `definition` with `scope:"personal"` + the `org`. Spend fields include budgetUsd {perDay?, perWeek?}, budgetPending, and spend {today, week, state: ok|warn|reached|unpriced}; spend counts all machines on this core.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

includeManifest.description:
Resolve each agent's startup manifest and add its `{files, bytes,
error_count}`. Default false: it reads every startup file.

scope.description:
`all` (default), `mine` (your Only me agents and the team agents you
created), `team` (team agents only) or `builtin` (the read-only starter
agents CodeSense ships: `builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex`, their unattended twins
`builtin/claude-unattended` and `builtin/codex-unattended`).

tools.name: agent_list

tools.description:
Agent preview — what an agent would resolve to, writing nothing. Takes exactly agent_create's fields (`name`, `runtime`, `id`, `description`, `args`, `env`, `launch`, `mcpServers`, `mcpBridgeTools`, `startup`, `context`, `repoOverrides`, `permissions`, `defaultPrompt`, `scope`, `org`, `team`, `sessionId`), each meaning what agent_create describes (`context` omitted or `null` is the runtime default); or `agent` (a saved agent's `id`) to preview that agent as saved instead of a draft (no draft fields then; `org`+`team` name the team it would launch into). Optional `repo` (`host/owner/repo`, or `owner/repo` which always means github.com; a clone URL also works): resolve its context for that repo's workspace (the team's `repos/{host}/{owner}/{repo}/content/` tier wins per file, and the agent's override for that repo applies); `teamWorkspace` true previews native discovery in a context worktree: team files are already checked out, with inherited native instructions (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/commands`, `.claude/skills`) layered at CWD. Returns { ok:true, data: the `resolved` shape agent_get returns (check `manifest.errors`, `warnings`, `provides`; launch.bridge_tools is the declared Codex bridge restriction, null for all, and launch.effective_bridge_tools lists the registered tools it permits; warnings explain unknown names, excluded completion/inbox tools and by-name dispatch requiring both wrapper and target) plus `context`: the want set {repo?, defaulted, entries:[{path, dest?, source: context|default|startup|repo_add, files, bytes}], files:[{destination, logical, bytes, mode, tier:{kind: repo|personal|team, …}}] (at most 500; `truncated:true` when cut), totals:{files, bytes} (every file), warnings:[{path?, code: missing|excluded|empty|unreadable|invalid|layer|unsafe_destination|collision|skipped|large, message}]} and `repo_overrides` }, or { ok:false, error:{code:"invalid", message, field} } for anything agent_create would refuse except a taken id. `agent_create` with `dryRun:true` is the same check plus the id. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

`.claude/commands/bmad-help.md`; never `skill:`/`command:` keys, absolute
paths, `..`, globs, reserved top-level dirs such as `.git`, duplicates or
an entry inside another. A file may list more content paths it needs in
`requires:` frontmatter, and they come along. A path no content layer has
is a manifest error, except the runtime's root instructions file
(`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`), skipped where the team has none.

startupSettings.description: Non-secret native settings saved with this agent; no global model or credential store.

teamWorkspace.description: Resolve the team-workspace default instead of the runtime's.

tools.name: agent_preview

tools.description:
Agent restore — make an old revision's definition current again, as a new revision (an archived agent stays archived). Required: `id`, `revision` (from agent_get `revisions`), `baseRevision` (the `revision` you last read). Optional: `sessionId`. Returns { ok:true, data:{ id, revision, archived } }, `conflict` with `current_revision`, `read_only` for a starter, `invalid` or `not_found`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

id.description: The agent's `id` as `agent_list` returns it.

revision.description: The old revision whose definition becomes current again.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: agent_restore

tools.description:
Agent unarchive — bring an archived agent back into agent_list and pickers, as a new revision. Required: `id`, `baseRevision` (the `revision` you last read). Optional: `restoreRoutines` (true also unarchives the routines its archive archived; otherwise they are offered back as `archived_routines`), `sessionId`. Returns { ok:true, data:{ id, revision, archived:false, archived_routines?:[{id, name}], restored_routines?:[{id, name}] } }, `conflict` with `current_revision`, `read_only` for a starter, or `not_found`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

id.description: The agent's `id` as `agent_list` returns it.

restoreRoutines.description:
Also unarchive the routines archiving it archived (listed as
`archived_routines` when this is false). Default false.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: agent_unarchive

tools.description:
Agent update — change any agent you can see, a teammate's team agent included (no owner checks; the revision is credited to you). Required: `id`; `baseRevision` (the `revision` you last read). Optional, each replacing what is there and omitted ones unchanged: `name`, `description`, `runtime`, `args`, `env` (replaced whole; `{}` or `null` clears it; values are strings; OTEL_* and telemetry enable/disable variables are engine-owned and refused; visible to anyone who can read the agent (stored in agent.yaml), not for secrets), `launch`, `mcpServers`, `mcpBridgeTools`, `startup` (`[]` clears a list), `context` (the content sets a launch's workspace gets, replaced whole: `[{path, dest?}]` or bare paths, at most 32, NFC, relative, no `..`, no VCS data, `dest` never a managed file or colliding with another entry; `[]` = none; `null` returns it to the runtime default, which is what a launch gets while it is absent — omit it to leave it unchanged; agent_get's `context` (and `repo_overrides`) can be passed back as it is, and keys a newer build stored on an entry are kept on the entry with the same path and `dest` (else the same path), never sent or needed in input; anything else an agent needs is fetched at run time with hydrate_worktree; e.g. `{"id":"acme/api/backend/dev","baseRevision":3,"context":["CLAUDE.md",".claude/skills",{"path":"_bmad-output/plans","dest":"plans"}]}`), `repoOverrides` (`[{repo: "host/owner/repo" or "owner/repo", add?, remove?}]`: replaces the override of each repo named, as part of the new revision; `{repo}` alone removes it), `permissions` (each runtime block given replaces that block whole, `{codex: null}` drops one, `null` drops all), `defaultPrompt`, `avatar` (a face `pack:id`, a colour or an emoji; `""` removes it), `sessionId` (optional). Each field means what agent_create describes; anything else in the stored agent.yaml is kept as it is. A local edit to the context repo, shared by the user's own git push; tells no one. Returns { ok:true, data:{ id, revision, context (null while defaulted), repo_overrides, preview } } (as agent_create); { ok:false, error:{code:"conflict", current_revision} } when it changed since `baseRevision` (nothing changed: agent_get it again and reapply); `read_only` for a starter (`builtin/…`: copy it with agent_create instead); or `invalid` / `not_found`. budgetUsd {perDay?, perWeek?} replaces the cap; null requests removal. Lowering is immediate and ratchets the local accepted ceiling. Raising or removing saves the edit as pending; only a person in the native app can accept it, never MCP or a dashboard. Through CodeSense surfaces this approval boundary is enforced; unrestricted same-user shell agents are trusted not to edit private engine files. Use sandboxed permissions for untrusted agents. Read the Docs page before creating a team. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

allowWake.description:
`true` lets a routine wake a running session of this agent even while it
skips permission checks; `false` turns that off.

avatar.description: The default face (`pack:id`, a colour or an emoji); `""` removes it.

context.description: Replaces `context`; `null` returns it to the runtime default.

anyOf.description: A content-relative file or directory, e.g. `docs` or `.claude/skills`.

dest.description: Where the prefix lands in the workspace instead, e.g. `plans`.

env.description:
Replaces the launch environment variables whole; `{}` or `null` clears
them. Values are strings. Visible to anyone who can read the agent
(stored in agent.yaml); not for secrets.

id.description: The agent's `id` as `agent_list` returns it.

mcpBridgeTools.description:
Replaces Codex's bridge tool list. Omit to keep it, null to allow all,
[] to allow none. Local Codex only. Native enabled_tools and the relay grant
enforce it; by-name dispatch needs wrapper and target enabled. Generated
bridge aliases always auto-approve without changing the CLI shell/filesystem
sandbox or other MCP servers. Unknown or excluded required tools warn.

permissions.description:
Replaces each runtime block it names (`{claude: …}` replaces only the
claude block, `{codex: null}` removes the codex one); `null` removes
every permission.

repoOverrides.description: Replaces the override of each repo it names; `{repo}` alone removes it.

items.description:
One per-repo override as the tools take it. Naming a repo replaces its
override; one with neither `add` nor `remove` removes it.

add.description: Extra context sets this repo's workspace gets.

anyOf.description: A content-relative file or directory, e.g. `docs` or `.claude/skills`.

dest.description: Where the prefix lands in the workspace instead, e.g. `plans`.

remove.description:
Globs over content paths this repo's workspace never gets, e.g.
`.claude/skills/legacy-*`.

repo.description:
`host/owner/repo`, or `owner/repo` (always github.com); a clone URL
also works.

resumeAfterRestart.description:
`true` relaunches its sessions with a resume brief after a terminal
server update; `false` turns that off.

role.description: Omit to keep the default queue, null to clear, or pass its stable id.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: agent_update

tools.description:
Apply canvas — validate + atomically write a shared Excalidraw canvas. Inputs: `path` (a target `.excalidraw` file on the codesense content rails, OR under a registered source-repo attachment / worktree for pre-release docs authoring) and `elements` (lightweight shape skeletons: `{type, x, y, width?, height?, text?, label?, points?, strokeColor?, backgroundColor?}`, where type ∈ rectangle|ellipse|diamond|text|line|arrow). Expands the skeletons into a full valid Excalidraw scene and writes it atomically — watcher-suppressed on the content rails (hot-reloads the open canvas), plain atomic write on a source-repo path (visible to `git status`). Whole-scene apply: the `elements` you pass become the ENTIRE scene. Malformed input is REJECTED before any write — fix and retry. Returns {writtenPath, elementCount}.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/calling-codesense.html

elements.description:
The full intended scene as lightweight element skeletons. Whole-scene
apply — these elements become the entire canvas.

items.description:
Agent-supplied lightweight element. Only `type`, `x`, `y` are universally
required; the rest are type-specific and defaulted during expansion.

anyOf.description: Bound text label for a container shape.

label.description: Optional bound text label for a container shape (rectangle/ellipse/diamond).

points.description:
For `line`/`arrow`: relative points `[[0,0],[dx,dy],...]`. Defaults to a
straight segment derived from width/height when omitted.

type.description: One of: rectangle, ellipse, diamond, text, line, arrow.

width.description: Shape width. Defaults to 100 for shapes; derived from `points` for lines.

path.description: Target `.excalidraw` file path on the codesense content rails.

tools.name: apply_canvas

tools.description:
Archive (`archived:true`) or unarchive (`archived:false`) a team — org-wide, reversible retirement, the same edit as the UI's Archive. An archived active team is switched off in the UI. Pass `org`, `team`, `archived`. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ orgSlug, edit:"ArchiveTeam", team } }; an unknown team returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

org.description: The context-repo org slug (`owner/repo`).

team.description: The team to archive or unarchive.

tools.name: archive_team

tools.description:
Ask the human a BLOCKING question via the CodeSense UI and wait for the answer (MCP elicitation). Pauses you until the user answers — no need to watch the terminal. Use when you hit real ambiguity you cannot resolve. While it waits, your session shows its waiting state in agent workspaces. Contrast with post_agent_message (fire-and-forget chat). Returns `{action, content}`: `accept` (`content` is the answer), `decline` (refused), `cancel` (dismissed / timed out / session died — no answer), `handled` (the human settled it themselves outside this question, e.g. did the action in the pane: check the current state before acting, and don't redo it). ALWAYS branch on `action`; never assume. Inputs: `sessionId` (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID), `question`. Optional: `options` (discrete choices), `category`/`stakes` (triage hints — never used to auto-answer).
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

category.description: Triage hint for presentation only — NEVER used to auto-answer.

options.description: Optional discrete choices; a free-text answer is expected when absent.

question.description: The question to ask the human.

sessionId.description:
The calling session's tab id — pass your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`.
The UI routes the question to the surface bound to this session, and the
session-death sweep keys off it.

stakes.description: Urgency/impact hint for presentation only — NEVER used to auto-answer.

tools.name: ask_user

tools.description:
Attach an existing local context checkout in place. No provider account, remote URL or active team required. Never copies files or runs Git transport. Paths are on this Mac.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

clonePath.description: Absolute path to the existing checkout on the local desktop.

tools.name: attach_context_repository

tools.description:
Bind (or rebind) a local clone to one of a team's source repos, so worktrees, terminals and editor actions find its code. Pass `org`, `team`, `repo` (owner/repo, or host/owner/repo when the same owner/repo is on two forges) and `path` — the absolute path of a git working tree's root with a remote that names that repo. Remotes are tried `origin`, then `upstream`, then the rest, so a fork whose `upstream` is the team's repo binds; the result's `remoteName` says which remote matched. A folder that is not a working-tree root (the error names the root to pick), has no remote, or has no remote naming the repo is refused. Rebinding replaces the previous clone. CodeSense never clones: clone with git first. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ owner, repo, provider, host, remoteKey, localPath, remoteName, remoteUrl } }; an unknown team returns { status:"unauthorizedTeam" }; a repo the team does not track or a bad clone returns { status:"validation", message }.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

path.description: Absolute path to a git working tree whose `origin` is `repo`.

repo.description:
One of the team's source repos: `owner/repo`, or `host/owner/repo`
when the same `owner/repo` is on two forges.

tools.name: attach_source_repo_path

tools.description:
Avatar add — make an image a face agents can wear. Workflow: 1) fetch or draw the image yourself and crop it roughly square (PNG, WebP or SVG; at most 1 MB and 1024px a side; 64px or more looks best); 2) save it into the pack folder, `<add_to>/<pack>/` from avatar_list (or anywhere on this machine: it is copied in as `<id>.<ext>`); 3) call avatar_add. It checks the file, cleans an SVG (no scripts, event handlers, foreignObject or references outside the file), writes a 64px `<name>.small.png` beside a PNG or WebP for the list, and adds or replaces the face in the pack's `pack.yaml` (written atomically; entries it does not touch are kept). Required: `pack` (the folder name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 32, not starting `builtin-`; made on first add), `id` (at most 31, same characters; a face with this id is replaced), `file` (the image's path). Optional: `label` (e.g. "Grumpy"), `scope` (`team` default: the active team's content, which teammates get once it is pushed with git; `personal`: your private space for the open org, which only you see), `packName` (the display name of a new pack). Nobody's permission is checked: any teammate may change a team pack. Use images the team may use. Returns { ok:true, data:{ ref (e.g. `office:grumpy`, for open_workspace `avatar`), scope, pack_dir, file, small_file?, manifest, replaced, warnings } }, or { ok:false, error:{ code:"invalid", message } } (an unsupported format, not roughly square, too large, a bad id, an unreadable pack.yaml): nothing is written then.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

file.description:
The image (PNG, WebP or SVG; roughly square; at most 1 MB and 1024px a
side): a path inside the pack folder (used where it is), or any other
absolute path on this machine (copied in as `<id>.<ext>`). A relative
path is read from the pack folder.

id.description:
The face's id within the pack: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at
most 31 characters. An existing face with this id is replaced.

label.description: A short display label, e.g. "Grumpy Cat".

pack.description:
The pack (its folder name under `avatars/`): lowercase letters, digits
and dashes, at most 32 characters, not starting `builtin-`. Created on
first add.

packName.description:
The pack's display name when this add creates the pack (default: from
its folder name).

scope.description:
`team` (default: the active team's content, shared with teammates when
you push it) or `personal` (your private space for the open org: only
you see it).

tools.name: avatar_add

tools.description:
Avatar list — the faces agents can wear in the agents list, for the active team: the team's packs (folders `avatars/<pack>/` in its content, shared with teammates once pushed), your personal packs (your private space for the open org: only you see them), then the built-in packs `builtin-chess`, `builtin-funny` and `builtin-crest`. A face is named `pack:id`; pass that as `avatar` to open_workspace (display only). Optional: `check` (a list of `pack:id` refs; each comes back in `checked` as available on this machine or not, with why: a ref to a pack this machine does not have, such as a teammate's personal pack, simply shows the next fallback face). An agent with no face of its own (none at launch, none in its definition, none picked by a person) is dealt one from the team default pack, stably by its name; the default pack is `default_pack` in `avatars/settings.yaml` in the team content (unset: `builtin-funny`). An agent definition can carry its own default face as `avatar` (agent_create / agent_update). Returns { ok:true, data:{ team, default_pack, packs:[{ id, name, scope: team|personal|builtin, dir?, faces:[{ ref, id, label?, file? }] }], add_to:{ team, personal } (the `avatars/` folders a new pack goes under), warnings:[packs and faces skipped, with why], checked? } }. To add a face, see avatar_add.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

check.description:
Face references (`pack:id`) to check: each comes back in `checked` as
available on this machine or not, with why.

tools.name: avatar_list

tools.description:
Avatar share — copy one of your personal avatar packs into the active team's content, so every teammate gets its faces once it is pushed with git. The pack keeps its id, so a face already in use (`pack:id`, e.g. an agent's `avatar`) now resolves to the team's copy for everyone; your personal pack stays, for your org's other teams, and in this team it is listed once, as the team's (`personal_copy: true` in avatar_list). Required: `pack` (a pack avatar_list shows with `scope: personal`). Nobody's permission is checked. Returns { ok:true, data:{ pack, pack_dir } }, or { ok:false, error:{ code:"invalid", message } } when the team already has a pack with that id (rename your pack's folder first), the pack holds a link, it is not one of your packs, or the active team is not synced on this machine: nothing is written then.
Docs: arc-e-agents/agent-design.html

pack.description:
The id of one of your personal packs (its folder under your
`add_to.personal`), as avatar_list lists it with `scope: personal`.

tools.name: avatar_share

tools.description:
Cancel a running explicit context operation (hydrate_worktree, hydrate_story, reverse_sync_worktree) by its operationId. A hydrate stops between files (locally) or before its Apply (on a machine): no partial file is left in the workspace, and the result says cancelled and lists what had already landed. A publish stops before it writes team content. Returns {operationId, cancelling: true} when it was running, else {cancelling: false, state}.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

operationId.description: The id an operation returned (or the `requestId` of a selected one).

tools.name: cancel_context_operation

tools.description:
Request cancellation of one owned remote task. A cancelled status requires confirmed owned process termination; an unknown outcome is not proof of stopping.
Docs: arc-e-agents/spend-caps.html
tools.name: cancel_remote_agent_task

tools.description:
Cancel wakeup — stop one timer on YOUR OWN session; a fire it already queued is dropped, nothing is typed. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused), `timerId` (from schedule_wakeup or list_wakeups). On a machine whose desktop is away, the machine answers it. Returns { cancelled } — false when your session has no such active timer. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; a supplied sessionId must name that caller, and an unbound caller is refused.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

sessionId.description: Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`.

timerId.description: The timer, from schedule_wakeup or list_wakeups.

tools.name: cancel_wakeup

tools.description:
Explicitly open the secure local passphrase dialog for keyPath. Returns only a credential reference or cancelled; no passphrase crosses MCP.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/machine-tools.html
tools.name: capture_machine_passphrase

tools.description:
Take messages from a role's queue so no other holder works them. Args: {team} `{org, team}`, {role}, {instanceId} and {generation} exactly as register_role returned them; {limit} optional, 1-50, default 50. Returns {deliveries: [{deliveryId, messageId, role, claimToken, claimExpiresAt, text, from, createdAtMs, existingReceipt?}]}, oldest first; an empty list means the queue is empty. text/from/createdAtMs are the message itself (createdAtMs epoch ms), so no second read is needed. claimToken is this claim's proof: pass it to accept_role_message, then ack_role_message. claimExpiresAt is epoch seconds; while your session runs (registered with sessionId) CodeSense keeps your claims alive with your registration, otherwise accept and ack before it or the message returns to the queue. existingReceipt {receiptId, kind, queueItemId}, when present, means an earlier holder already accepted this message: do not accept again, finish the work and ack_role_message with that receiptId. queueItemId is deprecated and always null for new receipts — role work is not mirrored into wv_queue. Reading the inbox never claims; only this verb does, in one atomic step. Fails with 'registration is stale or expired' when your registration lapsed or the generation is wrong: call register_role again and use the generation it returns. Next: accept_role_message.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

limit.description: Up to 50. Omit for the default (50).

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: claim_role_messages

tools.description:
Close a terminal tab opened with open_terminal_tab or open_remote_tab, the symmetric counterpart of the open verbs. Args: {handle} only, no {tab}/{machine}/{workspace} name address (the opaque handle from the open or from list_sessions; a raw sessionId is refused). Terminates the CLI if one is running (SIGTERM then SIGKILL via the host's kill path), closes the tab, drops it from list_sessions. Works for local AND remote tabs — the handle resolves to its host transparently (same way read_terminal_tab does). Idempotent: a handle whose session is already gone returns { closed: true, alreadyClosed: true } instead of refusing; a handle nothing ever had returns { closed: false, reason: "unknownHandle" }. A session trying to close its own tab mid-call is refused with { closed: false, reason: "selfClose" } (the reply would never reach it). Does NOT remove the worktree or its files: a tab close never touches them, even when it is the last tab. close_workspace ends every session in a workspace and keeps its files too. Removing a worktree is a separate, explicit act. Gated by the trusted-side Interactive tier. Returns { closed, hadCliRunning, remote, alreadyClosed? }.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

handle.description:
The opaque tab handle from `open_terminal_tab`, `open_remote_tab` or
`list_sessions`. A raw sessionId is refused with `unknownHandle`.

tools.name: close_terminal_tab

tools.description:
Close a workspace: ends every live terminal session in it (every tab, on every machine that holds it) and removes its pill from the workspace tray. Close keeps files: the worktree, its files and its git registration are never removed by this verb. Address it by {story_id} (the story) OR {workspace_id} (the raw viewer id — root:/story:/generic: etc.). A story with no tray row still closes the sessions filed under its story. REFUSALS: { closed: false, reason: "discardUnsavedRefused" } when discardUnsaved is true (close never removes a worktree; removing one is a separate explicit act in the Worktrees panel); { closed: false, reason: "selfClose" } when the caller's own session is one of the workspace's tabs; { closed: false, reason: "ambiguousWorkspace" } when a bare story_id has live sessions in more than one team; { closed: false, reason: "unknownWorkspace" } for a workspace_id nothing holds; { closed: false, reason: "tabsNotClosed", failed: [...] } when a session would not end (its pill stays). IDEMPOTENT: a workspace already closed returns { closed: true, alreadyClosed: true, tabsClosed: [], worktreeRemoved: false }. Returns { closed, tabsClosed: [handle...] (the sessions this call ended), workspaceRetired (its pill was removed from viewer state and the saved state), worktreeRemoved: false }. Does NOT archive the agent definition (agent_delete does that), and does NOT touch chat history or documents. Gated by the trusted-side Interactive tier.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

discardUnsaved.description:
Always refused. Close keeps the worktree and its files; removing a
worktree is a separate, explicit act.

machine_id.description:
Accepted for compatibility and ignored: the sessions are found by
workspace key on every machine that holds them.

story_id.description: The story whose workspace to close. Resolves trusted-side.

workspace_id.description:
The raw viewer workspace id (`root:/story:/generic:` etc.) when not
addressing by story.

tools.name: close_workspace

tools.description:
Invoke a CodeSense MCP tool by name with an arguments object — escape hatch for hosts that cannot dispatch outside tools/list. Hosts that already route by name should just call the tool directly after `codesense_get_tool_schema`. Args: {name}, {arguments} (defaults to {}). Returns the inner tool's result verbatim. Cannot invoke itself (returns an error). The usual MCP permission layer applies.
Docs: mcp-explorer.html

arguments.description:
Arguments object the inner tool expects. Defaults to `{}` (no args).

Typed as `Map<String, Value>` (not `Value`) so the `JsonSchema` derive
emits `type: "object"`. Strict MCP clients that drive untyped
parameters serialize to strings — spelling the type here keeps the
escape hatch callable from those hosts.

name.description: The exact tool name to invoke.

tools.name: codesense_call_tool

tools.description:
Return the full description + input JSON schema for one CodeSense MCP tool, so an agent knows how to call a tool after `codesense_search_tools` surfaced its name. Args: {name}. Returns `{name, description, inputSchema}` or `{status:"unknown", name}` if no tool by that name is registered. Prefer calling the tool directly by name after this; use `codesense_call_tool` only on a host that cannot dispatch outside tools/list.
Docs: mcp-explorer.html
tools.name: codesense_get_tool_schema

tools.description:
Overview of CodeSense right now, in ONE read-only call: start here to answer any question about CodeSense state. Returns { generatedAt, context (active org/team), machines (connection status), sessions (running agents/terminals by state and machine, who launched whom, who needs you), agents (saved Agents), routines (enabled, last run, needs you), inbox (human unread; sessions with unread mail), roleQueues (per role in the active team: pending/claimed/accepted deliveries and live instances), workspaces (open workspaces and their tabs), docs (where the bundled CodeSense docs and the concepts guide are) }. Each section has `detail`: the tools to call for the full data. A section that could not be read has `error` instead of data; the rest still answer. Lists are capped (`truncated: true` when cut). Optional {guide: true}: return the concepts guide instead (how CodeSense works: orgs, teams, content layers, workspaces, machines, sessions, Agents, roles, inboxes, routines, notes, dashboards, each with its MCP tools).
Docs: arc-a-first-touch/identity-menu-and-switcher.html

guide.description:
Return the concepts guide (how CodeSense works, with the tool for each concept)
instead of the state overview. Default false.

tools.name: codesense_overview

tools.description:
Find a CodeSense MCP tool by keyword among every tool the server offers. tools/list advertises all of them, but a client that loads tool schemas lazily (Claude Code does) shows only names, so search by what you want to do: substring over each tool's name + family + description, then call `codesense_get_tool_schema` for its inputs. Args: {query} (substring; case-insensitive; multiple terms are AND-matched). Optional: {limit} (default 20, max 100). Returns `{tools: [{name, description}]}` sorted by match score — name hits beat description hits; name and family matches precede prose matches, with stable catalog and name ties.
Docs: mcp-explorer.html

query.description:
Substring query — case-insensitive. Multiple whitespace-separated terms
are AND-matched; each term must appear in either the tool name or the
description. A name hit scores higher than a description hit.

tools.name: codesense_search_tools

tools.description:
List the commands the slot dashboards (right-pane, dock and file-nav) declare that you may run: `[{id, label, scope, binding, dashboard, active, humanOnly}]`. `id` is what command_run takes. `scope` is where the person's chord fires (`global`, `slot-visible`, `slot-focused`); it doesn't limit command_run. `binding` is the person's current chord (empty when none). `active` is false while the dashboard has narrowed its commands with codesense.commands.register; an inactive command can't run. `humanOnly` commands are the person's: command_run refuses them. A dashboard whose policy grant lacks commands:run is left out. The page verb codesense.commands.list() returns the same rows.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/calling-codesense.html
tools.name: command_list

tools.description:
Run a slot dashboard's command by `id` from command_list, with optional `args` for the page. The app reveals the dashboard's slot if it is closed and delivers the command once, after the page is ready, as the person's chord does. Returns {requested:true} once dispatched; the page acts on its own. Refused with `denied: grant` when the dashboard's policy grant lacks commands:run, `denied: … is for humans only` for a humanOnly command, `unavailable:` for an inactive one, and `unknown command` for an id command_list doesn't list. The page verb codesense.commands.run(id, args) does the same for the person.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/calling-codesense.html

args.description: Passed to the page's `onCommand` callback as `args`.

id.description: A command id from `command_list` (`<dashboard>/<command>`).

tools.name: command_run

tools.description:
Apply an existing registry edit to a local organization working tree, without commit or transport. Pass orgSlug and edit, e.g. {type:'CreateTeam',team_name:'engineering'}. Supports team create/rename/archive/delete/parent and source repository registration through the same desktop registry service. Creator identity comes from the selected local profile; no active team needed. Emits org-registry-changed so the UI reloads. Paths are on this Mac.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

edit.description:
Existing registry edit, e.g. {"type":"CreateTeam","team_name":"engineering"}.
Creator identity is supplied by the selected local profile.

oneOf.description:
Append a new person to `people.yml` by GitHub username. The
Tauri command resolves the username to a full profile before
this variant reaches `apply_add_person` — `apply_registry_edit`
does NOT handle this variant directly (it requires network).

Remove a person from `people.yml`. Single commit, single-file
`AppliedEdit` (teams no longer carry members).
Remove any roster person by their stable, provider-independent key.
Append a source repo slug to a team's `source_repos` in `teams.yml`.
Remove a source repo slug from a team's `source_repos` in `teams.yml`.

Append a brand-new team to `teams.yml` (`source_repos` empty). The
creator's profile rides in the payload (not resolved via network) so this
stays a pure file-mutation; it is appended to `people.yml` if absent so
the org roster records the creator (open access — `connect_to_org` does
not seed the joiner). Teams no longer carry members, so the team
entry itself only names the team.

DE-REGISTER a team — strip its entry from `teams.yml` and
nothing else (AC-3). Content under `_team/{team}/`, installs, worktree
config, and the `.meta/` mirror are deliberately left on disk; the
removed entry is a revertible commit, so a delete is git-recoverable.
Local-only, mirrors `CreateTeam` (no remote write / PR).

Set (or clear) a team's `archived` flag in `teams.yml`. Archive
is org-wide, reversible retirement — distinct from the per-user
`shownTeamsByOrgSlug` hide (AC-4). `archived: false` unarchives.
Local-only.

Rename a team in place: rewrite its `name` in `teams.yml` AND move
everything keyed by the old name (its `_team/{name}/` content subtree,
its `installs/{org}/{name}/…` lockfiles, and any team-keyed metadata).
Unlike every other variant this is NOT a pure `(path, bytes)` file-write
— it moves directories across the git / non-git boundary, so it is
rejected by `apply_registry_edit` and handled by the dedicated
`rename_team` orchestrator (see `team_rename.rs`), which owns the
pre-flight, the single commit, the guarded non-git moves, and rollback.

Set (or clear) a team's `parent_team` in `teams.yml`. `None`
clears the link (the team becomes a root). A pure in-place field flip —
mirrors `ArchiveTeam`: only the matched entry changes, so untouched teams
serialize byte-stable. Local-only. Cycles and dangling parents are caught
at load time; the picker prevents cycles at write time.

Set (or clear) a team's starter page — `teams.yml` `landing_page:`, the
file the viewer opens whenever the team has nothing open. `Some(path)` is
relative to the team's content folder and must name a file there (no
`..`, no hidden file or folder); `None` removes the key, so the app falls
back to README.md / README.html / index.html. A pure in-place field flip
like `SetTeamParent`: untouched teams serialize byte-stable. Local-only.

Set (or clear) the per-org `workspace_root_dir` in
`org.yml::config_flags`. `Some(abs_path)` points managed clones at a
visible root; `None` reverts to the hidden default. A pure single-file
`org.yml` rewrite — mirrors `RenameWorkspace`/`apply_rename`. Affects only
FUTURE clones (existing managed clones stay put). Local-only.

tools.description:
The team's context repo history: what changed, by whom, on which branch. Read-only, local (no network), newest first, paged. Args (all optional): {branch} "all" (default: every branch, remote branch and open PR head), "main" (the main line, first parents), or a branch name (that branch's own commits, then the commit it left main from, marked forkPoint); {team} a team name to keep only commits that changed that team's content; {paths} repo-relative paths, keeping only commits that changed a file under one of them; {limit} (default 60, max 500); {cursor} the nextCursor of the previous page. Returns {commits: [{sha, shortSha, parents, refs: [{name, kind: local|remote|tag|head}], subject, author, byYou, committedAt (unix s), pr (the PR it merged, from the subject), lane: main|merged|open|local|backup, localOnly (not on GitHub yet), agent: {name, avatar?} (from Actor-Name or an agent Co-Authored-By trailer), forkPoint}], nextCursor, openPrs: [{number, sha, branch?}] (from PR head refs fetched into the clone, e.g. refs/remotes/pr/24), branches: [names, main first]}. A commit's files: get_publish_set does the working tree; to read one commit's changes use git show in the repo. Which repo: {org} (an org slug), else {sessionId} (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID: the org that session was launched in), else the org of the tab this MCP connection runs in, else the org shown in the app; the result's `org` and `repoPath` say which was used.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

org.description: The org slug whose context repo to use.

paths.description: Repo-relative paths: keep only commits that changed a file under one of them.

sessionId.description: Your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID (or a list_sessions handle): its org's context repo.

team.description: A team name: keep only commits that changed that team's content.

tools.name: context_repo_history

tools.description:
The team's context repo as git sees it, right now. Read-only. Returns {branch (null when HEAD is detached), headSha, hasUpstream, upstream (e.g. "origin/main"), ahead (commits GitHub does not have), behind (commits on GitHub this clone does not have), sync: {state: ok|syncing|failed|signin|retrying, lastSyncedAt (epoch ms of the last fetch or reported sync, or null), reason?, attempt?, maxAttempts?, progress?, noSender (true when the clone has no remote, so nothing sends its changes)}, conflicts: [{path, mine: {who, subject, at, deleted}, theirs: {...}, lastWriter, heldBack: [paths]}]}. CodeSense does not sync this repo itself: agents do the git. `syncing`/`failed` come from a merge or rebase git has in progress (failed once it has sat untouched for 10 minutes); `failed`, `signin` and `retrying` otherwise come from what the syncing agent last sent with report_context_sync. Uncommitted edits are listed by get_publish_set. Commit history is context_repo_history. Which repo: {org} (an org slug), else {sessionId} (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID: the org that session was launched in), else the org of the tab this MCP connection runs in, else the org shown in the app; the result's `org` and `repoPath` say which was used. Optional worktree (registered id or name) reads that checkout instead: ahead/behind are versus local main; uncommitted counts working-tree edits; owner is {kind:"agent",handle,name}, {kind:"person"}, or null, and agents lists the running sessions. worktree names the source and its mergeBase. No sync actions run.
Docs: arc-k-sync/index.html

org.description: The org slug whose context repo to use.

sessionId.description: Your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID (or a list_sessions handle): its org's context repo.

tools.description:
Copy content between contexts — the source-RETAINING sibling of move_between_contexts: the item is duplicated into the target and the source keeps it. Same gate ladder and precedence as move. Copying from one org's private space to another's (`personal:<a>` → `personal:<b>`, both synced on this Mac) needs no org switch — it is the app's Copy to another org. Copies into a team or another org's private space record the same `shared_by` / `shared_from` / `shared_on` frontmatter as a move (markdown only); only the item's own file is copied, never settings or anything outside it. Params, `org`/`confirmMakeShared`/`policy` resolutions, and the `{ status: "gate", reason }` shape are identical to move_between_contexts. Returns `{ status: "ok", outcome: "copied", renamedTo? }` on success.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

confirmMakeShared.description: Gate 2: confirm making a private item shared (visible to the team).

from.description: The source context's stable logical id (loses the item on a move).

logicalName.description: The stable `logicalName` of the item (from list_context_content).

org.description:
Switch into this org (with `team`) before the op so a cross-org target
becomes reachable — the same full switch as a prior set_active_team call,
so the app's view moves to that team too.

anyOf.description:
The collision-resolution policy an agent supplies to satisfy gate 4. Mirrors
the UI's Keep-both / Replace / Cancel chooser (§P step 4) as a typed param, so
the MCP and UI resolve a collision the same way. Deserialized snake_case.

oneOf.description: Land the moved/copied item under a fresh `-N` name; both survive.
Overwrite the colliding target item.

Keep the existing target item; do not move/copy over it (a no-op reject the
caller reads as "left as-is").

team.description: The team within `org` to activate; required when `org` is set.

to.description: The target context's stable logical id (gains the item).

Create content file. path is an absolute own-team content path; content defaults to empty. onCollision is fail (default) or keep-both, which chooses the first available numbered sibling. tools.description:
Create a new dashboard folder that can be published to codesense.ai as it is. Writes dashboard.yml (publish.state draft, visibility private, every written file listed in publish.files), index.html plus any extra pages, a shared style.css and app.js, and data/<name>.json files. The pages load their data with fetch("data/<name>.json") relative to themselves, link to each other by relative file name and make no bridge calls, so they work in the CodeSense viewer on this Mac and in the hosted viewer. folder must be absolute and must not exist yet or be empty; slug is 3 to 40 of a-z, 0-9, -; title 1 to 200 characters; pages are extra file names such as runs.html; data maps a name to its first JSON content (default one data/summary.json placeholder); live is the dashboard.yml live block ({queries: [names] | [] | "all", fields?, streams?}), checked against the query and stream catalogs; template workspaces instead writes the Workspaces dashboard (open workspaces, their sessions, a live read-only terminal each, phone first) with cs-live.js and vendor/xterm.js; template mission-control extends it with an agent list ordered by attention and a role line. template bug-triage adds owner-only fixed status actions, an activity feed and Work it when agent is supplied. For either live template, control: true opts into owner-only terminal input (default off); leave pages, data and live out. Nothing is written when an input is refused. Put the folder inside a team's context repo (its content folder): CodeSense shows it there, and live queryContext reads that team. Returns {folder (resolved), slug, title, state, visibility, entry, files, pages, data, live, template, team ({org, team} or null), warnings (e.g. the folder is outside a team's context repo), nextSteps}. A path with . or .. is refused, and no existing file is ever written over. Next: fill the data files, then publish_dashboard and share_dashboard. Rules and limits: get_live_data_contract, section hosted.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

agent.description: Agent id for the bug-triage template's Work it action. Omitted: only status actions.

control.description: Enable owner-only terminal control for workspaces or mission-control (default false). Writes live.control: owner. Viewers can only watch; the owner must sign in and press Take control in the shell.

data.description: Data files: name to first JSON content, written as `data/<name>.json`. Omitted: one `data/summary.json` placeholder.

folder.description: Absolute path of the new dashboard folder on this Mac. It must not exist yet, or be empty.

live.description: The dashboard.yml live block: `{"queries": ["sessions", "runs"]}`, `{"queries": []}` (owner's Mac online or not, no answers), or `{"queries": "all"}`; optional `"fields": {"queryContext": ["priority"]}` and `"streams": ["terminals"]`. Checked against the query and stream catalogs.

pages.description: Extra pages besides index.html, as file names such as `runs.html` (a-z, 0-9, -).

slug.description: The dashboard's address on codesense.ai: 3 to 40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -.

template.description: `starter` (default: pages, data files, optional live section) or `workspaces`: the team's open workspaces, their agent sessions and a live read-only terminal per session, built for a phone, with the toolkit cs-live.js and xterm.js in the folder and live streams [workspaces, terminals, terminal]. Or `mission-control`: agents ordered by attention, the same terminal view and a role line, with queries [sessions] and streams [terminals, terminal]. Or `bug-triage` with optional agent: bug status actions, capped agent launch, activity and the shared terminal. Leave pages, data and live out for live templates.

title.description: The title viewers see: 1 to 200 characters.

You are recorded as the creator. The UI shows the new team without a reload. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ orgSlug, edit:"CreateTeam", team, activated, activationError?, warnings? } }; warnings appears only when `parent` has no config/sharing.yml and so shares nothing with the new team. If the switch fails the team stays created with activated:false and activationError saying why; an invalid, reserved or duplicate name or a bad parent returns { status:"validation", message } with the registry's reason and writes nothing.

tools.description:
Setup checklist. No arguments. The first attribution replacement notice is acknowledged in its diagnostic receipt. Returns `{status:"ok", data:{activeOrg, activeTeam, orgs:[...], scratch:{orgs:[...], allOrgs}, attribution:{status, binary, gitAiVersion, daemonReachable, supportedVersions, previousBinary, warnings, capture, notesRef, notesPushRepos, daemonRepoRoots}}}`. `attribution` is the machine's line-attribution doctor: whether the exact bundled git-ai pin at ~/.codesense/bin/git-ai is installed and its managed daemon answers (`supportedVersions` names the accepted pin; `status.kind` active | off with reason | installing | install_failed with message | not_installed | unsupported_version with found | unsupported with reason | error with message). A PATH copy is never run; `warnings` reports user_copy_present, user_hooks_present, replacement and install-failure messages, or restart pending. Old or restored copies keep capture off; a restored copy reports unsupported with reason user_pinned. To reinstall, call save_source_repo_attachment with {repoPath: absolute checkout path, attribution: on}. `previousBinary` is null or {version,replacement,path}, persisted across restarts; a pending replacement warning survives restart and is shown once. Install failures stay readable until a successful retry; app restart retries them. `capture` reports the last completed startup or watcher checkpoint pass: {lastSweepAt (epoch ms or null), trigger (startup|watcher or null), clonesSwept, logsSeen, logsNew, traceRowsStored, sessionMappingRowsStored, watchErrors, lastError}. It is retained per CodeSense home in memory since app start; reads never trigger a sweep. watchErrors counts registration failures in the latest watch reconciliation. Counts cover that pass; logsNew means first-imported files, and sessionMappingRowsStored counts stored rows carrying an s_ identity. A repo's own setting can still keep a worktree off (save_source_repo_attachment `attribution`: on|off|auto). Notes stay on this Mac in refs/notes/sense (`notesRef`) unless a repo is set `notes`: push; `notesPushRepos` lists those repos. `daemonRepoRoots` counts the attached clones CodeSense lists in git-ai's daemon_repo_roots, so its daemon ignores other repos (0: no list, so every repo; null while no attached clone resolves and the list written before is kept), and a worktree of an unattached repo launches off with reason repo_not_attached until its clone is attached. Each org has `{slug, displayName, orgRoot, remoteUrl, loadErrors?, teams:[...]}`; each team has `{name, archived, parent?, starterPage?, synced, sourceRepos:[{repo, status, localPath}]}` (`starterPage`: the declared file the team opens when nothing is open, relative to its content folder; absent ⇒ README.md / README.html / index.html) where `status` is `attached` (bound to an existing checkout), `missing` (bound but the checkout is gone), or `unattached` (no checkout recorded). `scratch` is your private space (never shared), one local git repo at `scratch.repo.path`, never pushed; uncommitted counts edits no commit holds yet. Use set_viewer_state navLens source private to show it, and set_private_items_use to change a team switch. Per-org: `{counts:{notes, overlayFiles, panes, routines, agents}, offTeams, settingsDamaged}` applies only in that org; `scratch.allOrgs:{skills, prompts, snippets, templates, notApplied}` are inert files that apply across every org. Use the result to decide the next tool: create_team/set_active_team, attach_source_repo_path (for `unattached`/`missing`; never add_source_repo for an already-tracked repo), agent_list → agent_create, routine_create.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html
tools.name: describe_setup

tools.description:
Send beta feedback to the CodeSense team, the same way the person does from Help → Send beta feedback. Use it to report a CodeSense bug you hit (a tool that errors or returns something wrong, a screen that misbehaves), an idea that would make CodeSense better, or a question about how CodeSense works. The CodeSense team reads every one and replies to the person by email; it is not a support chat and you get no answer here. Args: {kind} "bug" | "idea" | "question"; {text} 1 to 5000 characters, plain words: what you did, what you expected, what happened instead, and the CodeSense tool or screen involved. Do not paste code, file contents, repository or file names, terminal output, secrets or personal details into {text}: say what kind of thing happened, not the user's work. {include_logs} optional, default false: true attaches the last 200 KB of the CodeSense app log with keys, tokens, email addresses and home folder names removed (the same log the person can choose to attach); set it only for a bug the log may explain. {session_id} optional: identity comes from the verified connection; if supplied, it must name the same caller. An unbound MCP caller is refused. The feedback is marked as from an agent and names your tab (see who_am_i). No screenshots. Beta builds only: in other builds it sends nothing and says so. Limits: 5 submissions an hour from this Mac, person and agents together. Returns {status:"ok", data:{id, kind, from, includedLogs}} or {status:"validation", data:{message}} (bad kind, empty or too long text, not a beta build, this Mac not activated, the hourly limit, or the server not reachable).
Docs: arc-n-reference/troubleshooting.html

include_logs.description:
Attach the last 200 KB of the CodeSense app log, with keys and signed tokens
removed. Default false; set it only for a bug the log may explain.

session_id.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

text.description:
1 to 5000 characters, plain words: what you did, what you expected, what happened.
No code, file contents, repository or file names, terminal output or secrets.

tools.description:
Sync status: {setupState, recentOperations, unpublished}. setupState lists the active org's story worktrees ({codeRepoPath, storyId, intendedTeam, setupComplete}; setupComplete is true once the worktree's setup — worktree.yaml — has finished). recentOperations lists the explicit context operations (hydrate_worktree, hydrate_story, reverse_sync_worktree) running now and the latest finished ones, each {operationId, kind, state: running|ready|failed|cancelled, target, startedAtMs, finishedAtMs, result summary}. unpublished: team files changed inside the active team's workspaces and not back in the team yet, like unsaved changes — {total, cleanWorkspaces, workspaces:[{target, name, state, reason?, counts, files:[{path, kind: changed|new|removed|conflict|cannotPublish, destination:{kind: team|parentTeam|private|repo|other}, changedAtMs?, reason?, workspaceHash?, teamHash?, teamPath (the team file it publishes to, on this Mac), discardable?}], lastChangedAtMs?, checkedAtMs, fresh (counted on this call, else the last count as old as checkedAtMs), machineOnline?, machineName?, cwd?}], machineWorkspaces:[{target, name, machineOnline, checkedAtMs?}] (every machine workspace of the team, clean ones too)} (or {error} when it couldn't be read). Only workspaces with edits, or not counted cleanly, are listed; state is checked, notChecked, offline (machine not connected: its last count), unfinishedCopy (an earlier copy there never finished; not counted), missing (a completed workspace whose folder no longer exists; use forget_missing_workspace to remove its entry), or unknown (reason says why). Missing folders add no edits to total. Workspaces on this Mac are counted on every call. A machine workspace shows its last count from this session; pass target:{kind:"remote",machineId,workspaceHandle} (your own, from who_am_i or list_sessions) (from list_hydrated or this list) to count it now — one read-only call, never to a disconnected machine. CodeSense's own local and generated files (.claude/settings.local.json, .mcp.json, merged launch files) and repo-tracked files are never listed. When you finish a task, settle the team-file edits you made in your workspace: publish with reverse_sync_worktree (preview_reverse_sync_worktree first), undo a copied file's edits with hydrate_worktree {paths, overwriteModified:true}, delete new files you don't want; on a conflict (the team file changed too) tell the user. Read-only. Optional context selects only the destination of new files; copied files are counted against their recorded sources, named in each row’s contexts. Accepts {kind:"team"}, {kind:"worktree",id}, or {kind:"launcher"}; omission uses your clone.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html
