tools.description:
Get CodeSense viewer state and app status. Returns app_version, repos_registered, localProfile, dependencies, and full viewer state (tabs, terminal, settings, etc.) from live in-memory state. Optional sections: [names] returns only those parts: localProfile, dependencies, or viewer fields listed below (e.g. ["navLens","openTabs"]); names that match nothing are listed in missingSections.

Viewer state fields (per-team fields are keyed by teamKey, `${orgSlug}:${teamName}`):
- openedTeams: [teamKey] — teams the user has visited this session
- activeTab: {teamKey: filePath} — which file is shown per team
- openTabs: {teamKey: [{name, path}]} — open file tabs per team
- drillPaths: {teamKey: dirPath} — nav drill root per team
- cliChrome: {visible, layoutMode, lastTerminalMode, splitRatio, expanded, agentsDockCollapsed, agentsDockWidth} — the CLI's chrome, one value for every team. A write is merged field by field and honoured as asked: the agent decides, and may leave full screen, fold the CLI or bring it back. layoutMode is 'console' (full screen), 'shared' (a pane under the viewer) or 'viewer' (folded); visibility follows it (a 'shared' write may carry visible: false), and a shown layout becomes lastTerminalMode unless the write names one. visible written alone folds the CLI (false) or brings it back in lastTerminalMode (true). splitRatio is the viewer's share of the left column above the CLI pane (clamped to 0.1..0.9); expanded zooms the focused workspace when the team has multiple tiles and stays set with fewer tiles; agentsDockWidth is px or null
- navCollapsed: {teamKey: bool} — left-nav collapsed state per team
- navLens: {teamKey: {source, view}} — context nav source (clone, private or a context worktree id or name) and view; worktrees default to changes; writing source opens the nav. Only source and view are writable.
- terminalLayout (read-only; get_viewer_state only): the terminal hosts' layouts, one snapshot per host — `workspaces` keyed `{teamKey}|{workspace id, or a story's story_id}` → {tabs: [{session, name, role, placement, state}], lastActive, grid}. Terminals are opened and closed through their host (open_terminal_tab); set_viewer_state cannot change them
- statusNavExpandedPaths: {teamKey: [dirPath]} — expanded folders in status nav per team
- rightPaneOpen: bool — right-pane visibility (global; hosts the Inbox, Notes and custom panes)
- rightPaneRatio: number — right-pane width ratio (global)
- rightPaneLayout: {sections: [{id, group: {panelIds, activePanelId}, collapsed, size}]} — the right pane's layout (global; ordered sections → tab-groups). Its panels are the Inbox (`weft-board`), Notes (`scratch`) and custom panes (`pane:…`); a panel id that is none of these is dropped. Send the whole `sections` array — partial array patches are replaced wholesale, not merged
- settings: {editor, terminal, appTheme, viewerFontSize, ...} — app settings. appTheme: codesense | dracula | github | nord | catppuccin | confluence

A caller that knows only a repoPath resolves it to a teamKey first. rightPaneOpen, rightPaneRatio and cliChrome are global, so a per-team patch of them is invalid: the app ignores it, and its next save corrects what get_viewer_state returns. set_viewer_state takes a partial JSON patch — e.g. {"openTabs": {"acme:default": [{"name": "a.md", "path": "/a.md"}]}}
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/reacting-to-state.html

sections.description:
Only these parts: `localProfile`, `dependencies`, or viewer fields (`navLens`,
`openTabs`, `terminalLayout`, `settings`, ...). Omitted: everything.

tools.description:
Hydrate story — copy a story's epic context (its epic dir, or the closure a policy names) from team content into a workspace, on This Mac or a machine. Pass target:{kind:"local",codeRepoPath,sessionId} (your $PWD and $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID) or {kind:"remote",machineId,workspaceHandle} (your own, from who_am_i or list_sessions; or the handle prepare_remote_workspace returned), storyId, and an optional closure policy {referenceDepth, ancestryLevels, siblingBreadth, maxMembers}. Forward only: it never takes the workspace's edits back into team content (reverse_sync_worktree does that), and a file you edited is kept as it is. One comparison and one batched copy; the copies are hidden from git and recorded as managed. Optional operationId (UUID): calling again with it returns the kept result. Progress arrives as agent-prepare-progress events with that operationId; cancel_context_operation stops it. Returns status (ready/failed/cancelled), written/unchanged/kept counts, a note and the story's epicDir. Optional context:{kind:"team"} (default, your clone), {kind:"worktree",id} (a registered context checkout in the same org), or {kind:"launcher"} (the launching session’s captured launcherContext). A context choice never moves git refs. Worktrees are listed by list_worktrees {kind:"context"}.
Docs: arc-k-sync/index.html

anyOf.description:
The scope dial. Each axis `0`/`false` = off. `LIGHT` (all off) is
SY-5's single-epic hydrate exactly. Serialized `camelCase` for the FE mirror
(`src/shared/lib/hydration/policy.ts`).

ancestryLevels.description:
Ancestry axis: include parent epic dirs this many levels up, bounded at
the team content root. `0` = off.

maxMembers.description: Epic-dir ceiling. On overflow the closure stops and flags `truncated`.

referenceDepth.description: Reference axis: BFS over `supporting_docs` this many hops. `0` = off.

siblingBreadth.description:
Sibling axis: include the whole surrounding epic (the parent dir's
subtree). `false` = off.

policy.description:
The closure policy: {referenceDepth, ancestryLevels, siblingBreadth,
maxMembers}. Absent: the story's own epic dir.

tools.name: hydrate_story

tools.description:
Hydrate a workspace from team content: copy the named files or context sets in, on This Mac or a machine. Pass target:{kind:"local",codeRepoPath,sessionId} (your $PWD and $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID) or {kind:"remote",machineId,workspaceHandle} (your own, from who_am_i or list_sessions), and paths:[exact files] and/or sets:[folders such as "docs" or "docs"]; with neither, the default agent context (CLAUDE.md, .claude/{runtime discovery folders}, AGENTS.md, native runtime folders). Forward only: it never publishes workspace edits. Additive: it adds missing files and refreshes ones nobody edited; prune:true also removes copies this workspace no longer wants under the paths/sets named (or the default context when none), never edited ones and never anything outside that scope. A file you edited (or one CodeSense didn't copy) is kept and reported; overwriteModified:true replaces it with the team's version (the Restore pinned files recovery). Files the repo tracks are never written. One comparison and one batched copy (on a machine: one manifest call and one batch); copies are hidden from git and recorded as managed. Optional operationId (UUID): calling again with it returns the kept result. Progress arrives as agent-prepare-progress events with that operationId; cancel_context_operation stops it, leaving no partial file. Returns status (ready/failed/cancelled), written/unchanged/kept/skipped counts with paths, and a note. Compatibility: kind:selected with requestId and items:[{ref:"doc:<path>"}] hydrates those paths; the scope-less {codeRepoPath, sessionId} form hydrates the default context. All forms are one flat object: `kind` picks the selected form, a scope-less field the scope-less form, anything else the target form. Optional context:{kind:"team"} (default, your clone), {kind:"worktree",id} (a registered context checkout in the same org), or {kind:"launcher"} (the launching session’s captured launcherContext). A context choice never moves git refs. Worktrees are listed by list_worktrees {kind:"context"}.
Docs: arc-k-sync/index.html

codeRepoPath.description: Scope-less form: the worktree root (your `$PWD`), with `sessionId`.

items.description:
Selected form (required): `[{ref:"doc:<path>"}]`, hydrated as those
paths.

kind.description:
Compatibility: `"selected"` picks the selected form (with `requestId`,
`target` and `items`).

operationId.description:
A UUID naming this operation; calling again with it returns the kept
result instead of running again. A new one is made when absent.

overwriteModified.description:
Replace files the workspace holds differently (edited, or not copied
by CodeSense) with the team's version: the "Restore pinned files"
recovery. Files the repo tracks are never touched.

prune.description:
Also remove managed files this workspace no longer wants (only ones
nobody edited). Without it a hydrate only adds and refreshes.

requestId.description: Selected form (required): the request's UUID (its operationId).

sessionId.description: Scope-less form: your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, with `codeRepoPath`.

sets.description:
Context sets: workspace-relative folders (`.claude/skills`, `docs`).
With neither paths nor sets, the runtime defaults (CLAUDE.md,
`.claude/{commands,hooks,agents,skills}`, AGENTS.md, `.agents/skills`).

target.description:
The workspace: `{kind:"local", codeRepoPath, sessionId}` or
`{kind:"remote", machineId, workspaceHandle}`. Required, except in the
scope-less form, which takes none.

tools.description:
List inbox messages WITHOUT marking anything read (read_messages is the one that drains your own unread mail). Every agent session, every role (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id) and the human (`human`) has an inbox in each team. Args, all optional: {scope} `to-human` (messages to the human), `to-agents` (to sessions and roles) or `all` — default `to-human` with no filter, `all` with one; {agentId} (a saved Agent id from agent_list: its role inbox, the inboxes of the sessions running it, and every reply under them); {sessionId} (a list_sessions handle or a session id: what that session sent and received, and the replies; pass your own $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID for your own history); {role} (messages to and from that role queue); {limit} (newest N; default 50, at most 500); {before} (a messageId: only older ones; to page, pass the last listed messageId while hasMore); {include} ["text"] for every body in full (else a body over 2 KB comes as textPreview, its first 512 bytes, with truncated:true) and ["conversations"] for the human's conversation summaries; {kind} `needs-you` | `update` (only messages of that kind, applied before {limit}; kind marks whether mail waits on the human for agent views and dashboards); {team} `{org, team}` (default: the {sessionId}'s team, else the team active in the app). Returns {messages, humanUnread, hasMore, total (messages that matched, older than before when given, ahead of limit)}; an answer stays under 64 KB, so older messages past that wait for the next page; conversations are opt-in: include:["conversations"]. `messages` is newest first: [{messageId, from, fromName, to, toName, text (or textPreview and truncated), createdAtMs, inReplyTo, inReplyToTeam, toHuman, unread, primaryFile?, archivedAtMs?, delivery, onClick?, contentType?, replyTo?, replyToName?, summary?, replyTargetEnded, via?, kind}]. `kind`: `needs-you` (waits on the human) or `update` (informational); the human Inbox shows both in conversations and counts all unread human mail, so on a message to a session or role (scope `to-agents`/`all`) it is just what the sender set — text typed into a terminal is always `update`; else the kind its sender set; else `needs-you` when it carries a `replyTo` naming someone other than the human, its sender or a role its sender holds; else `update`. `via`: `terminal` for text typed into the recipient's terminal with send_to_session (it already has it: stored read, never returned by read_messages); absent for mail. `summary`: the sender's one-line plain-text preview (show it instead of `text` in a list; absent when the sender gave none). `replyTo`: where replies to it go instead of its sender (a session handle, `human`, or `role:<id>`); `replyToName` its display name. `replyTargetEnded`: a reply would go to a session that is no longer running (it waits unread in that inbox; send to a role instead). `from`/`to` are session handles, role ids or `human`; `fromName`/`toName` their display names. `createdAtMs`/`archivedAtMs` are epoch milliseconds. `unread`: the recipient has not read it yet. `inReplyTo`: the messageId it answers (thread link). `primaryFile`: an attached team-content path. `onClick`: `{type: goto-agent|open-file|show-message}`. `contentType`: plain | markdown (default) | html. `delivery` (role messages and withdrawn ones; else null): {state, pickedUpAtMs, instance, acceptedAtMs, disposition (work|no_work), note, withdrawnAtMs} where state is `queued` (no instance holds it), `reading` (claimed), `accepted`, `done` (acknowledged) or `withdrawn`. `humanUnread` counts unread messages to the human in the whole team inbox, of both kinds. Next: answer one with reply {messageId}; see a role's queue and who holds it with role_state; see who runs with list_sessions.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

agentId.description:
A saved Agent's id (`agent_list`): its role inbox, the inboxes of its running
instances, and every reply under them.

before.description:
A messageId: only messages older than it. To page, pass the last listed messageId
while `hasMore`.

include.description: `text`: every body in full; `conversations`: the human's conversation summaries.

items.description: What an agent's `inbox_list` asks for beyond the bounded default.

oneOf.description: Every body in full, however long.
The human's conversation summaries (`conversations`).

anyOf.description:
What a message asks of the human, for agent views and dashboards. The human
inbox shows both kinds as conversations and counts all unread human mail. Stored as given on `wv_inbox.kind` (NULL when the sender set none); reads
resolve the effective kind with [`InboxMessage::effective_kind`].

oneOf.description: Waits on the human: a question, a decision, something only they can unblock.
Informational: progress, "merged", "done".

kind.description:
Only messages of this effective kind: `needs-you` (waits on the human) or
`update` (informational). Applied before `limit`.

limit.description:
At most this many messages, newest first: at most 500 (the inbox keeps the newest
500); an agent's `inbox_list` lists 50 when it names none, a page's `inbox()` 500.

role.description: A role (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id): messages to and from it, and replies.

scope.description:
`to-human` (messages to the human), `to-agents` (messages to sessions and
roles) or `all`. Default: `to-human` with no filter below, `all` with one.

sessionId.description:
A session (a `list_sessions` handle or a session id): what it sent and received,
and every reply under them.

anyOf.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

team.description:
The team `{org, team}`; default: the `sessionId`'s team, else the team active
in the app.

tools.description:
Post an item to the Inbox ("I need you"). The dead-simple outbound primitive: An agent with a verified CodeSense tab connection calls this to call a human back (an unbound CLI or trigger is refused; start it in a CodeSense terminal) — it appears on the ONE universal Inbox next to CodeSense-native items. Inputs: `title` (REQUIRED, non-blank — the headline the human lands on), optional `context` (folded into the item's sentence), optional `backlink` (a link back to the run/subject), and `need` — one of `awaiting-answer` | `needs-approval` | `needs-attention` | `awaiting-validation` | `done` (defaults to `needs-attention`) so the Inbox maps need → the matching action. This SHOWS a pending item; it does NOT gate a run. Returns {id}.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

backlink.description:
Optional backlink to the run / subject this post is about (an opaque routing
ref the Inbox row links back to). Scrubbed + bounded.

context.description:
Optional extra context, folded into the item's one-sentence summary after the
title. Scrubbed + bounded.

need.description:
The DECLARED need — one of `awaiting-answer` | `needs-approval` |
`needs-attention` | `awaiting-validation` | `done`. Defaults to
`needs-attention` when omitted, so every posted item carries a need.

title.description: The headline the human lands on — REQUIRED, non-blank. Scrubbed + bounded.

tools.description:
List context content — enumerate the content items in one Context (your private space for an org, all-orgs, All of <Team>, or a <Team> · <Repo>) by its stable logical id. Each item carries its `logicalName` (the stable id that feeds straight into move_between_contexts / copy_between_contexts / remove_from_context) and human `path`. An empty or not-yet-set-up context returns an empty list, never an error. Returns `{ items: [{ logicalName, path }] }` with context. Omit context to use file navigation: scope (team default, private, story, agent), team?, storyId?, agentId?, dir? returns {rows:[{id,path,name,kind,size?,mtime?}]}, identical to files.list. Story uses the hydrate_story default closure; agent uses its context want set. Ancestor reads use the calling session's team and return only files shared with that child.

The stable logical id of the context to enumerate: `personal:<org>` (your

List hydrated — what CodeSense copied into a workspace, from its managed record. tools.description:
List the machines an org/team sees, as the Machines panel lists them: This Mac first, then the team's shared machines, then your private ones. Required: `orgSlug`. Optional: `team` (include that team's shared machines; describe_setup lists orgs and teams). Returns `[{machineId, kind, label, scope, declaration, binding, canPublish, status, attention, capabilities, remoteMcpControl?, terminalServer?, load1?, cpuCount?, memUsedBytes?, memTotalBytes?, diskFreeBytes?, diskTotalBytes?, diskPath?, sampledAt?, machineStatsSupported?}]`. `machineId` is what open_workspace {machineId} and open_remote_tab take (`local` = This Mac). `kind`: `local` | `ssh`. `scope`: null for This Mac, `{kind:"personal"}`, or `{kind:"team", orgSlug, team}`. `declaration` (null for This Mac): the shareable half — `{host, port, jumpHost, defaultBaseDir, pinnedHostKeyFp, pinnedServerId}`; `binding`: your own connection settings for it, null when you never connected. `status.state`: `connected` (with `workspaces`, the open workspace count), `idle`, `connecting`, `handshaking`, `reconnecting` (`attempt`), `disconnected`, `unreachable` (`lastReachedAtMs`, `retryInSecs`), `connectionFailed` (`lastError`), `needsCredential`, `authFailed` (`reason`), `hostKeyChanged`, `notInstalled` (its terminal server is not installed), `versionMismatch`, `terminalServerFrozen`. `attention`: how many agents there wait on you. `capabilities.agentCallbacks`: whether agents launched there can reach this app's MCP (inbox, roles, progress, hooks): true only for a set-up private-account machine with remote MCP control on (set_machine_remote_mcp_control); a team-shared machine has none. `terminalServer` (connected machines only; absent otherwise): the running terminal server next to this app — `{serverVersion?` (the app release it was built for; absent for an older build that predates build stamps), `appVersion`, `upToDate`, `relation` (`same` | `older` | `newer` | `otherBuild`: This Mac's server belongs to another CodeSense build sharing this Mac — `upToDate` is false, but only `older` servers are out of date and offered the update), `announcedVersion`, `buildCommit?`, `builtAtMs?`, `buildDigest?`, `devBuild`, and for This Mac `serverPath`, `appServerPath` (the server this app ships), `startedAtMs`, `pid}`. A remote machine whose server is `older` also has `status.terminalServerUpdate: true`, and after connect_machine or retry_machine `status.terminalServerSessions` (the sessions an update ends; a list leaves it out). Resources are optional self-reported terminal-server observations: `load1` is the 1-minute load average, `cpuCount` logical cores; memory and disk are bytes, memory used is total minus available, disk is the volume holding the server workspace directory labelled by `diskPath`, and `sampledAt` is Unix epoch milliseconds on the server. A call reuses a sample under 30 seconds old or takes one one-shot sample without subscribing. An older server has `machineStatsSupported: false` and no resource fields: unknown (update the terminal server). Disconnected rows omit these fields. Samples are local runtime state, never synced or a reservation; re-check before depending on free disk. The visible Machines tab receives a 30-second stream through the machineStats LiveHub topic; it stops watching when hidden. No secrets are returned. A dashboard's codesense.machines() returns the same list for the page's team.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/index.html
tools.name: list_machines

tools.description:
Read durable run events on this Mac, newest first by record time (ts), then append sequence. Read-only. Required: since_ms (inclusive Unix epoch milliseconds). Optional: until_ms (inclusive epoch ms; omit for no upper bound), kinds ([outcome, advance]; omit for both, [] for none), limit (default 50, max 500; 0 uses default). CamelCase sinceMs/untilMs also accepted. Returns an array: outcomes {kind: outcome, ts, story_id, run_id, status, summary, ended_at}; advances {kind: advance, ts, story_id, from, to, trigger, by, run_id}. ts is epoch ms; ended_at is RFC3339; status is success|failed|needs-attention; trigger is human|auto-run; by is human:<login>|codesense|agent:<profile> or null; missing from/run_id/summary are null. The window filters StoreRecord.ts, not ended_at. Only outcomes and advances are returned, never transient progress. This store spans teams; scope story_id to query_context rows in your org/team before using an event in a team review. If limit is reached, narrow the time window and deduplicate boundary events. Next: read_run {runId} for outcome evidence; query_context for the story.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

kinds.description: Omit for both outcomes and advances; an empty list returns no events.

limit.description: At most this many events, newest first (default 50, max 500).

since_ms.description: Inclusive start of the window, Unix epoch milliseconds (record time).

until_ms.description: Inclusive end of the window, Unix epoch milliseconds. Omit for no upper bound.

tools.description:
List agent runs — the latest recorded outcome of every agent run on this Mac (story runs, automation and routine launches, headless agents), newest first by when it ended; what the run-detail pane shows. Read-only. Optional: `limit` (default 50, max 500). Returns `[{outcome:{story_id, run_id, status, summary?, exit_code?, started_at?, ended_at, source, automation_id?, trigger_source?, workspace?, scheduled_at?, fired_at?, artifact_ref?, work_product?, org?, team?, session_ids?}, validated, has_structured_transcript, link}]`. `status`: `success` | `failed` | `needs-attention` (as the agent reported it, or from its exit). `validated`: the state to show — `completed` | `needs-attention` | `failed`. `source`: `signal` (the agent called signal_done) | `process_exit` (from its exit code). `summary`: its signal_done summary. `story_id`: the story it worked, empty for a run outside a story. `org`, `team` (the trusted launch owner) and `session_ids` (every CodeSense session that worked the run, first seen first) join the run to its session record and usage; `link` is `linked` when the outcome names its sessions and `unlinked` for a run recorded before it did (never rewritten). Times are RFC3339. A run still going has no outcome yet and is not listed (list_sessions shows it). Next: read_run {runId: outcome.run_id} for its transcript and output. A dashboard's codesense.runs() returns the same list.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

limit.description: At most this many runs, newest first (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: list_runs

tools.description:
List every session CodeSense is running — local + remote. Returns `{sessions: [{handle, displayName, state, sessionId, effectiveStatus, crashId?, needsYouKind?, launchedBy, unread, oldestUnreadAt, mailNotice, notifiedAt, inboxWaiter, subagents?, story?, workspace?, machine?, machineId?, workspaceHandle?, role?, avatar?, agent?, progress?, launchTelemetry?, deadlineAtMs?, expiring?}]}`. `effectiveStatus` is the sessions projection's display status; `crashId`, when present, names the current crash/failure mark for dismiss_agent_mark. `needsYouKind`, when set, says why it needs you (`startup`: stuck on a startup screen). `deadlineAtMs` is the epoch-ms deadline of a bounded local launch (`open_workspace`'s `maxRuntime`), pushed later while a person types in its pane; absent for unbounded or remote rows. The row goes once the sweep's kill releases it. `expiring: true` marks the ~30s grace between the sweep's `/exit` and its kill; absent otherwise. `progress` is its latest signal_progress: `{phase, step?, total?, note?, atMs}`, phase as in signal_progress, `step` of `total`, `atMs` epoch ms; kept while the app runs. `launchTelemetry` is the saved-agent launch's record, present once finalized: `{sessionId, agent, launchMode: "shell"|"argv", metricsVersion, startedAtMs, ptyFirstByteMs?, settleMs?, injectedAtMs?, agentLiveMs?, outcome: "succeeded"|"settle_timeout"|"wait_live_elapsed"|"spawn_failed"|"canceled", errorText?, binaryPath?, binaryVersion?} — `binaryPath`/`binaryVersion` are present when the launch resolved the agent CLI (metricsVersion 3+); the shell-only `settleMs`, `injectedAtMs` are null on argv launches; absent on older sessions. `releaseQualified: false` (+`releaseNote`): its CLI release is unqualified; status, wake and usage may fail. Else absent. `agent` is the saved Agent it runs (an agent_list id; agent_get shows it with all its running instances); `role` and `avatar` are display labels its launcher gave it, not a role inbox. `state`: `running` | `idle` (turn finished) | `needs-you` (a real permission prompt, an open ask_user question, or blocked progress; never a completed needs-attention outcome) | `exited` | `offline` (machine disconnected; may still run there) | `unknown` (no observation). `subagents` counts its running subagents (absent at none); `state` stays the agent's own, so a finished turn with subagents working is `idle` with `subagents: N`, and mail reaches it as for any idle agent. `displayName` is the live tab name. `machine` is "This Mac" for local tabs; `launchedBy` is the launcher handle or null for human-launched. `unread` is this session's unread inbox count (same as read_messages with its session id; role-inbox mail excluded; null when the team is not synced here); `oldestUnreadAt` is the RFC-3339 timestamp of the oldest unread, or null when unread is 0. `mailNotice` says whether its inbox notice told the agent about that unread mail: `told` (all of it; told is not read; the agent decides when), `pending` (newer mail not announced yet), null with none unread; `notifiedAt` is when it was last told (RFC 3339) or null. `inboxWaiter` is true when new mail reaches the agent at once (an idle agent starts a turn, a running one hears at its next step or turn); false when CodeSense cannot tell it (no CLI wake path, an unnamed process, or a gone waiter), so its mail stays held. An idle Claude with a dead waiter may be recovered with a one-line inbox notice only when its input box is empty and nobody is typing; otherwise wake it with send_to_session telling it to call read_messages. A supported CLI can be inbox-ready before its first prompt once its engine and trusted observers establish readiness; startup menus, approvals and unavailable engines keep it unready. `inboxWaiter` is "unknown" for a tab on a machine that is not connected now (its waiter may still be waiting there). Listing marks nothing read (inbox_list {sessionId: handle} peeks). Optional {launched_by} filters to sessions that launcher started.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

launched_by.description: A session id or handle: list only the sessions it launched.

tools.description:
List worktrees — every managed git worktree on this Mac, as the Worktrees panel lists it (for remote machines' workspaces see list_hydrated). Read-only (it drops records of worktrees already deleted from disk and counts them in `reaped`). Optional {kind, org, team} filters. A context row is a team context worktree: id, name, orgSlug, team, branch, path, launchCwd, baseSha, createdAt, lastUsedAt, dirty, liveCliSession, agents:[{handle,name,role}], newest lastUsedAt first. Launch one with open_workspace {target:team-workspace, worktree:id or name}. Returns `{rows, reaped}`; each row has `kind` (`story` | `epicIntegration` | `orphan`: a git worktree of a managed clone with no record), `workspaceKey` (the story id, epic id, or parent clone path it groups under), `path`, `branch` (null when detached), `dirty` (uncommitted changes; null when unknown), `repoPath` (its parent clone; null when vanished), `liveCliSession` (a terminal is running in it). A `story` row adds `storyId`, `sourceRepo`, `syncStatus`, `failureReason`, `storySourcePath` (the story file), `orgSlug`, `team`, `orphaned` (its clone or story file is gone), `lastReverseSyncAt` (epoch ms its edits last synced back to context, or null) and `lastReverseSyncBy` (`user` | `agent`; `auto` only on records from before automatic sync was removed), and `attribution` (null before an agent launch; else `{status, gitAiVersion, checkedAt}`: whether git-ai line-attribution capture was working at the last launch here. `status.kind` is `active` (wired; no checkpoint proven), `off` with `reason` `disabled_for_repo` | `notes_would_push` (the git-ai in use cannot keep this repo's notes local, or the managed daemon still needs a restart: relaunch, or see describe_setup attribution warnings; notes:push publishes the repo's notes and is not a capture fix) | `not_managed_worktree` | `repo_not_attached` (this worktree's repo isn't attached on this Mac, so git-ai's daemon ignores it: attach its clone with save_source_repo_attachment to track the next launch, no app restart), `installing` (relaunch after completion), `install_failed` with `message`, `not_installed`, `unsupported_version` with `found`, `unsupported` with `reason` (e.g. `opencode`, `remote_machine`, `platform`, `newer`, `user_pinned`), or `error` with `message`; a launch never fails because of it). An `epicIntegration` row adds `epicId`, `owner`, `repo`. Empty when no team is active. A dashboard's codesense.worktrees() returns the same.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/index.html
tools.name: list_worktrees

tools.description:
Mark human-directed inbox messages unread without changing archive state. Args: {messageIds: positive integer[], org?, team?}. Pass both org and team, or omit both for this session's team (else the active team). Uses the same scoped batch operation as codesense.markUnread. Returns {marked}, counting rows that changed once. Messages addressed to agents are unchanged.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

tools.description:
Model rates — every stored price session_usage prices usage with, USD per million tokens. Read-only. No inputs. Returns `[{modelPrefix, effectiveFrom, inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok, long, source}]`, by model prefix and then by day. A model's rate on a day is the latest one from on or before that day, under its longest matching prefix. `effectiveFrom` is a local day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (`1970-01-01` for a seeded list price). `cacheReadPerMtok` null: 0.1x input. `long` null: one price at every prompt length; else `{fromTokens, inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok}`, the prices of a call whose prompt (input, cache reads and cache writes) is over `fromTokens` tokens, its `cacheReadPerMtok` null: 0.1x the long input price. `source` is `set by the user` (from a page), `set by an agent` (from set_model_rate), or the seeded list price's note. Next: set_model_rate to price a model session_usage lists in `unpricedModels`. A dashboard's codesense.modelRates() returns the same.
Docs: arc-e-agents/spend-caps.html

tools.description:
Move content between contexts — move a content item (by its stable `logicalName`) from one Context to another, both directions, any pair (private space ↔ team, team ↔ team; context ids as list_context_content takes them: `personal:<org>` names the org explicitly and must be an org synced on this Mac; `all-orgs` accepts only allowlisted inert files — markdown/plain-text skills, prompts, snippets, templates — and refuses anything else). Enforces the SAME deterministic gate ladder as the UI, ONE gate at a time in fixed order: cross-org → privacy → collision (a move lands the item somewhere, so it never asks about a sole copy; only remove_from_context does). If a gate is unmet the call returns `{ status: "gate", reason, ... }` naming the FIRST unmet gate and its resolution (switch org via set_active_team / an explicit `org`; `confirmMakeShared: true`; a collision `policy` of keep_both|replace|keep_mine) so you retry deterministically. A move out of the private space writes the target BEFORE removing the source (source-preserving on failure); if the source then can't be removed the outcome is `movedSourceKept` with a `reason`, and calling again finishes it — a target already holding exactly this item is the op done, never a collision. A path that goes through a linked folder out of its context is refused. A markdown file moved out of the private space into a team records `shared_by`, `shared_from` (its place in the private space) and `shared_on` in its frontmatter — the same record the app's Share with ‹Team› writes; other files move byte for byte. Returns `{ status: "ok", outcome, renamedTo? }` on success.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

confirmMakeShared.description: Gate 2: confirm making a private item shared (visible to the team).

from.description: The source context's stable logical id (loses the item on a move).

logicalName.description: The stable `logicalName` of the item (from list_context_content).

org.description:
Switch into this org (with `team`) before the op so a cross-org target
becomes reachable — the same full switch as a prior set_active_team call,
so the app's view moves to that team too.

anyOf.description:
The collision-resolution policy an agent supplies to satisfy gate 4. Mirrors
the UI's Keep-both / Replace / Cancel chooser (§P step 4) as a typed param, so
the MCP and UI resolve a collision the same way. Deserialized snake_case.

oneOf.description: Land the moved/copied item under a fresh `-N` name; both survive.
Overwrite the colliding target item.

Keep the existing target item; do not move/copy over it (a no-op reject the
caller reads as "left as-is").

team.description: The team within `org` to activate; required when `org` is set.

to.description: The target context's stable logical id (gains the item).

tools.name: move_between_contexts

tools.description:
Move content file — rename/move a context-layer content file OR directory in team content, preserving content + frontmatter (incl. story_id). Explicit two-path gesture — no delete+create correlation. Copies already in worktrees are NOT moved (nothing syncs a worktree on its own); call hydrate_worktree to update a worktree. Pure Rust action (headless). Inputs: `fromPath`, `toPath` (absolute context-layer paths). Returns {fromPath, toPath}.
Docs: arc-k-sync/file-tools.html

fromPath.description: Absolute context-layer source path (file or directory) being moved.

toPath.description: Absolute context-layer destination path. Must not already exist.

tools.name: move_content_file

tools.description:
Move a team's workspace to another machine. Give storyId and targetMachine (from list_machines, or local); local targets also require targetWorktreePath. Reports running agents (handle/name), uncommitted paths, unpushedCount, sourceTip and unpushedCheck (fetched or cached, with a reason). Refusals include the same report. Running source sessions refuse unless stopRunningAgents:true explicitly ends them through the normal Kill path; selfClose always refuses. Unpushed commits (rev-list tip --not --remotes) require carryUnpushed or discardUnpushed; both together is invalid. Carry uses the source branch tip without pushing: Mac to machine via bundle, machine to Mac via fast-forward-only fetch. Machine-to-machine carry refuses; move through this Mac. Dirty sources require discardUncommitted:true. Uses the existing Interactive gate with no new prompts or grants. Source cleanup follows exact target-tip verification and a fresh source-tip/session/dirty check; a changed source stays intact with cleanupPending:true and reason. Durable intents retain the failed step; boot recovery uses the same safety checks. Returns moved, from, to, handle, cwd, report, stoppedAgents, reason, cleanupPending. Does not relaunch agents.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/remote-workspaces.html

carryUnpushed.description: Policy: carry committed work without publishing it to a remote.

discardUncommitted.description:
Default `false`. When `false`, an uncommitted change on the source
worktree refuses with `dirty_worktree` (listing the dirty paths and
the flag hint).

discardUnpushed.description: Policy: explicitly release commits absent from remote-tracking refs.

stopRunningAgents.description: Policy: explicitly stop source sessions through the normal close path.

storyId.description:
Workspace handle in the active team — the viewer id, matching the
field the 7 refusal sites compare against.

targetMachine.description: Target machine id from `list_machines`, or `"local"` for This Mac.

targetWorktreePath.description:
Required when `target_machine == "local"` — the FE-derived managed
worktree path (via `render_worktree_dir(worktree.yaml, clone, branch)`).
For remote targets, this is derived server-side from the account
home and ignored if given.

tools.name: move_workspace

tools.description:

The note is committed to the notes' local history and the person's Notes pane shows it at once. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ org, note:{ id, title, pinned, lastOpenedAt, updatedAt, updatedBy }, changed:true, commit } } (`commit`: the history revision it was saved as) or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.

Notes history — who changed a private note and when, newest first. Required: `id`. Optional `org`, `limit` (default 50). Every agent write is a revision credited to its session; the person's typing becomes a revision after about 30 seconds of quiet (asking for history commits it first). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ org, id, revisions:[{ commit, at (ms), actor:{ kind: human|agent, name, sessionId?, handle?, avatar? }, change: create|write|restore|meta|delete, summary, added, removed (body lines), restoredFrom? }] } }. Read an old version with notes_read_at; bring it back with notes_restore.

tools.description:
Notes list — the person's private notes for one org: Markdown notes kept on this Mac only (never pushed or shared), each with local history. Use notes to keep plans, prompts, todos and findings the person can read in CodeSense's Notes pane; how to organise them is up to you and the person. Optional `org` (`owner/repo`): omit for the org your session works in (a remote session: its workspace's org; on this Mac: the org open in CodeSense); every notes reply names the `org` it used, so pass it back to stay on it. One org's notes are never visible from another. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ org, notes:[{ id, title, pinned, lastOpenedAt, updatedAt?, updatedBy?:{ kind: human|agent, name, sessionId?, handle?, avatar? } }] } } (pinned first, then most recently touched; bodies not included: notes_read), or { status:"validation", data:{ message } } (no org open, an org not synced on this Mac). Related: notes_search, notes_create, notes_write, notes_history.

Required: `id`, `commit` (from notes_history). Optional `org`, `sessionId` (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID, for credit). The title is left as it is. The person's open Notes pane reloads at once. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ org, note, changed, commit? } } (changed:false when the text was already that), or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.

Returns { status:"ok", data:{ org, hits:[{ id, title, matched: title|text|both, snippet? (the first matching body line) }] } }: title matches first, then body matches, most recently touched first. tools.description:
Notes write — change a private note (see notes_list). Required: `id`, and exactly one of `content` (the whole new Markdown body), `append` (text added at the end on a new line) or `patch` ({ find, replace }: `find` must occur exactly once in the body; read the note first), and/or `title` (rename). Optional `org`, `sessionId` (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID, so the change is credited to your session; a remote session is always credited to its own tab). Each change is committed to the notes' local history with you as its author, the note's updatedAt/updatedBy are set, and the person's open Notes pane reloads at once; anything the person typed before your write is committed first under their name, so notes_restore can undo you. A write that changes nothing reports changed:false and makes no commit. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ org, note:{ id, title, pinned, lastOpenedAt, updatedAt, updatedBy }, changed, commit? } }, or `validation` (no such note, no edit given, more than one of content/append/patch, a patch that matches 0 or several times). Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-l-factory/team-and-notes-tools.html

append.description: Text to add at the end, on a new line.

sessionId.description: Identity comes from the verified connection; a supplied id must name the same caller.

tools.description:
Create or Attach an exact native remote terminal tab in an already-open workspace. One flat object: operation (create|attach) picks the form, and a field the picked form does not take is refused. Create requires requestId UUID, configured machineId, teamKey, workspaceId, absolute existing host cwd; launch is shell (default), claude or codex. Desktop MCP servers come only with a saved Agent; otherwise CodeSense only, when permitted. Claude/Codex require remote MCP permission and the remote account runtime/login. Saved Agent startup uses agentKey plus preparedWorkspaceHandle from a verified prepared owned worktree; runtime and MCP servers derive from the Agent. Exact selected files, permissions and essentials finish before spawn. Attach requires exactly one handle/requestId; it can resume pinned preparation before the durable spawn attempt, then only reconciles. Retry an unknown Create only with Attach; never use a new requestId to recover. headed defaults true. Optional name (Create) is the tab name shown by list_sessions and addressed by {tab}. Create records the verified caller as launchedBy; a supplied launchedBy may only name that caller. Attach retains the existing launcher. Raw claude/codex launches ask for approval before tools run (their ordinary interactive permissions) unless Create sets permissionMode "bypass": Claude then starts with --dangerously-skip-permissions and Codex with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, still with CodeSense's MCP server, status hooks and new-mail nudges (the first bypass run on a machine account may show Claude's one-time confirmation; answer it with run_in_terminal_tab). permissionMode needs an updated terminal server on the machine (refused with code terminalServerOutdated otherwise) and does not apply to shell launches or saved Agents, which use their declared permissions. Send prompts to a launched agent with send_to_session or run_in_terminal_tab. Opening the CLI does not prove authenticated inference. Origin metadata is informational, never accepted as authority. Local open_terminal_tab remains local. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied launchedBy must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

agentKey.description: Create: the saved Agent to start.

cwd.description: Create (required): the absolute existing folder on the host.

handle.description: Attach: the tab's opaque handle (instead of `requestId`).

headed.description: Whether the tab is shown in the app; defaults to true.

launch.description: Create: what runs in the tab.

launchedBy.description:
Create: the verified MCP caller is recorded as launchedBy. A supplied value
must name that caller. Native app launches retain their own launcher.

name.description: Create: the tab name shown by list_sessions.

operation.description:
`create` opens a new tab; `attach` reconnects to one by `handle` or
`requestId`.

permissionMode.description:
Create, with launch `claude` or `codex` (not a saved Agent): `bypass`
starts it without approval prompts (Claude `--dangerously-skip-permissions`,
Codex `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`), still with
CodeSense's MCP server, status hooks and new-mail nudges. Omitted or
`default`: the runtime's ordinary approvals.

oneOf.description: The runtime's ordinary interactive approvals.

No approval prompts: the runtime's bypass flag (Claude
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, Codex `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`).

preparedWorkspaceHandle.description: Create, with `agentKey`: the verified prepared workspace.

requestId.description:
Create: required UUID naming the open. Attach: the create's requestId
(instead of `handle`).

teamKey.description: The team the workspace belongs to (`org:team`).

tools.name: open_remote_tab

tools.description:
Open a NORMAL CodeSense CLI terminal tab in an already-OPEN workspace and return its opaque {handle} (address it later with run_in_terminal_tab / read_terminal_tab). The tab is the SAME one a human opens by hand — rightmost, its shell started at the workspace cwd. Args: {workspaceId} (the viewer id of an OPEN workspace, e.g. a root:/story:/generic: id; a non-existent or non-open workspace is refused — every OPEN kind is accepted on this gated path), optional {headed} (default true → the workspace's focused tab; false → quiet, opens without taking focus), optional {name} (a display name for the tab so a fleet of tabs is legible — e.g. "build watch", "claude: triage"; omitted → the default "Terminal <n>"). Anti-forgery: the returned {handle} is opaque — a caller never learns or supplies the raw sessionId (resolved trusted-side via the launch registry). Gated by the trusted-side Interactive tier. Returns { handle, headed, kind }.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

headed.description:
`true` (default) opens a VISIBLE tab (focuses the workspace so the tab is on
screen). `false` opens it quietly, without stealing focus / switching the
active workspace.

name.description:
An optional display name for the new tab — so a spawned tab
reads as what it's FOR ("build watch", "claude: triage"). Omitted → the
default `Terminal <n>`. Additive optional param (no new command/tool).

workspaceId.description:
The viewer id of an OPEN workspace to open the tab in (e.g. a `root:<path>`
/ `story:<id>` / `generic:<path>` id). A non-existent or non-open workspace
is refused. camelCase `workspaceId` on the wire.

tools.name: open_terminal_tab

tools.description:
Open a story workspace and return its handle (the story_id — pass back as an abstract address, never a raw PTY id). Creates the managed worktree on first open (no context is copied until an agent launches there or calls hydrate_worktree/hydrate_story). Args: {story_id} (e.g. "DEMO-1"; unknown/non-managed id is refused). Optional: {mode} `headed` (default; visible + focused) | `visible-unfocused` | `headless` (background agent, opt-in); {initial_prompt} (the agent's starting prompt — a slash command works). Returns `{handle, mode, headed, reconciled}` (reconciled: `{from,to}` when the story's `branch` frontmatter was converged to the opened branch, else null). Drive with send_to_session. Gated by the Interactive tier (refuses `not-granted:`/`denied:`/`busy`).

LAUNCH AN AGENT: pass {target} `story` (with {story_id}; add {name} to open a new tab in that worktree — handle `<storyId>#<name>`; name is lowered + dash-normalized, max 64) or `team-workspace` (with {name}; a context worktree of the team's context repo, on its own branch, with CWD <team>/content. Pick an existing one by {worktree} id or name from list_worktrees {kind:context, team}, or create one with {worktree, createWorktree:true}. Pass {worktree} whenever the user named one. Omit both to reuse the most recently used, or create one named after {name} when none exists. Several agents share a worktree as tabs; reopening is the same call. Result adds worktree:{id,name,branch,created}; tell the user where it landed). Optional: {team} (defaults to your own team for agent sessions, or the active team when a person calls it; with `story`, a team other than the story's is refused), {org} (defaults to your own org; a person's story is found by id, and an id in several orgs needs org), {agent} (an agent id from agent_list; default `builtin/claude`, or `builtin/claude-unattended` for headless), {initial_prompt}, {launched_by} (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID; omit for human-launched), {queue_role} (queue id; omitted inherits the saved agent default; null joins no queue), {role} (display label; a story launch whose role or saved agent is a reviewer gets a `type: review` task with `typeSource`), {reviews} (story target only: the dev task id the reviewer reviews, linked `relates_to:reviews` exactly; omitted, the story's latest open task, `associated`), {avatar} (display only: `pack:id` from avatar_list, a `#rrggbb`, or an emoji), {max_runtime} (how long the launched session may run, like `30m` or `2h`, range 1m–24h; when it is reached the agent is sent `/exit`, then killed 30s later, and the launcher is notified; while a person types in the session's pane the deadline moves to at least 15 minutes after their last keystroke, so a session someone is using is not stopped; absent = no limit; This Mac only). Returns `{status:"opened"|"alreadyLive"|"busy"|"invalid", handle, name, message, warnings?}`. On `alreadyLive` with `maxRuntime`, the existing deadline (or lack of one) is left unchanged and the result carries a `maxRuntime ignored: session already live` warning.

ON A MACHINE: pass {story_id} + {machine_id} (from list_machines; "local" = this Mac). First open on a new machine copies the local clone there (no GitHub creds needed). To launch an agent there, add {target} `story` + {name}/{agent}/{initial_prompt}. A story whose workspace lives elsewhere is refused. With {machine_id} the call returns once the workspace is open there (status `opened`), or fails with the reason; it waits up to 10 minutes, then fails as `unconfirmed`. Team-workspace targets run on this Mac only; machine launches are never headless. {max_runtime} + a non-local {machine_id} is refused `invalid` (enforcement is This Mac only; follow-up for remote). Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied launched_by must name the caller itself. Omitted team selects the agent session's own team; human calls use the active team. A child agent cannot open a workspace on a shared parent story; a human can.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/index.html

agent.description:
The agent to launch (with `target`): its key, or a bare id found in the target
team, then your private space, then the starters. Defaults to `builtin/claude`, or
`builtin/claude-unattended` for a headless open.

avatar.description:
The face to show for the session: `pack:id` (see `avatar_list`), or a colour or
emoji hint. Display only; a face whose pack is not on this machine falls back.

createWorktree.description: Create worktree as a new name; refuse an existing name.

headed.description:
Legacy visibility toggle, kept for back-compat. Prefer
`mode`. When `mode` is absent: `Some(false)` → background (headless),
`Some(true)`/`None` → headed (visible + focused). `mode` wins when both set.

initial_prompt.description: Optional first prompt seeded into the spawned agent (e.g. "/review").

launched_by.description:
Who is launching: your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`. Omit when a person asked.
Shown as "Launched by"; nothing is checked against it.

machine_id.description:
Open the story's workspace on this machine (an id from `list_machines`, or
`local` for This Mac) instead of This Mac. Its worktree is created there on
first open; later opens reuse it. With `target: "story"` the agent launches
there; a team-workspace target runs on This Mac only.

max_runtime.description:
how long the launched session may run, like `30m` or `2h`
(range 1m–24h). When it is reached the agent is sent `/exit`, then killed
30s later, and the launcher is notified. Absent/blank: no limit. This Mac
only — combining it with a non-local `machineId` is refused.

mode.description:
How the workspace surfaces — `"headed"` (visible + focused, the
default) · `"visible-unfocused"` (a real tab that does not steal focus) ·
`"headless"` (background; opt-in only). Absent → resolved from `headed`
(default headed). An unrecognized value is refused `denied:`.

org.description: The org of the story or team. Defaults to your own org for agent sessions. For a person, the story's org is found by id, and an id in more than one org needs `org`.

queue_role.description: Team queue id; omitted inherits saved default, null joins no queue.

reviews.description:
The task a reviewer launch reviews (a task id from `task_list`). `target: "story"`
only: the launch's review task links `relates_to:reviews` to it (`fieldSources.reviews:
exact`); without it, a reviewer's task links the story's latest open task
(`associated`).

role.description:
The role to show for the session: `manager`, `worker` or any free
label (`reviewer`, `qa`). Display only; nothing is checked against it.

story_id.description:
The story id to open (e.g. "DEMO-1"). Required for a story target and
resolved trusted-side to its managed worktree; an unknown id or a story
with no worktree yet is refused (the frontend never supplies a path).
With `target: "team-workspace"`, optional:
links the session to that story without changing its context worktree.
Otherwise it inherits its launcher's known story within the same org and team.
Never inferred from names or carried implicitly across teams or orgs.

target.description:
`"story"` or `"team-workspace"`. Absent → the legacy story open (its result
shape is unchanged and the fields below are ignored).

team.description: The team to open in: defaults to your own team for agent sessions, or the active team when a person calls it. With `story`, a team other than the story's is refused.

worktree.description: Context worktree id or name. Pass it whenever the user named one.

tools.name: open_workspace

tools.description:
Pane list — the custom right panes a team sees: the panes of every team in its chain (nearest first), then your private ones for that org. The same id in two places is two entries. Optional `org`+`team` (both, or neither for the active team). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ contentRoot (the content a pane's reads resolve against), panes:[{ id, scope (team|private), team?, title, icon?, path, panesDir, panelId, modified? }] } }, or `validation`, `unauthorizedTeam`, `notSyncedLocally`. Write one with pane_write, show one with pane_open; to delete a pane, delete its file. How to write a pane (the `window.codesense` SDK, theme, errors): see pane_write; full reference: get_live_data_contract.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

org.description: The org (`owner/repo`); pass with `team`, or omit both for the active team.

team.description: The team whose chain to list; pass with `org`, or omit both.

tools.name: pane_list

tools.description:
Pane open — place a custom right pane in the right pane and reveal it (opening the right pane if closed); it stays placed across restarts like a built-in panel. Required: `id` (from pane_list or pane_write). Optional `scope` (`team` default, or `personal`), `org`, `team`, as for pane_write. Optional `intent`: an opaque JSON object of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes (larger objects return `validation`), forwarded to the page through codesense.onIntent(cb) once its shim is ready. A newer pending intent replaces an older one; delivered intents are not replayed on reload. A team pane shows while that team or a child team is active, a private one while its org is. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ panelId, path, placed } }: `placed` false (and `reason`) when the active team does not show that pane, so nothing was placed; the user must switch to its team. Or `validation` (no such pane). How to write a pane (the `window.codesense` SDK, theme, errors): see pane_write; full reference: get_live_data_contract.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

id.description: The pane id, as pane_list returns it.

intent.description: Opaque page intent, a JSON object of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

tools.name: pane_open

tools.description:
Pane write — create or replace a custom right pane in ONE call: writes `html` to `<space>/panes/<id>.html` as a plain overwrite (no merge, no revision). Required: `id`, `html` (the whole document). Optional `scope`: `team` (default; `org`+`team`, or neither for the active team) or `personal` (your private space for `org`, which is then required; only when the user asks for a private pane). The pane appears in the right pane's Panels menu at once and an open one reloads; nothing is shared until your git push. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, scope, org, team?, path, panelId, created } } or `validation` (a bad id or scope, a team not synced here). Then pane_open shows it. A pane is ONE self-contained HTML file beside `content/` and `config/`, in a team space (the team and its child teams see it; teammates get it by git push like any team file) or your private space for an org (this Mac only). `id` matches [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*; the `<title>` is its label. Other files in `panes/` (e.g. `panes/lib/chart.js`) are never panes but load as relative assets (`<script src="lib/chart.js">`). It renders in the right pane in an iframe with the same `window.codesense` SDK as an HTML dashboard: reads `codesense.queryContext(q)` (context files by metadata, resolved from the active team, so it sees the same stories a dashboard does), `codesense.sprints()`, `codesense.taxonomy()`; live updates `codesense.subscribeContext(q, (result, err) => ...)` (returns an unsubscribe); routine results `codesense.routineResult({id})`, `routineStatus`, `routineRefresh` (only on a user action), `onRoutineResult(cb)`; `codesense.readWorkspace(args)`; actions `codesense.act(verb, args)` (`openWorkspace`, `runPrompt`, `sendToSession`, ...; rate-guarded against runaway loops). Every call returns a Promise; a rejection carries the bridge's message unchanged (e.g. `unavailable: ...`) and is also echoed to the pane's error banner. Theme: the app sets its theme on the page root as CSS custom properties (`--cs-bg`, `--cs-fg`, `--cs-muted-fg`, `--cs-border`, `--cs-surface`, `--cs-accent`, `--cs-link`, `--cs-danger`, `--cs-success`, `--cs-warning`, `--cs-font-sans`) with `color-scheme` to match; style with them and keep the body background transparent, never `prefers-color-scheme` (the right pane can be dark while the app is light); `codesense.onTheme(cb)` fires on a change. Chrome: `<meta name="codesense:icon" content="<lucide-name>">` sets the panel icon, `codesense.setBadge({count, severity})` a title-bar count. `codesense.onVisibility(cb)` says when the pane is on screen (pause polling while hidden). `codesense.onIntent(cb)` receives the opaque intent from pane_open (a JSON object of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes, interpreted only by the page); the host sends it after ready and the shim buffers the last one until a subscriber registers, then consumes it once; returns an unsubscribe. Agents: `codesense.sessions()` / `onSessions(cb)` list the live sessions, `act("stopSession", {handle})` stops one, `codesense.agents()` lists the launchable agents. Errors are loud: a load failure, an uncaught error, a failed asset or an unhandled rejection shows a banner in the pane, never a blank pane. The page must call `codesense.ready()` once its first useful state is painted (after registering its handlers); a first `codesense.subscribe(...)` also counts (`subscribeContext` does not), else after 30 s the pane falls back (docs: your-first-dashboard, lifecycle-and-liveness). Saving the file reloads the pane within a second, keeping its scroll. Installed authoring references in the codesense/docs getting-started team: content/generated/pane-declaration.schema.json (declarations and manifest schema), content/generated/pane-declarations.md (HTML meta and YAML forms), content/generated/codesense.d.ts (exact SDK signatures), and content/generated/page-sdk.md. Full verb and argument reference: get_live_data_contract.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

id.description: The pane id: its file name without `.html`, `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`.

scope.description:
`team` (default) or `personal` (your private space for `org`, which is
then required).

team.description: For scope `team`: the team, with `org`; omit both for the active team.

tools.name: pane_write

tools.description:
Post a progress note to the chat surface bound to your session and to the agent-updates store, available to dashboards through codesense.updates(). Notes do not appear in the native human Inbox. To send the human a report there, use send_message to human with kind update. Fire-and-forget: emits a UI event and returns immediately — for a blocking question, use ask_user instead. Inputs: `sessionId` (your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, stamped into your PTY at spawn), `text`. Optional: `role` (default "agent"). The render tripwire may route long or artifact-bearing messages to a doc or artifact pane; pass `subclass` (your Weft subclass: `review`/`research`/`impl`/`planning`) and `hasArtifacts: true` after a report_artifact call for better routing. For a DrillDoc target, `openDocPath` is the absolute context-repo path to open in the viewer (absent → DrillDoc rule skipped).
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

hasArtifacts.description:
Set `true` after calling `report_artifact` so the render
tripwire can annotate the bubble. The server does NOT infer this from
run-store state — the agent is the authoritative source.

openDocPath.description:
The context-repo absolute path to open in the viewer when the
render target resolves to `DrillDoc`. Absent → the DrillDoc rule is
skipped (no blind navigation to an unknown path).

sessionId.description:
The calling session's tab id — pass your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`
(codesense stamped it into your PTY env at spawn). The UI routes the
message to the chat surface bound to this session.

subclass.description:
The sending worker's Weft subclass (e.g. `"review"`,
`"research"`, `"impl"`, `"planning"`). Feeds the render tripwire — agents
that set it get better routing; omission falls through to length-based
rules.

text.description: The message text to surface in the chat.

tools.name: post_agent_message

tools.description:
Prepare a one-use terminal server restart token for a registered machine. Does not stop sessions. Confirmation will end all terminals and agents running at shutdown, including sessions started after preparation.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/terminal-servers.html
tools.name: prepare_machine_terminal_server_replacement

tools.description:
Prepare an owned remote Git repository/worktree on a configured private machine. Explicit teamKey/workspaceId, structured configured sourceRepo, UUID requestId, baseRef/branch and absolute remote repoPath/worktreePath required. Reuses verified desktop checkout committed objects and existing remote repository; returns exact pinned commit, opaque handle and cwd for open_remote_tab. A locally available ref is a local snapshot, not latest-provider assurance. Missing refs must be prepared locally by the user or their agent; only bounded credential-free Git bundles cross the admitted connection. Repeat the SAME immutable request after unknown; never delete/reset partial work. Context hydration is a separate operation.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/remote-workspaces.html
tools.name: prepare_remote_workspace

tools.description:
Preview a publish read-only: exactly what reverse_sync_worktree would write to team content, with the same inputs (target, optional paths, sets, to). On a machine it is one manifest call. Returns entries [{path, action: add|update|remove, targetLayer, targetPath, bytes}], conflicts (never written: the team changed since the copy, or a new file's team path is taken), skipped (tracked by the repo, excluded, symlinks, over 4 MiB), unchanged, and withheldRemovals (team files a publish would only remove with includeDeletes:true; pass includeDeletes:true here to preview them as removals). Writes nothing. Compatibility: kind:selected with items:[{op:update,path,ref}], and the scope-less {codeRepoPath, sessionId} form. All forms are one flat object: `kind` picks the selected form, a scope-less field the scope-less form, anything else the target form. Optional context:{kind:"team"} (default, your clone), {kind:"worktree",id} (a registered context checkout in the same org), or {kind:"launcher"} (the launching session’s captured launcherContext). A context choice never moves git refs. Worktrees are listed by list_worktrees {kind:"context"}.
Docs: arc-k-sync/index.html

codeRepoPath.description: Scope-less form: the worktree root (your `$PWD`), with `sessionId`.

includeDeletes.description:
Preview with removals included (as `reverse_sync_worktree
{includeDeletes:true}` would do them).

items.description:
Selected form (required): `[{op:"update", path, ref}]`, previewed as
those paths.

kind.description:
Compatibility: `"selected"` picks the selected form (with `target`
and `items`).

paths.description: Only these workspace files or folders.

sessionId.description: Scope-less form: your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, with `codeRepoPath`.

sets.description: Also look for new files under these folders.

target.description:
The workspace: `{kind:"local", codeRepoPath, sessionId}` or
`{kind:"remote", machineId, workspaceHandle}`. Required, except in the
scope-less form, which takes none.

to.description: Where a NEW file would go, as reverse_sync_worktree takes it.

tools.name: preview_reverse_sync_worktree

tools.description:
Publish a dashboard to share.codesense.ai: sets its dashboard.yml publish.state to published (and visibility), validates the manifest and the publishable files first (allowlist, limits, no bridge calls in pages), then pushes it. A notes array advises when a listed cs-live.js has an older version comment than this app's toolkit; this does not block publishing. Pass dashboard as the absolute folder path. visibility is private or team; team is reserved and currently the same as private (only invited viewers get in). hostedCopy is live, or retrying / auth_failed / not_sent with hostedCopyError. A retrying publish is pushed again by calling publish_dashboard again. A dashboard.yml `live` block (queries: [names], [] for presence only, or all; optional fields) needs a person to confirm it once in the native CodeSense app before it takes effect. The result's live is on (a person published it), unchanged, none (no block: live data off), pending_confirmation (a new or wider block, or a legacy one, is waiting: the page is published without live data and a dialog asks the person) or declined (the person said no; it is not asked again until dashboard.yml changes). A narrower or removed block applies at once. An agent cannot switch a private dashboard that streams terminals to team: visibility stays private until a person confirms. On a dashboard that is already published, pushes the current folder and updates the requested visibility; an edited narrower live block also takes effect within seconds without calling this again, while CodeSense is open. A child agent cannot publish a parent's dashboard, even when shared. Copy shared files into its own team and publish the copy, or ask a human to publish the parent's dashboard.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

dashboard.description: Absolute path of the dashboard folder on this Mac (the folder holding dashboard.yml).

visibility.description: `private` or `team`. `team` is reserved and is currently the same as `private`.

tools.name: publish_dashboard

tools.description:
Find context files by metadata across synced orgs (team context repos, your private space per org, and all-orgs content). Footprint-wide by default; narrow with `where`. Child callers see only shared ancestor files, even with where.teams. Every arg is optional; `{}` lists the first page of visible files sorted by path.

Rows: { id (story_id or file name), path, relPath, fileName, org (null = all-orgs), team (null = private/all-orgs), layer (team|private|all-orgs), kind (story|bug|spike|epic|doc|dashboard|skill|other), mtime (ms), title, fields (ALL frontmatter / HTML cs:* meta), relationships?, metadataTruncated?, textMatches?: [{title, anchor}] }.

Private items (the user's private space) come back only for ONE org you name: `where.orgs: ["acme"]` (exactly one) or `where.sameOrgAs`. With `orgs: "all"` (the default) or several orgs you get team and all-orgs content only, never private items — and links to private items stay hidden.

Top-level `reviews/` files are excluded by default. To read them deliberately, set `where.pathPrefix` or `where.pathGlob` starting with `reviews/` (for example `reviews/sam/` or `reviews/**/*.md`). Pane queries are unchanged.

- where: { orgs: "all" | ["org"], sameOrgAs: "/abs/path", teams: [..], layers: [..], kinds: [..], pathPrefix: "_bmad-output/13-x" or "/abs", pathGlob: "**/DEMO-*.md" }
- filters: [{ key, op, value | min/max }] — op: eq, in, not, exists, missing, contains (list item or case-insensitive text), range (numeric, or text e.g. ISO dates), prefix. Any frontmatter key or built-in (path, relPath, fileName, id, org, team, layer, kind, mtime, title, dir). Same key → OR; different keys → AND. Value "@me" = the signed-in user.
- match: { status: ["todo","review"], team: "default" } — shorthand (scalar = eq, array = in).
- relationships: { dependsOn, dependedOnBy, hasSupportingDoc, backlinkedBy, parentEpic, hasDeps, isBacklinked } — tokens are a path, story_id, file name or stem.
- text: token-aware full-text across title, headings and body (case-insensitive; reads at most 5,000 files / 64 MB per query after the other filters; textScanTruncated / totalApproximate say when that bound hit).
Text results rank by title coverage, then heading coverage, then body coverage unless sort is explicit. Schema-1 search-index.json sidecars supply optional textMatches anchors on the page row. Only nonempty text queries scoped exactly to where.orgs: ["codesense/docs"] default-exclude generated/ before scanning, reported as excluded: ["generated/"]. Opt in with where.pathPrefix: "generated/" or a pathGlob starting with "generated/". Listings and other orgs are unchanged.

- select: frontmatter keys to return (+ "relationships"); omit for everything. All query field keys accept an optional cs: prefix; topic/task/tools/audience are lists, returned with canonical unprefixed keys.
- sort: ["priority", "-mtime", {key, dir, missing, order}] — status sorts by the built-in workflow order (planning, todo, in-progress, blocked, review, qa, done) unless you pass `order` (e.g. the team's own status list); priority by p0…p4. Values order numbers < dates < text (text naturally: DEMO-9 < DEMO-10). Ties by path.
- eq/in/not compare text exactly ("01" ≠ "1"); pass a JSON number to compare numerically.
- limit (default 200, max 10000), cursor (prior nextCursor, same query; one snapshot per walk, 30 s idle/120 s max, text until a change; then data.code stale_cursor: restart), groupBy: a key → groups [{value, count}] over ALL matches (board columns).

Example — open stories in epic DEMO assigned to me, by priority, as a board:
{"where":{"kinds":["story"]},"relationships":{"parentEpic":"DEMO"},"filters":[{"key":"status","op":"in","value":["todo","in-progress"]},{"key":"assigned_to","op":"eq","value":"@me"}],"sort":["priority"],"groupBy":"status","select":["status","priority"]}

Example — dashboards in one org changed since a date: {"where":{"orgs":["acme"],"kinds":["dashboard"]},"filters":[{"key":"mtime","op":"range","min":1759300000000}],"sort":["-mtime"]}
Docs: arc-k-sync/file-tools.html

filters.description: Filter clauses `[{ key, op, value | min | max }]`; ops: eq, in, not, exists, missing, contains, range, prefix.

groupBy.description: Count matches per value of this key (board columns).

match.description: Shorthand filters `{ key: value | [values] }` (scalar = eq, array = in).

relationships.description: Relationship predicates `{ dependsOn, dependedOnBy, hasSupportingDoc, backlinkedBy, parentEpic, hasDeps, isBacklinked }`.

select.description: Frontmatter keys to return (add "relationships" for refs). Omit for every key.

sort.description: Sort keys: `"status"`, `"-mtime"`, or `{ key, dir: "asc"|"desc", missing: "first"|"last" }`.

text.description: Token-aware title, heading and body match (bounded scan).

where.description: Where to look: `{ orgs: "all" | [slugs], sameOrgAs, teams, layers, kinds, pathPrefix, pathGlob }`.

tools.name: query_context

tools.description:
React to a message in your inbox with one emoji, like a tapback: the sender and the human see it on the message, and it is not mail (no unread, no wake, no reply). Args: {message_id} (a message you sent, received, or are the reply target of; from read_messages or reply), {emoji} (any single emoji, one character cluster such as 👍, ❤️, 🎉, 🧑🏽‍💻 or a flag; at most 64 bytes; text or two emoji are refused), {remove} (optional boolean: omit it to toggle, true to take your reaction back, false to make sure it is there), {session_id} (optional: omit it to use this connection's verified tab identity). One reaction per (you, message, emoji): reacting again with the same emoji toggles it off, so to keep it pass {remove:false}. The message's sender hears of a new reaction once, in a `reactions` list next to `messages` the next time it calls read_messages. A message you are not a party to (for example mail between two other agents) answers `no message`. Returns `{status:"reacted",messageId,emoji,outcome:"added"|"removed"|"unchanged"}` or `{status:"invalid",message}`. Example: react {message_id: 42, emoji: "👍"}.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

emoji.description: Exactly one emoji (one character cluster, at most 64 bytes).

message_id.description: The message to react to, from `read_messages` or `reply`.

remove.description: Omit to toggle; `true` takes your reaction back; `false` makes sure it is there.

session_id.description:
Omit to react as this connection's verified tab. If supplied, it must name that
same tab. An unbound connection is refused.

tools.name: react

tools.description:
Drain your unread inbox messages (oldest first; each returned once then marked read). Inbox mail comes from people and agents that your user's setup lets reach you, so anyone who can message you is someone your user trusts. Call this when your hook tells you "You have N new messages. Call read_messages with session_id <id>." — pass that id as {session_id} (your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID), or omit it to read the inbox of the tab this MCP connection runs in. A hand-started CLI in a CodeSense terminal is bound to that tab. An outside or unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal. A supplied session_id must name this same tab. Returns `{messages: [{messageId, from, fromName, text, inReplyTo, inReplyToTeam, replyTo?, summary?, primaryFile?, attachmentHint?}]}`; `summary` is the sender's one-line plain-text preview of `text`, when it set one; `replyTo` (when the sender set one) is where your reply goes instead of to the sender; `primaryFile` is a logical path the sender attached, and when `attachmentHint` is present an agent whose workspace lacks the file can call `hydrate_story` with `attachmentHint.owningStoryId` to copy it in. Answer any one with reply, or acknowledge it with react. When someone reacted to a message you sent, the result also has `reactions: [{messageId, emoji, reactor, createdAtMs, team: {org, team}}]` (`team` names the team that holds the message, which matters when you mailed an agent in another team), each new reaction reported once (a reaction taken back before you read it is never reported); reactions are not mail and are never counted as unread.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

session_id.description:
Your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; omit it to read the inbox of the tab this MCP
connection runs in. An unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal.
