tools.description:
Read agent run — one run in full, as the run-detail pane shows it. Read-only. Required: `runId` (a list_runs row's `outcome.run_id`). Optional: `maxArtifactBytes` (how much of its captured output to return, from the end; default 65536, max 1048576). Returns `{outcome, transcript, artifact, artifactTruncated}`: `outcome` is its list_runs row, `link` included (null while it is still running or when it recorded none); `transcript` its structured conversation (stored once per session, read from the latest session the run names that has one; an older run reads its own record), `{turns:[{role (assistant | user | result), text?, tool_calls?:[{name, input?, result?, is_error?, native_id?, mcp_server?, skill?}], usage?, index?, ts_ms?, model?, reasoning?:{kind (full | summary | encrypted | none), text?}}], unavailable?:{field: reason}}`: a field the CLI never records is left out and named in `unavailable` (Codex records no `is_error`, so it is absent), or null when its agent CLI gives none; `artifact` the tail of its captured terminal output (secrets redacted), or null when it left none; `artifactTruncated` true when the output was longer than returned. A dashboard's codesense.run({runId}) returns the same.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

maxArtifactBytes.description:
Return at most the last this-many bytes of its captured output (default
65536, max 1048576).

tools.name: read_run

tools.description:
Read agent run evidence — one run's audit record, as the run-evidence view shows it: what fired it, how it ended, its step-by-step spine and what each step reported. Read-only. Required: `runId` (a list_runs row's `outcome.run_id`). Optional: `storyId` (the story it worked, `outcome.story_id`; omit it to use the story the run's latest outcome names — pass it only to read a run that worked several stories, like a sprint tick, for one of the others). Returns null when there is no evidence: the run is still going or recorded no outcome, or it worked no story. Otherwise `{header, run, perNodeResults, authority}`. `header`: `{runId, storyId, automationId?, trigger, scheduledAt?, firedAt?, startedAt?, endedAt?, status?, summary?, workflowRevisionId?}` — `trigger` is `{kind:"attributed", source}` (what fired it: `manual`, `schedule`, an event name) or `{kind:"preEnvelope"}` (no trigger was recorded; nothing is guessed); `status`: `success` | `failed` | `needs-attention` (absent while it runs); `summary` its signal_done summary (secrets redacted); `workflowRevisionId` the pinned automation revision it ran, when known; times are RFC3339. `run`: `{runId, parentRunId?, originNodeId?, correlationId, steps:[{stepExecutionId, nodeId, attempts:[{attemptId, attemptOrdinal, runId, result}]}]}` — one step per workflow node it ran (`nodeId` is the node's id), each retry a new attempt (`attemptOrdinal` 1, 2, ...); `result`: `passed` | `failed` | `pending`; an attempt's `runId` is what read_run takes for that attempt's transcript and output; `parentRunId`/`originNodeId` name the run and node that started this one, when it was started by another run; `correlationId` groups runs of one chain (the run's own id when it is alone). `perNodeResults`: `[{nodeId, summary?, outputs?:[{key, value}], artifacts?:[{kind, reference, label?}], footprint?:[{kind, reference, change}]}]` — what each node reported (report_step_result / report_artifact), plus the branch it produced as an `entity` artifact `owner/repo@branch` on node `agent`; `value` is any JSON; `kind`: `file` (a repo-relative path) | `pr` (a PR/MR URL) | `entity` (another id); `change`: `created` | `modified`; absent lists are empty. `authority`: `durable` (from the durable run store) | `currentStoreFallback` (from the run log; same shape). Next: read_run {runId} for the transcript and output, read_run_work_product {runId} for the branch. A dashboard's codesense.runEvidence({runId, storyId?}) returns the same.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

storyId.description:
The story the run worked (`outcome.story_id`). Omit it to use the story the
run's latest outcome names.

tools.name: read_run_evidence

tools.description:
Read agent run work product — the git branch an agent run produced, as captured when it ended. Read-only. Required: `runId` (a list_runs row's `outcome.run_id`). Returns `{branch}` (the branch name), or null when the run produced none, is still going, or is unknown. The repository is the list_runs row's `outcome.work_product.source_repo` (`{owner, repo}`); list_worktrees shows a worktree on that branch. Next: read_run_evidence {runId} for the full audit record. A dashboard's codesense.runWorkProduct({runId}) returns the same.
Docs: arc-h-pipelines-and-sdlc/runs-and-stories.html

tools.description:
Read a terminal tab's CURRENT scrollback — the open→run→read round-trip for tabs opened with open_terminal_tab / open_remote_tab. One-shot snapshot (not a live subscription). Args: {handle} (opaque; raw/forged sessionIds refused). Instead of {handle}, name the tab by {tab} (list_sessions name) + optional {machine}/{workspace}; ambiguous names return the candidate set. Local: `{output, altScreen}` — plain text from the emulator (cursor-addressed TUIs like Codex/Claude Code read as rendered, not as overlapping redraws); while a full-screen program holds altScreen, output is that screen's rows, else lines including scrollback (bounded by the emulator's scrollback limit). Remote: `{status:"ok", output, head, reset, altScreen}`; accepts optional {since} but every read returns the full text (reset always true — no byte delta). Optional {view} `scrollback` (default) | `screen` (just the current frame of a redraw-in-place program like top). Gated by the Interactive tier.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

handle.description:
The opaque terminal-tab handle returned by `open_terminal_tab`,
`open_remote_tab` or `list_sessions`. A raw sessionId, or a handle with no
live session, is refused. Give this or `tab`.

machine.description: With `tab`: the machine it runs on, by label ("This Mac" for this one).

since.description: Remote handles only: a canonical decimal-u64 `head` from an earlier read. Every read returns the whole text; a cursor beyond head is refused.

tab.description: The tab's name as its tab bar shows it now (e.g. "Terminal 2"), instead of a handle.

view.description:
`scrollback` (default): the tab's lines including scrollback. `screen`:
only the rows on screen now — the current frame of a program like `top`.

workspace.description: With `tab`: the workspace id it is in.

tools.name: read_terminal_tab

tools.description:
Refresh the frontmatter cache for a context-layer file after a NON-CodeSense writer (e.g. an agent's own filesystem `Write`) dropped bytes on disk. The CodeSense cache otherwise refreshes on `move_content_file` / `delete_content_file` / its own file APIs and on an fs-watcher event; a raw write bypasses all three, so `open_workspace` can't find a story that is physically present. Not needed when writing through CodeSense's own file APIs — those refresh automatically. Input: `path` (absolute context-layer path). Returns `{path, team, refreshed, storyId, previousStoryId?}` — `refreshed:true` means the cache's view of the file changed (added, swapped, or removed); `storyId` is what the cache now reads from the file (null when the file is not a pipeline story).
Docs: arc-k-sync/file-tools.html

path.description:
Absolute context-layer path (`{home}/users/.../orgs/.../{team}/content/...`)
of the file whose frontmatter the cache should re-read from disk.

tools.name: refresh_frontmatter_cache

tools.description:
Fetch a configured repo's attached checkout from its origin now, so why_line and story_changes can read history this copy lacks. Required repo (configured slug or host/owner/repo). Optional storyId: for a landed story (status done or merged), deepen a shallow copy only until its 2000-commit merge scan is inside the boundary, then unshallow if needed; a story in progress gets a plain fetch. Optional timeoutMs bounds the whole call (default 60000, 1000 to 300000). Updates only refs/remotes/origin/*, objects and the shallow file (sets a missing origin/HEAD from origin); never the working tree, index, HEAD, local branches, tags or notes. Never prompts: no terminal or askpass prompt, ssh in batch mode (a GIT_SSH program is left as set); the user's credential helper still answers. Clears the trail's remembered misses for that checkout. Returns {repo, historyAsOf {fetchedAt (epoch ms), originHead}, shallow, deepened (depth, unshallow or null), status?: partial, reason?} (partial: the first fetch landed, a deepen did not; reason also when the story's history is still past the boundary), or {status:unavailable, reason, historyAsOf, shallow} with reason fetch needs credentials, fetch skipped, repo busy (another git holds a lock; no retry), fetch timed out, fetch failed or no local copy. Ordinary reads never fetch; call this when you choose. Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html#tool-refresh_history.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

repo.description: Configured source slug; host/owner/repo disambiguates names shared by hosts.

storyId.description:
For a story that has landed (status done or merged), deepen a shallow copy until its
merge scan is inside the boundary. Another story gets a plain fetch.

timeoutMs.description: Bound on the whole refresh in milliseconds (default 60000, 1000 to 300000).

tools.name: refresh_history

tools.description:
Join a role's queue: register as a live holder of {role} in {team} so you can claim the messages sent to that role (send_role_message). Args: {team} `{org, team}`; {role} any role name (usually an agent id from agent_list; no name is special); {sessionId} optional: defaults to this connection's verified tab (a supplied id must name that same tab). CodeSense keeps the registration alive while that session runs and releases it when it ends; {instanceId} is bound to that tab. Unbound callers are refused; {exclusive} optional boolean, default false — true makes the role one-holder-only. Returns {instanceId, sessionId?, exclusive, generation, expiresAt, pendingCount, acceptedUnacked}: pass instanceId and generation to claim_role_messages, accept_role_message, ack_role_message and release_role; generation stays the same while your registration stays live (registering again is harmless and returns the same generation); expiresAt is epoch seconds (CodeSense moves it forward every 15s while your session runs); pendingCount is how many messages wait in the role's queue; acceptedUnacked lists work an earlier holder accepted but never acknowledged — adopt it (claim_role_messages hands it back with existingReceipt). Each acceptedUnacked entry has shape {deliveryId, role, receiptId, messageId, kind, queueItemId}; queueItemId is deprecated and always null for new receipts — role work is not mirrored into wv_queue. Refusals: {status: alreadyHeld, instance} when the role is held exclusive by another live instance; {status: modeConflict, heldExclusive} when the role's live holders registered in the other mode (exclusive vs shared). A registration lapses after 60s (180s from a remote machine) once its session stops running or its machine stays unreachable; your next claim then fails with a stale registration — call register_role again. Next: claim_role_messages.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

exclusive.description: `true`: one live holder at a time. Default `false` (shared).

instanceId.description:
Bound to this connection's verified tab session by MCP. Returned by
register_role and used with generation for subsequent role calls.

role.description: The role name (usually an agent id from `agent_list`).

sessionId.description:
Your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`. With it, CodeSense keeps the registration
alive while your session runs and releases it when the session ends.

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: register_role

tools.description:
Release this instance's registration for {role}: any still-claimed-but-unaccepted deliveries return to pending (so another instance of the same role can claim them). Accepted or acknowledged deliveries are not touched. In a shared role, other registered instances stay intact. Returns {released: N} = how many pending-reset. Call it to step down while your session keeps running; when a session that registered with sessionId ends, CodeSense releases its roles for it, and a caller with no session is covered by expiry.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

tools.name: release_role

tools.description:
Bring the committed work of a workspace that lives on a machine home into this Mac's local clone of its repository. Name it by machineId + workspaceHandle (the handle on the workspace record), or by storyId / workspaceId of an open workspace (add teamKey if more than one team matches). The commits the machine's checkout is on arrive as refs/remotes/codesense-machine-<machineId>/<branch>; the local branch of the same name is created, or fast-forwarded only when that is safe. Never merges, rebases or force-updates a local branch: a diverged branch, a dirty checkout of it, or a checkout of it in another worktree is reported (reason) and left as it was. Uncommitted work on the machine stays there. Returns branch, commit, remoteRef, the commits that arrived (sha, subject), localBranchState and fastForwarded. Pushing and pull requests stay with your own git or forge tools, run from the local clone.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/remote-workspaces.html

machineId.description:
The machine the workspace lives on. Optional when `storyId` or
`workspaceId` names an open workspace that lives on a machine.

storyId.description: An open story workspace's story id, resolved to its machine and handle.

teamKey.description:
The team whose open workspaces `storyId`/`workspaceId` are looked up
in, when more than one team has a match.

workspaceHandle.description:

workspaceId.description: An open workspace's id, resolved to its machine and handle.

tools.description:
Remove content from a context — delete a content item (by its stable `logicalName`) from a single Context. Removing a private item returns `{ status: "gate", reason: "sole_copy" }` first — the private space is the user's own folder and may hold the only copy — so nothing only you had is silently lost; re-call with `allowSoleCopyMove: true` to delete permanently. Removing an already-absent item is `{ status: "ok", outcome: "rejectedSourceMissing" }` (already gone — your goal), never an error. Returns `{ status: "ok", outcome }`.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

allowSoleCopyMove.description: The sole-copy override: acknowledge deleting a private item permanently.

tools.description:
Optional {requestId} deduplicates retries: send the same key and payload after a disconnect to return the original messageId; a changed payload is refused. Omit it to create a new message. Reply to an inbox message — delivered like send_message to whoever sent the original (agent or human), or, when the original carries a `replyTo`, ONLY to that address instead (email Reply-To): a session's inbox, the human, or for `role:<id>` a pending delivery in that role's queue that any instance of the role claims later, even after the original sender exited. Args: {message_id} (from read_messages), {text}, {session_id} (optional: omit it to answer as this connection's verified tab; if supplied it must name that same tab; an unbound connection is refused (start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal), never answered as the human; the reply shows as the sender's current tab name, see who_am_i). Optional {media:{url|path,alt}} attaches a GIF or image; alt is required. Reply body renders as markdown by default. {summary} is one plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this reply's preview in lists; set it when the body is long or heavily formatted. {kind} "needs-you" | "update": what a reply to the human asks of them, as in send_message; omitted, a reply is an "update" (the human is waiting on your answer, not you on theirs) — pass "needs-you" when your reply asks them something back. A reply queued for a role keeps no kind. Returns `{status:"sent",messageId,kind?,hint?}` (`kind` and `hint` as for send_message, for a reply to the human) or `{status:"invalid",message}` (blank text without media / unknown message id / a sessionId that is not running).
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

A refusal has spawnEligible false and a reason, with requestedAccountId echoing the override that failed: detached (reattach it), auth-required (sign in again), provider-mismatch (account is for another CLI), account-missing (it no longer exists), generation-mismatch (it changed after you read it; list and retry with the current generation), required-missing (no account is set up for this CLI).

Required: `confirmEndSessions: true`, and `expected` exactly as terminal_server_status returned it; `expected` may be omitted only while the state is `incompatible`. Returns `{restarted: true, ended, ends, otherInstances}`, as reviewed (`ended`: the sessions it ended; `null` when the old server did not say).

tools.description:
Publish workspace edits back to team content — the only way a workspace's changes reach the team. Pass target:{kind:"local",codeRepoPath,sessionId} or {kind:"remote",machineId,workspaceHandle}. Candidates are the files CodeSense copied into the workspace (each maps its original tier and path into the chosen context; the destination is checked against the copied baseline) plus new files under the workspace's declared context (they go to the active team, or to the tier `to` names: team, repo, personal). Optional paths:[files or folders] limits it; sets:[folders] also looks for new files there. A team file that changed since it was copied, or a new file whose team path already holds other bytes, is a conflict: it is never written, and comes back in conflicts. Team content is never deleted unless you pass includeDeletes:true: then a managed file removed in the workspace is removed from the team, only while the team still holds what was copied (without it such files come back in withheldRemovals). Files over 4 MiB are skipped. Batched: on a machine one manifest call and one streamed read of the changed files (plus one exclude-block batch when new files are added), then one all-or-nothing team write (each file compare-and-swapped; a race rolls back what this publish wrote). Call preview_reverse_sync_worktree first to see exactly what it will do. Optional operationId (UUID) makes a retry return the kept result. Returns status (published/publishedWithConflicts/nothingToPublish/failed/cancelled), entries [{path, action, targetLayer, targetPath}], conflicts, skipped, failed, withheldRemovals. Compatibility: kind:selected with requestId and items:[{op:update,path,ref,expectedSource,expectedWorkspace}] publishes those paths with those expected hashes; the scope-less {codeRepoPath, sessionId} form publishes every candidate. All forms are one flat object: `kind` picks the selected form, a scope-less field the scope-less form, anything else the target form. Optional context:{kind:"team"} (default, your clone), {kind:"worktree",id} (a registered context checkout in the same org), or {kind:"launcher"} (the launching session’s captured launcherContext). A context choice never moves git refs. Worktrees are listed by list_worktrees {kind:"context"}.
Docs: arc-k-sync/index.html

codeRepoPath.description: Scope-less form: the worktree root (your `$PWD`), with `sessionId`.

includeDeletes.description:
Also remove team files whose copy was deleted in the workspace (only
while the team still holds what was copied). Off by default: a
publish never deletes team content unless asked.

items.description:
Selected form (required): `[{op:"update", path, ref, expectedSource,
expectedWorkspace}]`, published with those expected hashes.

kind.description:
Compatibility: `"selected"` picks the selected form (with `requestId`,
`target` and `items`).

operationId.description:
A UUID naming this operation; calling again with it returns the kept
result instead of running again.

paths.description:
Only these workspace files or folders (absent: every managed file
and every new file under the workspace's declared context).

requestId.description: Selected form (required): the request's UUID (its operationId).

sessionId.description: Scope-less form: your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, with `codeRepoPath`.

sets.description: Also publish new files under these folders.

target.description:
The workspace: `{kind:"local", codeRepoPath, sessionId}` or
`{kind:"remote", machineId, workspaceHandle}`. Required, except in the
scope-less form, which takes none.

to.description:
Where a NEW file goes: `team` (default), `repo` (this repo's tier),
`personal`, or a tier label from a preview (`team:org/team`).
Edited files always go back to the team file they came from.

tools.description:
Save team role settings. teamKey is org:team; config has id (stable queue id), name, icon (pack:id or null to reset), defaultHandler (one saved-agent key or null). Changing settings never changes queued mail, existing holders, or the saved agent's default role. A default handler does not launch automatically.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html
tools.name: role_save

tools.description:
Show the role mailboxes of a team: who holds each role and where every message sent to it stands. A role is a queue shared by every session registered for it (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id from agent_list). Changes and claims nothing. Args, all optional: {role} (just that one), {limit} (acknowledged deliveries per role, newest first; default 20 — open ones are always all listed), {team} `{org, team}` (default: the team active in the app). Returns {roles: [{role, roleName, registrations, counts, deliveries, deliveriesTruncated}]}. `roleName` is the saved Agent's name (null when unknown here). `registrations`: [{instanceId, instanceName, generation, registeredAtMs, lastRenewedAtMs, expiresAtMs, live}] — the instances that registered with register_role; `live` is false once `expiresAtMs` passed (they must register again); `instanceName` is the session's display name when the instance id is a known session. `counts`: {pending, claimed, accepted, acknowledged} over all deliveries. `deliveries`: open ones oldest first, then the newest acknowledged: [{deliveryId, messageId, state, from, fromName, excerpt, createdAtMs, firstClaimedAtMs, claimOwner, claimOwnerName, claimOwnerGeneration, claimExpiresAtMs, claimLapsed, receipt}]. `state`: `pending` (waiting; no instance holds it), `claimed` (an instance took it with claim_role_messages and is deciding; `claimLapsed` true means the claim expired and it can be claimed again), `accepted` (accepted with accept_role_message, as work or no work, not yet acknowledged), `acknowledged` (finished with ack_role_message). `receipt` (once accepted): {receiptId, instanceId, generation, kind (work|no_work), note, queueItemId (deprecated — always null for new receipts; role work is not mirrored into wv_queue), acceptedAtMs}. `excerpt` is the start of the message text; inbox_list {role} shows the whole thread. All times are epoch milliseconds. Next: to work a role's queue yourself, register_role then claim_role_messages; to message it, send_role_message.
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/messages.html

limit.description:
Acknowledged deliveries per role, newest first (default 20). Open deliveries
are always all listed.

role.description: Just this role (any role name, usually a saved Agent's id).

anyOf.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

team.description: The team `{org, team}`; default: the team active in the app.

tools.description:
Routine arm on — move where a routine fires: `machine:"this_mac"` (this Mac fires it, as "Run on this Mac" does) or a machine id from list_machines (that machine's terminal server fires it on its own clock, in the routine's zone, whether or not any Mac is open; this Mac manages it: it prepares the agent there now and on every edit, pushes the routine's definition whenever it reconnects, and records its runs; later changes to the agent's own files reach the machine only through routine_refresh_on_machine). A routine armed on a machine runs on its schedule only (no agent_done, inbox_idle or role_pending triggers), once for the team, with its agent on that machine. Each move is a new revision under a new arm epoch: the machine refuses anything older, so a stale definition never re-arms it. Moving it off a machine waits for that machine to acknowledge before anything else fires it (`handover_pending`), so a move never doubles a fire. Required: `id`, `machine`. Optional: `sessionId` (omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Counts against the 25 enabled-routine cap. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, armed_machine, arm_epoch, revision, handover_pending, machine_warning? } } (`machine_warning`: armed, but not prepared on the machine yet, and why: not connected, preparation failed or still running, or waiting on the machine it moved off), or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

machine.description:
`this_mac`: this Mac fires it. A machine id (from list_machines): that
machine's terminal server fires it on its own clock, with or without
this Mac.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_arm_on

tools.description:
Routine cancel — cancel one queued or running run through the native stop path. Required: `runId` (a `run_id` from routine_runs or routine_run). Optional: `sessionId`; identity comes from the verified connection, and a supplied id must name that caller. An unbound connection or a foreign caller id is refused. Any shared team run you can see can be cancelled, regardless of its creator; personal runs stay private. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ routine_id, routine_name, run_id, phase, created_at, started_at, ended_at, ... } }, the same row as routine_run, with RFC3339 times. A fresh run's agent or command is stopped; a wake run keeps the session it woke alive. A queued wake is withdrawn at its host first: if already delivered, returns validation with its actual phase instead of claiming cancellation. Unknown or invisible runs and already finished runs return validation with a clear message; finished runs are unchanged. An unreachable wake host or remote launch still starting returns an error and leaves the run queued. Does not pause future fires or cancel other runs; held work may start next. routine_set_enabled pauses future starts. The pane routineCancel({key}) is a different, batch operation on this principal's live structured-result attempts.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

runId.description: A run_id from routine_runs or routine_run.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_cancel

tools.description:
Routine context — when a routine launched you: what you are running and why. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; it answers for the routine run that session is running). Optional runId selects the run named in a wake header. trigger_payload carries its document change; coalesced_payloads retains every merged change. Wake text stays static: call routine_context to read changes. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ run_id, routine_id, routine_name, revision, routine (the definition pinned to this run), source, scheduled_at, fired_at, variables (the values your task was rendered with), trigger_payload, last_run_summary, last_run_id, agent (the agent this run launched, `<key>@<revision>`), content_dir (the absolute path of the routine's content folder: for an Only me routine the `content/` folder of your private space for its org, since its working folder starts empty) } }, or { status:"validation", data:{ message:"not a routine run" } } when that session is not running a routine. Calling signal_done is up to your task: its summary becomes this run's result and the next run's `{{last_run_summary}}`; without it the run simply ends when you exit. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; a supplied sessionId must name that caller, and an unbound caller is refused.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

runId.description: The id in the wake header when the session holds several runs.

sessionId.description: Your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`.

tools.name: routine_context

tools.description:
Create a routine. For something only for your current session, use schedule_wakeup. Each fire runs `task` on `agent` per `mode`, with history. `task` is the agent's whole prompt: CodeSense adds nothing to it. It may use `{{date}}`, `{{timestamp}}`, `{{last_run_at}}` (empty on the first run), `{{last_run_summary}}` (the last successful `signal_done` summary) and declared `{{variables}}`. `task` is the whole contract: a run ends when the agent process exits, when it calls `signal_done`, or at `maxRuntime`. For a result or question, instruct `signal_done` with `summary` or status `needs-attention` and the question; otherwise the run simply ends. A `visible` agent stays open after work; without that call its run lasts until the user closes the tab or `maxRuntime`. Meanwhile fires follow `overlap`. For a structured result, declare `resultSchema` and have the task call routine_publish_result, then signal_done success. Headless Claude may call `routine_context` / `routine_publish_result` only when `permissions.claude.allow` lists them (as `mcp__codesense__<tool>`; `signal_done` always works). Routines never deliver results: to send, post or file something, the task must name the tool, and the agent needs that server in `mcpServers`. Example: `{"name":"Triage","when":"weekdays 09:00","agent":"triage","task":"Read mail, then signal_done with a summary."}`. Unsure? Pass `dryRun:true` first. Wake limits: maxWakes, maxWakesPerDay, minGap (mode wake only). Creation is a local context-repo edit that notifies no one, shown under its agent in Agents | Schedule; sharing needs a git push. An each_mac recipe is off until enabled on each Mac. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, agent, agent_key, mode, effective_mode, schedule_in_words, next_fires:[next 3, RFC3339; empty for a draft], enabled, revision, warnings:[{code, message}], deprecations? } }: `warnings` never block the save (e.g. a `/name` task missing from the agent's `startup`; fix with agent_update). Or validation, unauthorizedTeam, notSyncedLocally. Events use the YAML model: events:[{kind:"inbox_idle"}] fires on idle sessions with unread mail; events:[{kind:"agent_done",from_agent:"reviewer"}] watches that agent finishing (omit from_agent for all in reach). Use events:[{kind:"role_pending"}] to watch every queue in reach. Use events:[{kind:"role_pending",role:"reviewer"}] to watch only reviewer mail. role must be nonblank and is valid only for role_pending; from_agent only for agent_done. No role or from_agent existence check. Omitted/null events keeps current events; [] clears these three kinds; nonempty replaces only them, preserving schedules and metadata triggers. Event errors return status:validation with events[i].field and a hint. These events support each_mac; machine arming restrictions still apply. metadataTriggers takes query_context selection, target eq and optional previous eq for a transition. Existing matches baseline at discovery/restart. [] clears metadata triggers; omitted/null keeps them. Metadata triggers require one_mac. Recipients use routine_context and the wake header runId. action:command runs command:[program,arg,...] directly without an agent/model; rendered argv is returned. Commands are team/local only, default overlap queue/maxRuntime 5m. Bare executables use PATH; relative executable paths must stay inside the team content root; absolute executable paths are refused. Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes bounded, secret-redacted output (last 4 KB). after:{routine:id,on:succeeded|finished} chains in the same space; finished excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced, cycles and missing upstream are refused. after:null clears on update. budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?} is fresh-agent only; raising/removing a cap needs native Accept. dryRun:true validates resolved triggers and rendered argv without writing a definition. Verified caller required; sessionId must match.
Docs: arc-g-routines/trigger-cookbook.html

action.description:
agent (default) or command. action:command takes command:[program,arg,...]
instead of agent/task/mode; it runs as you, with no agent or model, in a
team workspace or managed repo clone. Defaults: overlap queue, maxRuntime 5m.
Only me and machine-armed command routines are refused.

after.description:
Fire after a routine in the same space succeeds or finishes. `finished`
excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced. Cycles and missing upstream routines
are refused. Chained fires carry trigger.{run_id,routine,phase,result_text,detail}.

agent.description:
The agent the routine belongs to and runs: its `id` from agent_list in the
routine's own space (a bare `triage` is the team's agent for a team
routine and your private agent for an Only me one), or its full key, which
lets an Only me routine run a team agent. A team routine needs an agent of
its own team or a starter (`builtin/claude`, `builtin/codex`), since any
teammate's Mac may run it. Required, unless `sessionId` names a session
launched as a saved agent (then that one; a session launched as a starter
still defaults to that starter, with a `deprecations` note). The routine
lives under it, in `config/agents/<agent>/routines/<id>/`; each run
launches it with the running user's own account at its current revision,
archived or not.
The reply names the one chosen; routine_update changes it.

budgetUsd.description:
budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?}: positive finite USD; local calendar day and
Monday-start week, not rolling windows. Fresh only: wakes cap the agent;
commands cannot. Machine-armed caps are refused. Raising/removing a cap
needs native Accept; lowering ratchets the local accepted ceiling.
Unrestricted shells are trusted; sandbox untrusted agents.

command.description:
Program and arguments, one entry each. A bare program uses PATH; a relative
executable path must be executable inside the team content root; absolute
executable paths are refused. Args render individually, never through a shell.
Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes the secret-redacted last 4 KB of output.

enabled.description:
Whether it fires from this Mac. Default true (false for a draft that
never fires until routine_set_enabled resumes it); for `runsOn:
each_mac`, default false, and true turns it on for this Mac.
The 25 enabled-routine cap is checked when enabling.

events.description:
Events: [{"kind":"inbox_idle"}], [{"kind":"agent_done","from_agent":"reviewer"}],
or [{"kind":"role_pending","role":"reviewer"}]. Omit role for every queue in reach.

items.description: Event inputs share the YAML model's spelling and validation.

from_agent.description: agent_done only: agent id or full key; omitted watches all agents in reach.

role.description: role_pending only: nonempty queue name; omitted watches every queue in reach.

id.description: The routine id within its team. Default: derived from `name`; a taken id is validation.

machine.description:
Where a wake looks for (and starts) the agent: `local` (default, this
Mac), a machine id from list_machines, or `any` connected machine (wakes
the agent wherever it runs, starts it here when none does). With
`runsOn: each_mac` it must be `local`, except that a `fresh` routine may
use `any`. A session on an offline machine still counts as running, so
that wake is undelivered (machine_offline) and nothing starts.

maxRuntime.description: How long one run may take, like `30m` or `2h`. Default `30m`.

maxWakes.description:
Optional: how many wakes this routine may deliver in all. Reached, it
pauses itself and posts one inbox note; resuming starts a new count.
Light checks need no wake limits; heavy work may use
"minGap":"4h","maxWakesPerDay":3,"overlap":"skip".
Past 120 wakes/hour per session, wakes return rate_limited (one inbox note).
Omit for no limit. Wake limits count wakes typed into a live session, so
they apply to `mode: wake` only (a `fresh` routine with limits saves with
a `wake_limits_ignored` warning; a start when none runs is not counted).
The terminal server running the session enforces them, so they hold
with the desktop closed; each Mac and machine keeps its own count, and
a machine whose terminal server is too old is sent no limited wake
(undelivered (unavailable), with one inbox note to update it).

maxWakesPerDay.description:
Optional: wakes in any rolling 24 h. Fires over it are
`undelivered(limit_reached)` and it resumes on its own. A wake limit
(see `maxWakes`): `mode: wake` only.

metadataTriggers.description:
Metadata conditions using query_context's selection and eq clauses. Example:
[{"selection":{"where":{"kinds":["story"]}},"target":{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"in-progress"}}].
Add previous:{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"planning"} for an exact transition.
Matches at first discovery or restart are a baseline; only later entry fires.
Omit to preserve; [] removes metadata triggers on update, keeping other events.
Not with runsOn:each_mac. Recipients read changes with routine_context and
the wake header runId (incl. coalesced_payloads).

minGap.description:
Optional: the least time between two wakes of this routine (into any
session) (`30m`, `2h`, `1d`; at most `7d`), for wakes that start heavy
work. A fire inside it is coalesced or skipped per `overlap`. A wake
limit (see `maxWakes`): `mode: wake` only.

missed.description:
`skip` (default) or `run_once`: what happens to fires missed while the
app was closed or asleep.

mode.description:
`wake` (deliver the task into the agent's live session when it is
idle, starting one with `task` as its first prompt only when none runs;
never a second instance) or `fresh` ("start a new" in the app: a new
instance in `where` on each fire, headless unless `visible`). Omitted: `wake` for a visible routine on a
saved agent that launches in a tab, else `fresh`; the reply's
`effective_mode` says what a fire does. A built-in starter's routines
are fresh only.

name.description: What the routine is called, e.g. "Morning triage".

overlap.description:
`coalesce` (default), `skip` or `queue`: what a fire does while a run is
still going.

resultSchema.description:
Optional bounded inline JSON Schema for the routine's private dashboard
result; omit when no structured result is required.

runsOn.description:
A team routine only: `one_mac` (default) runs it once for the team, on
this Mac until moved (a shared job, e.g. a bug bot or team triage); `each_mac` makes
it a recipe each teammate turns on for their own Mac (e.g. a digest or a
reminder for oneself), off everywhere until they do, with its own runs
on each.

scope.description:
`team` (default: teammates can see it) or `personal` (Only me, only when
the user asks for it: your private space for `org`, which is then
required and must be an org synced on this Mac; it runs in that org
only). A team routine goes in `org`/`team`, or the active team when both
are omitted. Anyone who sees it can change it; `owner` grants nothing.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

task.description:
What the agent should do on each run, in plain words. Example:
"Summarize acme/web issues since {{last_run_at}} to #web-triage with Slack
MCP tools, then signal_done with it."

tz.description: The IANA zone `when` is read in. Default: this machine's zone.

variables.description:
Task variables, `{ name: { type, default } }`, referenced as `{{name}}`:
e.g. `{"channel": {"type": "text", "default": "#web"}}` used as
`{{channel}}`.

visible.description: Run in a visible terminal tab instead of headless. Default false.

when.description:
When it runs, read in `tz`: a preset (`every 5m|10m|15m|20m|30m`,
`every 1h|2h|3h|4h|6h|8h|12h`, `hourly`, `daily 09:00`, `weekdays 08:30`,
`weekly mon 17:00`, on a 24-hour clock) or a 5-field cron such as
`0 9 * * 1-5`. Nothing fires more often than every 5 minutes. Omit it for a
routine that runs only when started by hand. Empty when removes schedules;
other event triggers are kept.

tools.name: routine_create

tools.description:
Routine delete — archive any routine you can see: it stops firing and leaves routine_list, and its run history stays readable. Required: `id`. Optional: `sessionId` (optional: omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Any routine you can see is yours to change, a teammate's included: the change is a local edit to the context repo, and sharing it with the team is a git push your agent makes. Notifies no one. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, archived:true, revision } }, or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

id.description: The routine's `id` as `routine_list` returns it.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_delete

tools.description:
Routine done — finish ONE routine run with your verdict, without ending your session: use it when a routine woke you inside a session that keeps working (signal_done instead ends your session's whole task). Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, checked against the terminal you call from: another session's id is refused), `runId` (the run_id from routine_context, or the id in the `[routine: <name> | run <id>]` line your task came with), `outcome` (`success` | `failed` | `needs-attention`). Optional: `summary`, a short result line (a successful run's summary becomes the next run's `{{last_run_summary}}`). Any other run your session holds, and the session itself, are untouched. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ run_id, routine_id, phase } } (`phase` succeeded | failed | needs_you), or { status:"validation", data:{ message } } when that run is not your session's running run. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; a supplied sessionId must name that caller, and an unbound caller is refused.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

runId.description:
The run to finish (`run_id` from routine_context, or the id in the
`[routine: … | run <id>]` header of a wake).

sessionId.description: Your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`: the session running the run.

summary.description:
A short result line: the run's result, and the next run's
`{{last_run_summary}}` when it succeeded.

tools.name: routine_done

tools.description:
Routine get — one routine in full. Required: `id` (from routine_list). Optional `agent`: refuse (`validation`) unless it belongs to that agent. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, scope, agent_key, unassigned, mode, effective_mode, owner, owner_name, armed_here, runs_on, enabled (this Mac's switch), revision, content_stale? (as in routine_list), schedule_in_words, routine (the full definition), runs:[this Mac's last 5 runs, newest first] } }, or `validation` when there is no such routine. Also returns budgetUsd, budgetPending, and spend {today, week, state: ok|warn|reached|unpriced}. A cap on a fresh routine counts handles routine:<key>@<run>. Agent caps also apply.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

agent.description:
Only when it belongs to this agent (its `id` or key from agent_list):
a routine of another agent is `validation`.

id.description: The routine's `id` as `routine_list` returns it.

tools.name: routine_get

tools.description:
Routine handover release — stop waiting for a machine that is GONE to confirm it stopped firing a routine moved off it. Until a machine confirms, nothing else fires the routine (so a move never doubles a fire); a machine that is shut down for good can never confirm. Required: `id`, `machine` (the machine it waits on, as routine_get shows), `machineGone: true` (you confirm the machine is gone: one that still runs may fire the routine once more). A routine moved to another machine is prepared there now. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, machine, machine_warning? } } (`machine_warning`: not prepared on the machine it moved to, and why). Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

machine.description: The machine the routine is waiting on.

machineGone.description:
Must be true: you confirm the machine is gone (shut down, deleted).
A machine that still runs may fire the routine once more.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_handover_release

tools.description:
Routine list — every routine you can see: your Only me ones (in your private space for the open org) and those of every team synced on this Mac, yours and teammates', all of which you can change. Optional `agent` (an agent's `id` or key from agent_list): only that agent's routines. Returns { status:"ok", data:[{ id, scope, org, team, name, schedule_in_words, agent, agent_key, unassigned (its agent is nowhere on this Mac: it never fires until routine_update gives it one), duplicate (another routine of its space has its id: it never fires), mode, effective_mode, where, runs_on, enabled, next_run_at, last_run:{status, reason, at}|null, owner, owner_name, created_by, armed_here, needs_you, revision, content_stale? }] }. `content_stale` ({ machine, since_ms, why }) marks a routine armed on a machine whose prepared content is behind it: the machine starts its agent from what was prepared before until routine_refresh_on_machine. Times are RFC3339. `runs_on` is `one_mac` (a shared job: it runs on exactly one Mac, and `armed_here` says it is this one; one written by hand that names no Mac runs nowhere, `armed_here` false and `next_run_at` null, until a save here places it on this Mac) or `each_mac` (a recipe each Mac runs: `enabled` says whether it is on for this Mac). `enabled`, `next_run_at`, `last_run` and `needs_you` are this Mac's. `id` is what every other routine tool takes; `revision` is routine_update's `baseRevision`.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

agent.description: Only the routines of this agent: its `id` or key from agent_list.

tools.name: routine_list

tools.description:
Publish a structured routine result candidate: your JSON `payload`, and optional `sessionId` (omitted, this connection's verified tab session for Claude or Codex; if supplied, the same tab only). An unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal. The recorded running session chooses the run and pinned schema; no runId is accepted. Call signal_done success after publication to promote the private snapshot. Returns {published:true}; failed status is an MCP error.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

sessionId.description:
Your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`. Omit it to use the tab this MCP connection
runs in.

tools.name: routine_publish_result

tools.description:
Routine refresh on machine — prepare a routine armed on a machine (routine_arm_on) from what it and its agent are now, and push it there. A machine-armed routine's workspace on its machine is prepared only when you arm, edit, resume or restore the routine, or call this: later changes to its agent's files or team content do not reach the machine on their own (edits to the routine's own definition do), and the machine starts the agent from what was last prepared. routine_list and routine_get show such a routine with `content_stale: { machine, since_ms, why }` until this is called. Required: `id`. Optional: `sessionId` (omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). The machine must be connected, and this Mac must be the one that manages the routine. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, machine, content_stale:false } }, or `validation` with why it could not (machine not connected, routine paused or handing over, its workspace on the machine not open, preparation failed). Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_refresh_on_machine

tools.description:
Read the last successful private structured result and latest attempt for routine id. Cached read only: never launches an agent; reports schema_compatible and success timestamp explicitly. Returns snapshot, latest_attempt status, revision and schema_compatible.
Docs: arc-g-routines/routine-yml.html

agent.description:
Only when it belongs to this agent (its `id` or key from agent_list):
a routine of another agent is `validation`.

id.description: The routine's `id` as `routine_list` returns it.

tools.name: routine_result

tools.description:
Routine run — one routine run in full, by id. Required: `runId` (a `run_id` from routine_runs, routine_get's `runs`, or routine_list's `last_run`). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ routine_id, routine_name, run_id, revision, source, phase, reason, linked_run_id, created_at, started_at, ended_at, result_text, detail, agent } }: the routine_runs row plus the routine it belongs to (`routine_id` is what routine_get takes); `detail` explains why it ended, as in routine_runs. `phase`: `queued` | `running` | `succeeded` | `failed` | `needs_you` (it ended asking you something; `result_text` is the question) | `ended` (its agent exited without signal_done) | `timed_out` | `cancelled` | `skipped` (did not run; `reason` says why) | `coalesced` (folded into `linked_run_id`). `source`: what fired it (`schedule`, `manual`, an event). Times are RFC3339. A run of a routine you cannot see is `validation`.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

runId.description:
A routine run's `run_id` (from routine_runs, routine_get's `runs`, or
routine_list's `last_run`).

tools.name: routine_run

tools.description:
Routine run now — fire any routine you can see once, by hand, on this Mac, through its own policy: a paused routine records a skip, and a run still going makes this fire coalesce, skip or wait per its `overlap`. Required: `id`. Optional: `variables` ({name: value} for its declared variables); `sessionId` (optional: omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ run_id, outcome } }, where outcome is `queued` (with `reason:"held"` when it waits behind the run still going), `coalesced` (with `active_run_id`), `skipped:<reason>`, or `duplicate` (this fire already has a run); or `validation`. Follow the run with routine_runs. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

variables.description: Values for the routine's declared variables.

tools.name: routine_run_now

tools.description:
Routine runs — a routine's run history, newest first, including fires that did not run (`skipped` with `reason`, `coalesced` with `linked_run_id`). Required: `id`. Optional: `limit` (default 50, max 200), `before` (the previous page's `next_before`). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ runs:[{ run_id, revision, source, phase, reason, linked_run_id, created_at, started_at, ended_at, result_text, detail, agent }], next_before } }. `agent` is the agent the run launched, as `<key>@<revision>`; a run whose agent did not resolve fails with reason `agent_unavailable`. `result_text` is what the agent produced (its `signal_done` summary); a run whose agent exited cleanly without calling it is `ended`, with none. `detail` explains why the run ended (a launch refusal, or a signal-only CLI's exit summary), or null; wake, machine and admission runs still explain themselves in `result_text`. Times are RFC3339.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

limit.description: At most this many runs (default 50, max 200).

tools.name: routine_runs

tools.description:
Routine set enabled — pause (`enabled:false`) or resume (`enabled:true`) any routine you can see. It changes only whether it fires from this Mac; the definition is untouched, so it is never a git change. A paused routine is a draft. For an `each_mac` routine this is "Run on my Mac": `true` turns it on for this Mac, `false` off. A shared job armed on another Mac (`armed_here` false) fires and is paused there; pausing it here changes nothing until it is moved to this Mac. Required: `id`, `enabled`. Optional: `sessionId` (optional: omitted, the verified connection; if supplied, the same caller only). Resuming counts against the 25 enabled-routine cap. Resuming a routine armed on a machine prepares it there. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, enabled, machine_warning? } } (`machine_warning`: resumed, but not prepared on its machine, and why), or `validation`. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; an unbound caller is refused. A supplied sessionId must name the caller itself.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

enabled.description:
false pauses it on this machine (turns an `each_mac` routine off for
this Mac); true resumes it (turns it on).

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tools.name: routine_set_enabled

tools.description:
Update a routine. Required: `id`; `baseRevision` (the `revision` you last read). Inside a run the agent can call `routine_context`. Routines never deliver results: if something should be sent, posted or filed, the task must say so. Pausing is routine_set_enabled, not this. Any routine you can see is yours to change, a teammate's included: it is a local context-repo edit, shared by a git push. Notifies no one. Returns { status:"ok", data:{ id, agent, schedule_in_words, next_fires, enabled, revision, warnings } } (warnings as for routine_create; machine_not_prepared means saved locally; delivery or preparation may be pending. The agent uses prior prepared content until preparation succeeds; routine_refresh_on_machine retries); { status:"conflict", data:{ message, current_revision } } when it changed since `baseRevision` (nothing was changed: routine_get it again and reapply); or `validation`. Events use the YAML model: events:[{kind:"inbox_idle"}] fires on idle sessions with unread mail; events:[{kind:"agent_done",from_agent:"reviewer"}] watches that agent finishing (omit from_agent for all in reach). Use events:[{kind:"role_pending"}] to watch every queue in reach. Use events:[{kind:"role_pending",role:"reviewer"}] to watch only reviewer mail. role must be nonblank and is valid only for role_pending; from_agent only for agent_done. No role or from_agent existence check. Omitted/null events keeps current events; [] clears these three kinds; nonempty replaces only them, preserving schedules and metadata triggers. Event errors return status:validation with events[i].field and a hint. These events support each_mac; machine arming restrictions still apply. metadataTriggers takes query_context selection, target eq and optional previous eq for a transition. Existing matches baseline at discovery/restart. [] clears metadata triggers; omitted/null keeps them. Metadata triggers require one_mac. Recipients use routine_context and the wake header runId. action:command runs command:[program,arg,...] directly without an agent/model; rendered argv is returned. Commands are team/local only, default overlap queue/maxRuntime 5m. Bare executables use PATH; relative executable paths must stay inside the team content root; absolute executable paths are refused. Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes bounded, secret-redacted output (last 4 KB). after:{routine:id,on:succeeded|finished} chains in the same space; finished excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced, cycles and missing upstream are refused. after:null clears on update. budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?} is fresh-agent only; raising/removing a cap needs native Accept. Verified caller required; sessionId must match.
Docs: arc-g-routines/trigger-cookbook.html

action.description:
agent (default) or command. action:command takes command:[program,arg,...]
instead of agent/task/mode; it runs as you, with no agent or model, in a
team workspace or managed repo clone. Defaults: overlap queue, maxRuntime 5m.
Only me and machine-armed command routines are refused.

after.description:
Fire after a routine in the same space succeeds or finishes. `finished`
excludes cancelled/skipped/coalesced. Cycles and missing upstream routines
are refused. Chained fires carry trigger.{run_id,routine,phase,result_text,detail}.
after:null removes it; omission preserves it.

agent.description:
Another agent, as for `routine_create`: the routine moves under it
(same id and history): how an Unassigned routine gets an agent.

baseRevision.description: The `revision` the change was made against.

budgetUsd.description:
budgetUsd {perDay?,perWeek?}: positive finite USD for the local calendar
day and Monday-start week, not rolling windows. Lowering is immediate
and ratchets the local accepted ceiling; raises/null removal need native
Accept. Omitted keeps the cap. Fresh only: wakes cap the agent; commands
cannot. Machine-armed caps are refused. Unrestricted shells are trusted;
sandbox untrusted agents.

command.description:
Program and arguments, one entry each. A bare program uses PATH; a relative
executable path must be executable inside the team content root; absolute
executable paths are refused. Args render individually, never through a shell.
Exit 0 succeeds; routine_run exposes the secret-redacted last 4 KB of output.

events.description:
Replaces inbox_idle, agent_done and role_pending triggers only; schedules and
metadata triggers stay. Omitted or null preserves; [] clears these events.

items.description: Event inputs share the YAML model's spelling and validation.

from_agent.description: agent_done only: agent id or full key; omitted watches all agents in reach.

role.description: role_pending only: nonempty queue name; omitted watches every queue in reach.

id.description: The routine's `id` as `routine_list` returns it.

machine.description: `local`, a machine id or `any`, as for `routine_create`.

maxWakes.description: As for routine_create; `null` removes the limit, omitted keeps it.

maxWakesPerDay.description: As for routine_create; `null` removes it, omitted keeps it.

metadataTriggers.description:
Metadata conditions using query_context's selection and eq clauses. Example:
[{"selection":{"where":{"kinds":["story"]}},"target":{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"in-progress"}}].
Add previous:{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"planning"} for an exact transition.
Matches at first discovery or restart are a baseline; only later entry fires.
Omit to preserve; [] removes metadata triggers on update, keeping other events.
Not with runsOn:each_mac. Recipients read changes with routine_context and
the wake header runId (incl. coalesced_payloads).

minGap.description: As for routine_create; `null` removes it, omitted keeps it.

resultSchema.description: Replaces the output schema; explicit null clears it, omission preserves it.

runsOn.description:
A team routine only: `one_mac` or `each_mac`, as for `routine_create`.
To `each_mac`: stays on the Mac that ran it as a shared job, off
elsewhere until turned on there. To `one_mac`: this editing Mac runs it
and others stop.

sessionId.description: Omit to use the verified connection identity. A supplied id must name that caller.

tz.description:
An IANA zone. Alone, it moves every schedule into it; with `when`, it is
the zone `when` is read in. Default: the routine's current zone.

when.description:
A new schedule (as for `routine_create`); replaces every schedule.
when:"" removes schedules and keeps events; omitted preserves schedules.

tools.description:
Type input into a terminal tab and submit it, or press one key. Address the tab by {handle} (from open_terminal_tab, open_remote_tab, open_workspace or list_sessions; never a raw sessionId) or by {tab} (its current name from list_sessions) with optional {machine}/{workspace}; ambiguous names return the candidate set. Give exactly one of {command} or {key}. {command}: when the tab is at a shell prompt it runs as a shell command (it may itself start an agent, e.g. `claude "fix the build"`); when Claude or Codex is running in the tab — launched that way, or started by hand in a shell — it is sent as a prompt: the text, then Enter as a separate keystroke so the agent submits it rather than leaving it in its input box (multi-line text is sent as one paste). {key}: one key alone, nothing typed — `enter` submits whatever is already in an agent's input box; also `escape`, `tab`, `shift-tab`, `backspace`, `ctrl-c`, `ctrl-d`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`. Gated by the Interactive tier. Local tab: `{submitted, input?}`. Remote tab: `{status: submitted|notSent|unknown|refused, submitted: true|false|null, input?, code?, message?}`. `input` says how a command was sent: `shell` or `agent`. `unknown` means the input may have been typed or submitted — check with read_terminal_tab and never automatically resend it.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

command.description:
The input to type and submit: a shell command, or — when Claude or Codex is
running in the tab — a prompt or slash command. Give this or `key`.
Remote `status: unknown, submitted: null` means it may have been submitted;
never automatically replay that input.

handle.description:
The opaque terminal handle returned by `open_terminal_tab`, `open_remote_tab`
or `list_sessions`. Give this or `tab`.

anyOf.description: A key `run_in_terminal_tab` can send on its own.

key.description:
One key to send on its own, nothing else typed: `enter` submits what is
already in an agent's input box; also `escape`, `tab`, `shift-tab`,
`backspace`, `ctrl-c`, `ctrl-d`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`. Give this
or `command`.

machine.description: With `tab`: the machine it runs on, by label ("This Mac" for this one).

tab.description: The tab's name as its tab bar shows it now (e.g. "Terminal 2"), instead of a handle.

workspace.description: With `tab`: the workspace id it is in.

tools.name: run_in_terminal_tab

tools.description:
Save a personal or team machine declaration using existing authorization. mode defaults to private-account, the only mode that opens terminal tabs; saving a legacy machine with mode private-account converts it in place (same id, host key and settings). connect validates setup; use connect_machine for actual runtime admission. Auto-connect remains default off.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/machine-tools.html

mode.description: Absent: a saved machine keeps its own mode; a new one is a private account.

tools.name: save_machine

tools.description:
Attach an existing local source Git checkout by absolute repoPath. Reads its origin locally and saves the checkout through the desktop attachment/reconcile service under the selected profile. Optional `attribution` (`on` | `off` | `auto`) sets git-ai line-attribution capture for the repo: `auto` (default) is on. Optional `notes` (`local` | `push`) sets where its notes go: `local` (default) keeps them on this Mac in refs/notes/sense, never pushed; `push` pushes them to the repo's origin (https and ssh forms), including notes written while the repo was local, and applies at once, and is refused as `no_remote` without an origin (nothing in that request is saved). With `notes`, the result has `notes: {mode, applied}`: `now`, `pending` (saved; applies once git-ai is installed), `unsupported` with message (this git-ai cannot keep notes local) or `failed` with message (saved, applied at the next launch). The push list is the union of every local profile's choices. `private` is deprecated and ignored. `attribution:on` may install the pinned, verified bundled git-ai; it also releases an unsupported user_pinned manual restore and reinstalls the bundle; it waits up to about 30 s and returns `attribution.kind: installing` if still running; `install_failed` includes a message and `unsupported` includes a reason. Relaunch sessions started during installation to enable capture. Checkout attachment does no provider lookup, credential lookup, clone or commit; afterwards CodeSense fetches origin once in the background (bounded, into refs/remotes/origin/* only, never prompting; see refresh_history). Use commit_registry_edit_local AddSourceRepoToTeam to register its source identity in a team. Paths are on this Mac; no active team required.
Docs: arc-b-model/orgs.html

anyOf.description: A repository's capture choice as the save-source tool names it.

oneOf.description: No explicit choice: capture is on.

attribution.description:
Line-attribution capture for this repo: `on`, `off`, or `auto` (the default: on).
Omit to leave the current choice.

anyOf.description: Where a repo's attribution notes go. Unset means local: they stay on this machine.

oneOf.description: Notes stay on this machine (`refs/notes/sense`, never pushed).
Notes push to this repo's origin with the branch.

notes.description:
Where this repo's attribution notes go: `local` (the default: `refs/notes/sense`, kept
on this machine) or `push` (to origin with the branch; refused as `no_remote` without
an origin). Omit to leave the current choice.

private.description:
Deprecated and ignored: capture no longer depends on whether the repo is private.
Accepted for one release so existing callers keep working.

repoPath.description: Absolute existing source Git checkout root. Its origin is read locally.
