tools.description:
Schedule wakeup — temporary routine / reminder for THIS session only — use it when asked to 'add a routine for your session', 'remind yourself', or 'check X every N minutes'. Unlike routine_create (a saved routine on an Agent that wakes its running session or starts a new one, and persists), the prompt is typed into this same conversation so you keep your context, and it ends when this session ends. When it fires, CodeSense types `prompt` into your terminal as a new message once you are idle: never while you are working or waiting on a permission prompt; a fire waits up to 24 h for you to be idle (then it is dropped as busy_timeout), and fires due while one still waits collapse into it. Works in any interactive CodeSense session, saved agent or not, on this Mac or a connected machine, where CodeSense can tell when the agent is idle (Claude; not a plain shell, not Codex yet); not for headless runs. It belongs to the session you call from, ends with it (exit, close, crash), and never starts anything. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, checked against the terminal you call from: another session's id is refused), `prompt`, and exactly one of `in` (a duration: `90s`, `20m`, `2h`, `1h30m`, `1d`; prefer it for relative times) or `at` (an RFC 3339 time WITH its offset, in the future, e.g. `2026-10-05T14:30:00-07:00`; `date +%z` prints your offset). The first fire must be within 366 days. Optional: `every` (repeat interval, at least `1m`), then at most one of `until` (RFC 3339 with offset, after the first fire) or `count` (fires, at least 1); `minGap` (`30m`, `2h`; 1m to `7d`: the least time between two of its deliveries; a fire inside it folds into the last one; a terminal server too old to enforce it refuses the timer); `name` (shown in the marker and the list; default: the prompt's first words). Choose the limits for the work each wake starts: a light check needs none, e.g. `{"in":"15m","every":"15m","prompt":"Check CI; if it is green, say so in one line"}` may fire hundreds of times over a week; a heavy one, e.g. `{"in":"1h","every":"1h","minGap":"3h","prompt":"Rebuild and rerun the integration suite"}`, never wakes you again inside three hours. Limits: 10 active timers per session, 200 per machine; a safety backstop of 120 wakes an hour per session (all sources together) refuses the rest as rate_limited, posts one inbox note and resumes on its own; prompt plus its header at most 8 KiB. Each delivery starts with `[timer: <name> | fire <n>]`. Setting needs the CodeSense desktop connected; while it is away, timers already set keep firing, and on a machine list_wakeups and cancel_wakeup are answered by the machine. Returns { timerId, nextAt (RFC 3339, UTC), name, machineId, sessionId }; a refusal is an MCP error that says why. Identity comes from the verified MCP connection; a supplied sessionId must name that caller, and an unbound caller is refused.
Docs: arc-g-routines/index.html

at.description:
First fire at this RFC 3339 time with its offset
(`2026-10-05T14:30:00-07:00` or `…Z`); in the future.

count.description: Stop after this many fires (at least 1).

every.description: Then repeat this often (at least `1m`). Omit for a one-shot timer.

in.description:
First fire after this long: `90s`, `20m`, `2h`, `1h30m`, `1d`.
Exactly one of `in` or `at`.

name.description:
A short name for the marker and the list (default: the prompt's
first words).

prompt.description: What your session receives when the timer fires.

sessionId.description:
Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`, checked against the terminal
you call from: another session's id is refused.

until.description:
Stop repeating after this RFC 3339 time (with offset), after the first
fire. At most one of `until` or `count`.

tools.name: schedule_wakeup

tools.description:
Send an inbox message to an agent session or the human. To the human, set {kind}: "needs-you" when it waits on them (a question, a decision, something only they can unblock), "update" for progress, "merged", "done" (informational). Both kinds appear as conversations in the human Inbox; all unread human mail counts in its badge. Kind remains available to agent views and dashboards. Omitted, it is an "update" unless you set a {replyTo} naming someone other than the human, yourself or a role you hold (a question whose answer must reach someone) — so mark every question or decision `kind:"needs-you"`, or use ask_user when you must wait for the answer; a manager's digest with replyTo "role:manager" is an update. Durable. Optional {requestId} replays the original messageId for the same key and payload; changed payloads are refused. A recipient CodeSense can tell (inboxWaiter true in list_sessions) hears the inbox notice: an idle one starts a turn, a running one hears at its next step or turn. A Claude is told by its inbox waiter; an idle Codex is started a turn with it through its own engine (headed `[inbox <token>]`; this needs Codex 0.159.3 or a newer 0.x release), and a working one hears it at its next tool call or prompt. If Claude's waiter died, guarded recovery submits only the inbox notice when idle, with tools connected, empty input and no person typing. A recipient it cannot tell (inboxWaiter false in list_sessions: its CLI has no wake path, or its waiter has gone) keeps its mail held; wake it with send_to_session telling it to call read_messages. A supported CLI can be inbox-ready before its first prompt once its engine and trusted observers establish readiness; startup menus, approvals and unavailable engines keep it unready. Collect replies with read_messages. Args: {to} (a list_sessions handle or "human"), {text}, {session_id} (optional: omit it to use this connection's verified tab identity, including a CLI started by hand in a CodeSense tab; if supplied it must name that same tab; an unbound connection is refused (start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal), never sent as the human; the message shows as the sender's current tab name, see who_am_i). Optional: {contentType} "plain"|"markdown"|"html" — markdown is the default so **bold** / code fences / tables render formatted. html to the human is a LIVE DASHBOARD: it renders in the Inbox exactly like an HTML dashboard file — scripts run, `window.codesense` is available (sessions(), inbox(), roles(), act(...) through the same action gate), and the frame hears pushed events (codesense:inbox-changed, codesense:agent-activity-changed); see get_live_data_contract. html to another agent is sanitized to plain formatting (agents read text). {onClick} makes the row actionable in the inbox: `{type:"goto-agent",agentId}` jumps to that agent's terminal, `{type:"open-file",path}` opens the path in the viewer, `{type:"show-message"}` (default) opens the thread. {media:{url|path,alt}} adds a GIF/image; alt and one source required. {attachFile} is a logical team-content path rendered as an attachment card with Open. {replyTo} is where replies to this message go instead of to you, like an email Reply-To (the answer goes ONLY there, not also to you): a running session's handle, "human", or `role:<agent id>` (that role's durable queue — any instance claims it with claim_role_messages). Use `role:` when you may exit before the answer: {replyTo:"role:manager"} sends the human's reply to the manager's durable role queue. {summary} is one plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this message's preview in the human's Inbox and lists. Set it for html and long markdown; otherwise the preview is derived. Returns `{status:"sent",messageId,kind?,hint?}` or `{status:"invalid",message}` — `kind` (to the human) says whether it waits on them; `hint` says when an unmarked question defaulted to update (it is never reclassified by its words) — (blank text without media / unknown recipient / a sessionId that is not running / a replyTo session that is not running).
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

attachFile.description:
Optional logical team-content path to attach — the inbox renders an
attachment card with an Open button. Stored verbatim; blank/omitted means no
attachment.

anyOf.description:
How a message body should be rendered. Stored as the lowercase variant name
on `wv_inbox.content_type`; omitted/`None` means the FE renderer applies its
default (`markdown` — see `DESIGN-inbox-ux.md` §3).

contentType.description:
How to render the body. `"markdown"` (default) renders GFM — tables,
strikethrough, task lists, highlighted code fences. `"plain"` preserves
whitespace with no formatting. `"html"` to the human is a live dashboard:
it renders in the Inbox like an HTML dashboard file, with scripts, the
`window.codesense` bridge, pushed events and actions through the same
action gate (e.g. `<script>codesense.sessions().then(...)</script>`).
`"html"` to another agent is sanitized to plain formatting.

anyOf.description:
What a message asks of the human, for agent views and dashboards. The human
inbox shows both kinds as conversations and counts all unread human mail. Stored as given on `wv_inbox.kind` (NULL when the sender set none); reads
resolve the effective kind with [`InboxMessage::effective_kind`].

oneOf.description: Waits on the human: a question, a decision, something only they can unblock.
Informational: progress, "merged", "done".

kind.description:
What the message asks of the human, for agent views and dashboards:
`"needs-you"` (waits on them: a question, a decision) or `"update"` (progress,
"merged", "done"). Omitted: `"needs-you"` when `replyTo` names someone other than
the human, the sender or a role the sender holds, else `"update"`.

media.description: Optional GIF or image: exactly one of HTTPS url or local path, and required alt text.

anyOf.description:
Per-message click action attached by the sender. Stored verbatim as JSON on
`wv_inbox.on_click`; omitted/`None` is the ordinary "open the thread" default.

oneOf.description:
Click the row → focus the agent's running terminal (`agents-list.tsx`
`onLocate`). The id is the agent definition id (`agents_list` row key —
the sender picks the agent to jump to; the UI resolves to a running
session at click time).

Click the row → open `path` in the viewer. The host validates the path
against the sender's team content root before opening (`openFileInTeam`).

Explicit default — same as omitting the field. Kept so an agent that
wants the row to open the message view can say so.

replyTo.description:
Where replies to this message go instead of to the sender, like an email
Reply-To (the answer goes ONLY there): a running session's handle, `"human"`, or
`"role:<agent id>"` (that role's durable queue). Use a role when the sender may
be gone before the answer comes: a worker that asks the human with
`replyTo: "role:manager"` and then exits still gets the answer to the manager's
queue. Omit for replies to come back to the sender.

requestId.description: Retry key: reuse the same value and payload after a transport disconnect.

session_id.description:
Omit to send as this connection's verified tab, including a CLI started by hand
in a CodeSense terminal. If supplied, it must name that same tab. An unbound
connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal. The message shows
the tab's current name. MCP cannot send as the person.

summary.description:
One plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this message's preview in the
human's Inbox and lists. Set it whenever contentType is html (otherwise the
preview is derived from the markup) and for long markdown messages.

text.description: Message body. Renders as `contentType` (markdown by default).

to.description: Recipient: a session handle from `list_sessions`, or `"human"`.

tools.name: send_message

tools.description:
Send a message addressed to a ROLE (any role name, usually an agent id); the inbox row + pending wv_role_delivery row commit together. {requestId} is an idempotency key: same key + same payload replays the stored {messageId, deliveryId}; same key + different payload returns `conflict` and the original wins (payload hash includes text, attachFile, contentType, replyTo and summary). Omit requestId to always create a new row. {sender} defaults to this connection's verified tab, including a CLI started by hand in a CodeSense terminal. A supplied sender must name that same tab. Unbound callers are refused; MCP cannot send as the human. The message stays queued until an instance of the role claims it (claim_role_messages); reading the queue never claims, and routines with a `role_pending` trigger hear of it. {replyTo} is where replies to this message go instead of to you, like an email Reply-To (the answer goes ONLY there, not also to you): a running session's handle, "human", or `role:<agent id>` (that role's durable queue — any instance claims it with claim_role_messages). Use `role:` when you may be gone before the answer comes: a worker briefed by a manager sends its question to the human with {replyTo:"role:manager"}, then exits; the human's reply lands as a pending delivery in the manager role's queue, not in the dead worker's inbox. The inbox shows "Replies go to: …" under the message. Optional: {contentType} "plain"|"markdown"|"html" — markdown is the default so **bold** / code fences / tables render formatted; html is strictly sanitized (scripts, iframes, forms, event handlers, and non-http(s)/mailto/# URLs are dropped). {onClick} makes the row actionable in the inbox: `{type:"goto-agent",agentId}`, `{type:"open-file",path}`, or `{type:"show-message"}` (default). {attachFile} is a logical team-content path rendered as an attachment card with Open. {summary} is one plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this message's preview in inbox lists. Set it whenever contentType is html (otherwise the preview is derived from the markup) and for long markdown messages. Returns `{status:"sent",messageId,deliveryId}`, `{status:"conflict"}`, or `{status:"invalid",message}` (blank text / a replyTo session that is not running).
Docs: arc-f-inboxes-and-triage/index.html

attachFile.description:
Optional logical team-content path to attach — the inbox renders an
attachment card with an Open button. Part of the `requestId` hash.

anyOf.description:
How a message body should be rendered. Stored as the lowercase variant name
on `wv_inbox.content_type`; omitted/`None` means the FE renderer applies its
default (`markdown` — see `DESIGN-inbox-ux.md` §3).

contentType.description:
How to render the body. `"markdown"` (default) renders GFM. `"plain"`
preserves whitespace with no formatting. `"html"` is strictly sanitized via
DOMPurify — scripts, iframes, forms, style tags, and event handlers are
dropped, non-https?/mailto/# URL schemes are rejected, only a plain
formatting tag allowlist survives. Part of the `requestId` hash.

anyOf.description:
Per-message click action attached by the sender. Stored verbatim as JSON on
`wv_inbox.on_click`; omitted/`None` is the ordinary "open the thread" default.

oneOf.description:
Click the row → focus the agent's running terminal (`agents-list.tsx`
`onLocate`). The id is the agent definition id (`agents_list` row key —
the sender picks the agent to jump to; the UI resolves to a running
session at click time).

Click the row → open `path` in the viewer. The host validates the path
against the sender's team content root before opening (`openFileInTeam`).

Explicit default — same as omitting the field. Kept so an agent that
wants the row to open the message view can say so.

replyTo.description:
Where replies to this message go instead of to the sender, like an email
Reply-To (the answer goes ONLY there): a running session's handle, `"human"`, or
`"role:<agent id>"` (that role's durable queue). Use a role when the sender may
be gone before the answer comes: a worker that asks the human with
`replyTo: "role:manager"` and then exits still gets the answer to the manager's
queue. Omit for replies to come back to the sender.

requestId.description:
Idempotency key. A retry under the same key with the SAME payload (text +
attachFile + contentType + replyTo + summary) replays the stored `{messageId, deliveryId}`.
A retry under the same key with a DIFFERENT payload returns
`status:"conflict"` and the original stays authoritative. Omit to always
create a new row.

role.description: Role id — usually an agent id (from `agent_list`).

sender.description:
Sender identifier (a session handle, or `"human"`). Omit to send as the tab this
MCP connection runs in; a caller outside any CodeSense tab, or in a tab CodeSense
did not launch or register (one started by hand), is `"human"`.

summary.description:
One plain-text line (≤280 chars) shown as this message's preview in inbox
lists. Set it whenever contentType is html (otherwise the preview is derived
from the markup) and for long markdown messages. Part of the `requestId` hash.

team.description:
The `(org, team)` the role mailbox lives in. The viewer-visible
team identity, mirroring `InboxTeam`.

text.description: Message body. Renders as `contentType` (markdown by default).

tools.description:
Send a prompt to a running agent session (Claude or Codex) by {handle} — the handle open_workspace, open_remote_tab or list_sessions gave you; a raw sessionId, or a handle with no running session, is refused and nothing is written. Args: {handle}, {text} (non-empty; a slash command works). The text is typed into the agent's input box and then Enter is sent as a separate keystroke, so it is submitted, not left as a draft (multi-line text is sent as one paste). Works for agents on this Mac and on remote machines. Gated by the Interactive tier. Local: returns `{submitted}` (false: the agent did not visibly start working; it may still be in its input box — check read_terminal_tab, or press Enter with run_in_terminal_tab {handle, key: "enter"}). Remote: returns `{status: submitted|notSent|unknown|refused, submitted: true|false|null, input, code?, message?}` — `unknown` means the prompt may have been submitted: check read_terminal_tab and never automatically resend it. Submitted text is also recorded in the target's inbox conversation (marked typed into terminal, already read) so its history shows it.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

handle.description: The opaque session handle returned by `open_workspace`.

text.description: The text to deliver to the live agent session (non-empty).

tools.description:
Adopt a file into team content — write `content` to `logicalName` in team content (`targetLayer`: "TeamProjection", the only layer). Only that team file changes: nothing is copied into any workspace (an agent gets it at its next launch if its context declares it, or by hydrate_worktree). Pass `expectedLayerHash` to refuse overwriting a team file that changed. To publish edits made in a workspace, prefer preview_reverse_sync_worktree then reverse_sync_worktree.
Docs: arc-k-sync/layer-tools.html

codeRepoPath.description:
CWD-derived; contract symmetry with Push (the only difference
between Push and Adopt is whether a lockfile entry already exists).

expectedLayerHash.description: Optional 64-digit blake3 hash of the current layer bytes; mismatch refuses overwrite.

targetLayer.description:
The content layer a file lives in.

**On-wire serialization** is by variant name. The retired install tiers are
gone. Inbound, `TeamWorkspace` (the old repo-agnostic default)
still loads as team content; `TeamRepo` (the per-repo tier) is refused
with a pointer to the repo tier's publish (`reverse_sync_worktree
{to:"repo"}`) — it must never land team-wide (review r1). The lockfile /
install-state readers go through [`super::lockfile::WireLayerId`], which
maps stored rows (and drains the retired tiers' wave rows).

oneOf.description: The team's own content — `{org_root}/{team}/content/`.

tools.name: sense_sync_adopt

tools.description:
List content layers — the content layers with their `writable` and `backed` flags. Today there is one: team content (`TeamProjection`). Read-only.
Docs: arc-k-sync/layer-tools.html
tools.name: sense_sync_list_layers

tools.description:

tools.description:
Read one session's joined record, models, tokens, cost, allowed/used tools, timing, story and run outcome. Required sessionId is a CodeSense or CLI-native id naming the subject, not the caller. Returns {session (record or null), nativeSessionIds, story, run, models, cost, tools, tasks, retries, unavailable}. Models have model,calls,tokens,costUsd,costSource,reason; cost has totalUsd,source,reason,state. Source is reported, rate_table, mixed, or null. Unknown cost is null with a reason; a real zero-token call can cost 0. tools.used groups name,mcpServer,calls,errors,errorUnknown (unknown isError is never success). firstError is the earliest indexed failure; firstRetainedError is the earliest failure outside the dropped-turn interval, or null when no failure text is retained. Each candidate has turn and toolUseId; confirm its conversation lookup before linking. tools.usedState and usedReason distinguish present/truncated/expired counts from absent/unsupported/unavailable (used:null); expired retains the index. allowed comes from the record. Timing is session.timing (milliseconds). retries is null: no retry signal is recorded. Missing record/fields keep explicit unavailable reasons; an id with no record or usage is an error. Optional include:[conversation] adds the existing conversation page with present/truncated/absent/expired/unsupported/unavailable state. Use cursor (next turn index) and limit (1–200, default 20), or jump with turn (zero-based) or toolUseId (default 1 turn; a Codex exec-… file-change id jumps to its enclosing call). cursor, turn and toolUseId are exclusive and require conversation include. include:[turns] instead pages the same turns as summaries {index,role,tsMs,text (200 chars),toolCalls,toolErrors,model} (same cursor, limit, turn and toolUseId and the same states) with no tool input or result text, and the answer holds only session {sessionId,cli,branch,timing}, story and turns (not both includes). Conversation is omitted otherwise. Read scope matches session_usage: every local agent can read every session; caller content scope only gates story enrichment. Dashboard codesense.sessionRead takes identical arguments and returns identical JSON from the same backend. Next: page conversation with nextCursor, or read_run with session.runId for run evidence.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

cursor.description: Next turn index from the preceding conversation page.

include.description:
Omit for facts only. `conversation` pages the stored turns in full. `turns` pages them as
summaries (index, role, tsMs, text up to 200 chars, toolCalls, toolErrors, model) with no
tool input or result and no provided skills (a call whose failure is not recorded adds
toolErrorsUnknown), and the answer holds only the session's id, cli, branch and timing, its
story, the reasons for those and the page. Not both.

limit.description: Turns to return (1–200). Defaults to 20, or 1 for a jump.

sessionId.description: A CodeSense session id or the CLI's native session id. Names the subject, not the caller.

toolUseId.description: Jump to the turn containing this CLI-native tool call id.

turn.description: Jump to this zero-based turn index; exclusive with cursor and toolUseId.

tools.name: session_read

tools.description:
Token use and spend per agent session on this Mac and the remote machines it connects to, from each agent CLI's own reports. A connected machine's usage is pulled each minute, so its newest calls can take a minute or so to appear; a disconnected machine's arrive when it next connects. It is read-only. It covers only the sessions CodeSense launched (their telemetry is switched on at launch); while this Mac's managed Claude settings send session telemetry elsewhere, a Claude session's usage is read from its own session log when each turn ends, so it can take a minute or so to appear. Optional: `sinceMs`, `untilMs` (epoch milliseconds; counted by whole local day: sinceMs's day is included, untilMs's day is excluded), `sessionId` (one session), `cwd` (one working directory, exact path, e.g. a PR's worktree), `story` (one story id, e.g. `DEMO-5`: only the sessions spent on it; the days and totals cover only them), `limit` (the most sessions to return, newest first; the totals still cover them all), `cursor` (the previous page's `nextCursor`, with the same other args). Returns `{sessions, days, totals, total, nextCursor?, unavailableReason?}`; `nextCursor` is present only when more sessions follow, so pass it back as `cursor` to read the next page (during a walk a session that becomes active moves to the first page; a walk is complete when its distinct sessionIds equal total, otherwise walk again from page 1 through continuation, merging by sessionId, up to 2 recovery rewalks; after that report the truthful latest N of M). Each session is `{sessionId, cli (`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`), org, team, agent, machineId, cwd, story, models, firstAtMs, lastAtMs, messages, tokens: {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, costUsd, unpricedModels, runId}`, newest activity first. `org`, `team` and `agent` say who ran it and are null when it was not launched by CodeSense or launched before attribution existed. `runId` is the run it worked (a list_runs `outcome.run_id`), from the session's durable record, and null when it has no record or ran outside a run. `machineId` is the machine it ran on, as list_machines names it (`local` for this Mac; the machine of its latest call when its usage came from more than one). `story` is the story the session was spent on, `{id, title, status, epic, basis?}` (title, status and epic from the story file's frontmatter, null when it does not say), or null when the session is not tied to a story: a session whose cwd is a story worktree (as list_worktrees lists it) or a folder inside one is that story's, else the story its launch was opened for (open_workspace's storyId), when that launch is still listed (title, status and epic then come from the org's story file); else a context worktree named `<team>/<epic>-<n>` (under context-worktrees) joins the story whose id ends `-<EPIC>-<n>` in that team, with `basis:"associated"` (no basis means exact). `days` has one entry per local day with usage, newest first, with `{day, tokens, costUsd, unpricedModels}`. Each API message counts once, including one the CLI sends on its own: Codex's start-up cache warm-up (input, no output) counts, though Codex's own "tokens used" total leaves it out. `costUsd` is null when a call used tokens on a model with no confirmed list price (`unpricedModels` names it), so that session's tokens still count. `totals` sums tokens, the cost of priced sessions, and counts `pricedSessions` and `unpricedSessions`. Next: model_rates for the prices on file, set_model_rate to price a model in `unpricedModels` with a price the user gives. A dashboard's codesense.sessionUsage() returns the same. Spend caps use this same priced event store and local calendar-day keys across machines; day windows and Monday-start weeks detect unpriced models and refuse new work for a capped scope.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

cursor.description:
The `nextCursor` of the previous page: continue after the last session it returned. Pass the
same other fields. A cursor from a different window or filter is refused.

cwd.description: Only usage recorded in this working directory (a workspace path, exact match).

limit.description: The most sessions to return, newest first. The totals still cover every session. Omitted: all.

sessionId.description: Only this session's usage (a session id from list_sessions or sessions()).

sinceMs.description: Count from the local day containing this time (epoch milliseconds). Omitted: no lower bound.

story.description:
Only the sessions spent on this story (a story id, e.g. `DEMO-5`; see each session's
`story`).

untilMs.description:
Count up to, not including, the local day containing this time (epoch milliseconds). Omitted:
no upper bound.

tools.description:
Set model rate — set a model's price from a local day, and price the usage it covers. Rates are the user's: set one only with prices the user gave or confirmed, never a guess. Required: `modelPrefix` (a model id or a prefix of it, e.g. `claude-opus-5-5`: at least 6 lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes, not starting or ending in a dot or dash; the longest matching prefix prices a model, so a family prefix such as `claude` prices only models with no longer prefix of their own; dots are stored as dashes, as model ids are matched), `effectiveFrom` (local day `YYYY-MM-DD`, from `1970-01-01`), `inputPerMtok`, `outputPerMtok` (USD per million tokens). Optional: `cacheReadPerMtok` (omitted: 0.1x input), `long` (`{fromTokens, inputPerMtok, outputPerMtok, cacheReadPerMtok?}`: the prices of a call whose prompt is over `fromTokens` tokens; omitted: one price at every prompt length). A rate is the whole price from its day on: a price it leaves out falls back to its default even where an earlier rate named one, so to change one price, read the model's rate with model_rates and pass every price it has. Every price is above 0 and at most 100000; `fromTokens` is a whole number from 1; `null` is the same as leaving a price out; an unknown key is refused. A later day adds a rate, so earlier usage keeps its price; the same model and day replaces the rate there, so a mistyped rate can be corrected. It then prices the usage it covers that was unpriced or priced from the rate table, each call at the rate in force on its own day, so a later rate still prices the days after it; a cost the agent CLI reported is never changed. It is recorded with `source` `set by an agent`. Returns `{changed}`, how many costs it changed. Next: model_rates to see the stored rates, session_usage for the new costs. A dashboard's codesense.setModelRate() does the same, returning the count alone. Safety: MCP and page changes that lower any effective price, or price an unpriced model, are saved pending and return changed:0, pending:true. Only a native app acceptance applies them. Raising prices applies immediately. Running turns finish, but capped agents with unpriced usage cannot launch or wake.
Docs: arc-e-agents/spend-caps.html

effectiveFrom.description: The local day it applies from, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Usage before that day keeps its price.

anyOf.description:
A long prompt's prices as the page's `setModelRate` and the MCP `set_model_rate` pass them and
`modelRates` returns them (USD per million tokens).

fromTokens.description: A call whose prompt (input, cache reads and cache writes) is over this many tokens.

inputPerMtok.description: USD per million input tokens on a long prompt.

outputPerMtok.description: USD per million output tokens on a long prompt.

long.description: Omitted or null: one price at every prompt length.

modelPrefix.description:
The model id, or a prefix of it, the rate prices (e.g. `claude-opus-5-5`): at least six
lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes, not starting or ending in a dot or dash. The
longest matching prefix prices a model.

tools.name: set_model_rate

The edit stays a local working-tree change of the context repo (publish it to share it). Returns { status:"ok", data:{ orgSlug, edit:"SetTeamLandingPage", team, starterPage } }; a missing `path`, a missing, hidden or outside file, an unknown team, or the read-only CodeSense Docs returns { status:"validation", message } and changes nothing.

relative to the team's content folder (`guide/start.md`), or an absolute

tools.description:
Update CodeSense viewer state. Pass a partial JSON patch. navLens: {teamKey: {source, view}} selects clone or private and opens that team nav without switching teams. Private switches Files, Changes and History; view defaults to the current view. The first private selection per org makes a local baseline commit; never pushed. Only source and view are accepted. Unknown teams or sources reject the whole patch. A context worktree id or name (list_worktrees kind:context) selects its Changes, default view changes; Files stays your clone. Reserved clone/private win. shown:false means another team is showing; use set_active_team only if asked.

Viewer state fields (per-team fields are keyed by teamKey, `${orgSlug}:${teamName}`):
- openedTeams: [teamKey] — teams the user has visited this session
- activeTab: {teamKey: filePath} — which file is shown per team
- openTabs: {teamKey: [{name, path}]} — open file tabs per team
- drillPaths: {teamKey: dirPath} — nav drill root per team
- cliChrome: {visible, layoutMode, lastTerminalMode, splitRatio, expanded, agentsDockCollapsed, agentsDockWidth} — the CLI's chrome, one value for every team. A write is merged field by field and honoured as asked: the agent decides, and may leave full screen, fold the CLI or bring it back. layoutMode is 'console' (full screen), 'shared' (a pane under the viewer) or 'viewer' (folded); visibility follows it (a 'shared' write may carry visible: false), and a shown layout becomes lastTerminalMode unless the write names one. visible written alone folds the CLI (false) or brings it back in lastTerminalMode (true). splitRatio is the viewer's share of the left column above the CLI pane (clamped to 0.1..0.9); expanded zooms the focused workspace when the team has multiple tiles and stays set with fewer tiles; agentsDockWidth is px or null
- navCollapsed: {teamKey: bool} — left-nav collapsed state per team
- navLens: {teamKey: {source, view}} — context nav source (clone, private or a context worktree id or name) and view; worktrees default to changes; writing source opens the nav. Only source and view are writable.
- terminalLayout (read-only; get_viewer_state only): the terminal hosts' layouts, one snapshot per host — `workspaces` keyed `{teamKey}|{workspace id, or a story's story_id}` → {tabs: [{session, name, role, placement, state}], lastActive, grid}. Terminals are opened and closed through their host (open_terminal_tab); set_viewer_state cannot change them
- statusNavExpandedPaths: {teamKey: [dirPath]} — expanded folders in status nav per team
- rightPaneOpen: bool — right-pane visibility (global; hosts the Inbox, Notes and custom panes)
- rightPaneRatio: number — right-pane width ratio (global)
- rightPaneLayout: {sections: [{id, group: {panelIds, activePanelId}, collapsed, size}]} — the right pane's layout (global; ordered sections → tab-groups). Its panels are the Inbox (`weft-board`), Notes (`scratch`) and custom panes (`pane:…`); a panel id that is none of these is dropped. Send the whole `sections` array — partial array patches are replaced wholesale, not merged
- settings: {editor, terminal, appTheme, viewerFontSize, ...} — app settings. appTheme: codesense | dracula | github | nord | catppuccin | confluence

A caller that knows only a repoPath resolves it to a teamKey first. rightPaneOpen, rightPaneRatio and cliChrome are global, so a per-team patch of them is invalid: the app ignores it, and its next save corrects what get_viewer_state returns. set_viewer_state takes a partial JSON patch — e.g. {"openTabs": {"acme:default": [{"name": "a.md", "path": "/a.md"}]}}
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/reacting-to-state.html

state.description: Partial JSON object to merge into the viewer state. Only include fields you want to change.

tools.name: set_viewer_state

tools.description:
Share a published dashboard on share.codesense.ai: add or remove viewers by email. Omit add and remove to list the current viewers. Changes apply to the server's current list, so addresses you do not name keep their access (unless the list is changed from somewhere else at the same moment; the last change wins). An address may not be in both add and remove. On a dashboard that streams terminals, added addresses wait for a person to confirm in the CodeSense app (the audience is unchanged until then); removing is immediate. Each added address gets an invite email; invite emails are reviewed before they are sent. Removing an address ends that viewer's open sessions at once. Pass dashboard as the absolute folder path. Returns {slug, viewers, notOnList}: notOnList names addresses asked to be removed that were not viewers. A child agent cannot share a parent's dashboard or list its viewers, even when the files are shared; a human can.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

add.description: Email addresses to give access to.

dashboard.description: Absolute path of the dashboard folder on this Mac (the folder holding dashboard.yml).

remove.description: Email addresses to take access from. Their open sessions end at once.

tools.name: share_dashboard

tools.description:
Report that your managed task is FINISHED — your FINAL act (the completion contract). `status`: `success` | `failed` | `needs-attention`. CodeSense records the outcome and notifies watchers; it does NOT run tests, validate, or move the story's status (do that yourself if your task says to). Going quiet without calling this leaves the session flagged `needs-attention` (not silently done). A routine run is the exception — its task decides. `needs-attention` records a completed outcome; it does not mean a permission prompt or needs-you. Optional `requestId` deduplicates retries with the same payload; reuse it after a disconnect. Optional `summary` is a short result line. Optional `doneRecord` (`{dispatchId, leg1Source, leg2Footprint, leg3Packet}`) is the Weft 3-leg verify payload a worker populates. Returns `{recorded}`. Inputs: `status`, and optional `sessionId` (omitted, this connection's verified tab session for Claude or Codex; if supplied, the same tab only). An unbound connection is refused; start the CLI in a CodeSense terminal.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

anyOf.description:
The wire shape of the worker-supplied 3-leg done record (a dedicated
sub-struct rather than inlining the four fields into `SignalDoneParams`, per
Task 5c). Deserialized with `#[serde(default)]` on `SignalDoneParams.done_record`
so existing call sites that omit it are unaffected.

leg1Source.description: Leg 1 — the canonical source ref the worker read at job start.

doneRecord.description:
The OPTIONAL 3-leg done record. A Weft worker populates it as part
of its exit checklist so the controller can re-verify the claimed green before
folding the queue row. Optional at the wire (a worker built before done
records existed still succeeds); without a matching `dispatchId` the ledger
write is skipped (a warning is logged) and `signal_done` succeeds normally.

requestId.description: Retry key: reuse the same value and payload after a transport disconnect.

tools.name: signal_done

tools.description:
Report WHERE IN THE RUN you are, mid-task, so dashboards show live per-story progress. Call repeatedly as you advance (contrast signal_done, which is your FINAL act). Fire-and-forget; routes over the same story-keyed stream as signal_done. `phase` is one of: `planning` | `dev` | `review` | `pr` | `blocked` (call this whenever you stop to wait on the human — surfaces that you need them) | `done`. Optional `step`/`total` drive an N-of-M sub-bar; `note` is a short safe-DOM line. Inputs: `sessionId` ($CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID), `phase`.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

note.description: Optional short, human-readable note (rendered untrusted / safe-DOM).

phase.description:
Where in the run you are — one of `planning` | `dev` | `review` | `pr` |
`blocked` | `done`. A closed lifecycle set (NOT the durable story status).

sessionId.description: The calling session's tab id — pass your `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`.

step.description: Optional sub-step index for an N-of-M bar (e.g. `3` of `total`).

total.description: Optional sub-step count for an N-of-M bar.

tools.name: signal_progress

tools.description:
Start one Codex or Claude task with its selected local native subscription account and an exact managed remote workspace. Official local CLI owns provider authentication; remote machine requires Codex 0.159.3 or a newer 0.x release as its execution runtime, without remote provider login. requestId is an immutable UUID; retry never repeats uncertain submission. Explicit accountId requires accountGeneration; omit both for existing active-account/SystemDefault resolution. The task gets CodeSense only; desktop MCP servers come with a saved Agent. No provider credentials cross to the machine; no API billing fallback.
Docs: arc-e-agents/spend-caps.html
tools.name: start_remote_agent_task

tools.description:
Start This Mac's terminal server for this CodeSense instance when none runs (one that runs is only connected to), as opening a terminal does. Returns the same fields as terminal_server_status.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/terminal-servers.html
tools.name: start_terminal_server

tools.description:
Stop This Mac's terminal server for this CodeSense instance, ending every terminal and agent it runs — other CodeSense instances' tabs too; their tabs show as exited. Nothing is launched in its place; the next terminal opened (or start_terminal_server) starts one. Required: `confirmEndSessions: true` and `expected` exactly as terminal_server_status returned it. Refused, and nothing ends, without the confirmation or `expected`, or when the server, its running sessions or the other instances connected changed since (the refusal says what holds now; read the status again). Returns `{ended, ends, otherInstances}`, as reviewed.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/terminal-servers.html

confirmEndSessions.description: Explicit authorization to end every terminal and agent the server runs.

anyOf.description:
What a stop or restart binds to, exactly as `terminal_server_status`
returned it in `expected`: the server, its running sessions, and the
other CodeSense instances connected to it (`null` when it cannot say).

expected.description:
`expected` from `terminal_server_status`. Required for a running

The incompatible server reviewed before authorizing a restart. Unknown
values stay unknown; learning a count after review is also a change.

reviewedIncompatible.description:
For an incompatible restart, pass `{pid, sessions, otherInstances}`

Optional for compatibility; passing it guards against a change.

tools.name: stop_terminal_server

tools.description:
Read the sessions, task tree and totals for one story. Required storyId. Returns {storyId,sessions,tasks,totals,unavailable,historyAsOf,warnings,pages}. sessions (once each, incl. attributed native ones) and tasks are summaries (fields: see include); include:["sessions.full"] gives session_read without conversation plus basis, include:["tasks.full"] adds task_read outcomes. totals (full set, any page) has sessions,costUsd,wallMs,activeMs,idleMs,reviewRounds,reviewTasks,lines. totals.lines={ai:{total,byRuntime:{<listed CLI id>:n,other:n+unlisted}},human,unattributed,total} counts lines added by landed non-merge commits: ai = exact git-ai agent author, human = recorded human, else unattributed (no note, unknown, association only; never human). Notes via the why_line cache; no session join. lines is null with unavailable.lines if any commit can't be attributed (unmerged: unavailable.branches) (no checkout, objects not local, notes changing, incomplete history); never partial. costUsd is null with unavailable.costUsd if any session cost is unknown or no session exists; never partial. wallMs spans first start to last end; activeMs/idleMs sum observed sessions, overlap included. Missing timing has a reason; none: null totals. reviewRounds = complete phase:review review-rounds markers (null + unavailable.reviewRounds if unreadable); reviewTasks = review tasks (else marker tasks; null+unavailable.reviewTasks); a mismatch is warnings.reviewRounds, never a gate. session_story links survive worktree removal and restart; launch links need launch capture. Same scope as session_usage; reads may record branch tips. Also returns branches (name,prs:[numbers],availability:local|remote|missing,basis, latest pr/mergedSha, unavailable reason), prs (observed PRs: number,url/urlReason,mergedSha,mergedAt (mergedSha committer epoch ms)/mergedAtReason,files (landed diff),source:merge-commit|squash-subject,branch or null,basis), worktrees (path,state:live|removed,basis), commits (sha,subject,author,authoredAt epoch ms,files,sessionIds,basis; newest first), total,nextCursor,scanLimit,planned,plannedBase,actual,plannedUntouched. Every array pages by limit; pages.<array>={total,truncated,cursor}. total and totals.commits/files cover every commit. prs[].files and commits[].files list 20, with filesTotal when cut. Over 64 KB the heaviest arrays end a page early. Origin default-branch first-parent scan bounded at scanLimit:2000; merges link exactly by subject branch name or by a second parent at a live or recorded branch tip, with M^1..M^2 commits (shared tips: unavailable.prs); number is #N or a local PR head, else null with numberReason; repeated merges and new live commits combine. Squash PRs have branch:null and commits.unavailable:squash-merged, never an unmatched deleted branch. Missing branches and open PR lookup carry reasons; no GitHub call; a missing merge fetches (see refresh_history). Managed notes use one snapshot/retry: missing promised blobs give basis:unknown + reason, absent notes associated, named sessions exact. planned: backtick Touchpoints paths minus line suffixes; plannedBase: only an explicit Paths are under declaration; root-relative or base+token matches dirs/globs. actual lists path,inPlanned,area (first two segments),decision (first matching Decisions number),lines:{added,removed}|null,linesReason. File lines: the containing branch range once, else each merged PR's first-parent diff once; incomparable branches give unavailable.fileLines. Binary/missing objects: null counts + reason; no Touchpoints: unavailable.planned. Recorded/live-index branch and worktree links are exact; convention-only branches, context-worktree-named sessions and squash PRs are associated; merge PRs inherit branch basis. Missing local evidence keeps durable facts. work_repo replaces source_repo for git reads; no clone: unavailable.commits "work repo not attached". include:["ranges"] adds why_line ranges. Page codesense.storyChanges: full arrays, limit pages commits (default 100); published pages reject include.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

cursor.description:
`pages.<array>.cursor` (or `nextCursor` for commits) from the previous answer, same
story: the next page of that array only, the other arrays empty. Cursors over a
changed set are refused.

include.description:
`ranges`: the current commit page's introduced added-line ranges (path, resolver
session/native IDs, basis and reasons) with rangesBasis and rangesReason; no-note and
merge commits have empty ranges with a reason; without it these fields are omitted.
`sessions.full`: each session as session_read returns it, not its summary
{sessionId,nativeSessionIds,basis,agent,cli,model,branch,worktree,timing,costUsd,
costReason}. `tasks.full`: each task row with its task_read outcome, not its summary
{taskId,parentId,taskType,status,goal (200 chars, goalTruncated),mainSkill,createdAtMs,
closedAtMs,reviews}.

limit.description: Page size of every array (default 20, at most 500). Totals cover the full set.

only.description:
Return only these arrays (plus `totals`); arrays not asked for are absent, not empty.
`tasks`, `sessions` and `reviews` never read git; `commits`, `prs`, `branches`,
`worktrees` and `actual` do. Omit for every array. Without a git array `totals.commits`,
`files` and `lines` are null, with `unavailable.commits`, `files` and `lines` saying why.
`reviews`: the story's complete review rounds, oldest report first, as {id, round, phase,
scope, skill, subjectKind, subjectRef, subjectRev, high, medium, low, dismissed,
converged, reportedAt} (high/medium/low kept findings, dismissed dropped at triage);
unreadable markers give `unavailable.reviews`. A cursor into an array not returned is stale.

items.description: An array a read can be narrowed to (`only`).

oneOf.description:
The story's complete review-round markers: round, phase, scope, skill, subjectRev,
high, medium, low, dismissed, converged and reportedAt. From the records, no git.

tools.name: story_changes

tools.description:
Read many stories' totals at once from this Mac's story totals index, without walking git. Required storyIds: 1 to 500 story ids. Returns {stories, reasons, pending, indexing}. stories maps each id as asked to {totals, unavailable, computedAtMs, refreshing?}, {pending:true} or {error}. totals equals story_changes {storyId}.totals (sessions,commits,files,costUsd,wallMs,activeMs,idleMs,reviewRounds and reviewTasks (null with a reason),lines); unavailable holds its unavailable reasons, each as an index into reasons. Each story also has mergedAt (latest merge, epoch ms; null with mergedAtReason), prs (newest 5 merged PRs as {number,merged}) with prsTotal, and runtimes (ids of the CLIs that reported its usage). It also has firstActivityAt and lastActivityAt (epoch ms over its sessions' usage, commits, merges, tasks and review rounds; null with activityReason when none is recorded) and openSessions (sessions with observed timing and no end that were active in the 15 minutes before computedAtMs, by usage or turn); a row computed before these existed answers them null with activityReason refreshing, never pending. linesInProgress is the lines on story branches not merged yet, shaped like totals.lines (null with linesInProgressReason); they move into totals.lines when the branch merges (after a squash or rebase merge, lines stay here while the story's branch ref still exists, local or on origin, until it is deleted). While a story's commits are still being counted its lines are the earlier ones with refreshing true, or unavailable ("counting in the background") when it had none, never 0. pending: not indexed yet and queued; ask again, never read it as zero. refreshing: something changed since computedAtMs (a commit, merge, session, task or review marker) and a recompute is queued; the values are the last computed. indexing {done,total} counts the indexed stories of this scope. An answer past 240 KB is cut: truncated:true and rest lists the ids left to ask again. Same read-only scope as story_changes. Dashboard codesense.storyTotals: same args, same JSON; kit.storyTotals and hosted CS.storyTotals take any number of ids and merge; hosted asks fit 2 KB of args (about 120 to 150 ids) and keep only the published reasons. Next: story_changes for one story's sessions, tasks and commits.
Docs: arc-e-agents/mcp-only-agents.html

storyIds.description: Story ids, for example DEMO-29; 1 to 500.

tools.name: story_totals

tools.description:
List tasks — the tasks of your own org and team, newest first. Read-only. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused). Optional filters: `story`, `type`, `status` (open, done, abandoned, superseded), `agent` (a saved agent's key, or key@revision), `parent` (the children of a task), `limit` (default 50, max 200). Returns {tasks:[{taskId, goal, taskType, subject, parentId, parentSource, storyId, fieldSources, mainSkill, targets, outcome (the same live plannedVsActual, rework, time and cost facts as task_read), status, rawStatus, closedAtMs, acceptanceMet, label, tamper, layers, unavailable, createdAtMs}]}. `layers` is what each layer was when the task started: its skills with the hash of each skill's files, the source commit and the context commit. The parent playbook is returned by `task_read.playbook`. `fieldSources` records goal/story/subject provenance; explicit task_update refinements survive late capture. A fact CodeSense could not know is absent, with its reason in `unavailable`. Next: task_read for one task's subtree, links and outcome facts.
Docs: arc-e-agents/tasks.html

agent.description: Only tasks run by this saved agent (`key` or `key@revision`).

limit.description: At most this many tasks, newest first (default 50, max 200).

parent.description: Only the children of this task.

sessionId.description: Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused.

status.description: Only tasks in this status: `open`, `done`, `abandoned` or `superseded`.

story.description: Only tasks of the named story.

tools.name: task_list

tools.description:
Read a task — the task, its links, its subtree and what it came to, as facts next to its targets. Read-only. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused), `taskId` (from task_list). Returns {task, links:[{kind, target}], children:[the same shape, for each task below it], outcome, playbook, otherSkills, agentLayers}. `links` hold the task's sessions, its artifacts (for example a review's `design/<story>/review-r1.md`) and its relations (`relates_to:reviews` points at the task a review looked at). `outcome` has `time` ({wallMs, activeMs, idleMs}, summed over the task's sessions), `cost` ({costUsd, models, tokens}), `reviewRounds` (review tasks that relate to this one, in `reviews`), `acceptanceMet`, and `targets` (each target next to its actual, when something measures it). `plannedVsActual` compares task commit files to story touchpoints (exact note-session links, otherwise commits within the task interval); `rework` counts later commits and changed files after the first closed review. Missing story, repository or closed review carries an unavailable reason; `scope` remains session or interval for time attribution; `otherSkills.skills` lists indexed skill invocations beyond the main skill. `agentLayers.sessions` joins each linked session record: {sessionId, agent (key@revision), manifestHash, unavailable}; missing facts say why. `playbook` is the parent skill and hash. Session root tasks cover the session; other tasks use their start-to-close interval for time, usage and skills. Missing evidence carries an unavailable reason. A task closed through signal_done also carries `tamper` ({flag, files}): whether files the team's policy calls tests or checks were edited during the task. Everything is a fact; nothing is a score. Only tasks of your own org and team are returned.
Docs: arc-e-agents/tasks.html

sessionId.description: Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused.

taskId.description:
The task to read, from `task_list` (a session's task is that session's id; a story's
root task is `story:<id>`).

tools.name: task_read

tools.description:
Start a task — a plain-words record of one thing you are doing, so it can be judged against its own goal and targets and improved over time. Every launched session already has a task, made from its brief; use this for a sub-task inside a session, for example a review pass or an exploration. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused, and identity comes from the verified connection), `goal` (plain words; at most 280 characters are kept). Optional: `type` (a tag: exploratory, feature, bugfix, review, routine, ops, or the team's own; omitted: unclassified, with the reason), `subject` (a free tag such as code, design, doc, security), `parent` (a task id; omitted: your own session's task), `story`, `skill` (the main skill's name), `targets` (for example {"wall_minutes": 60}, over the type's defaults from the team's tasks/task-types.yml), `links` ([{kind, target}] with kind `session`, `artifact` or `relates_to:<verb>`; a review of another task links {kind:"relates_to:reviews", target:<task id>} and its artifact path). A review is just a task of type `review`: there are no review-specific fields. A delta round in the same reviewer session is its own task: one `task_start {type:"review", links:[relates_to:reviews]}` per round. Returns the task: {taskId, goal, taskType, subject, parentId, parentSource, storyId, mainSkill, targets, layers, status, unavailable, ...}; a fact CodeSense could not know is absent, with its reason in `unavailable`. Nothing here scores an agent. Next: task_update to refine or close it, task_read for its outcome facts.
Docs: arc-e-agents/tasks.html

goal.description: What the task is to achieve, in plain words (at most 280 characters are kept).

links.description: Links to add, for example `{"kind":"relates_to:reviews","target":"<task id>"}`.

items.description: A link a task is given: `kind` is `session`, `artifact` or `relates_to:<verb>`.

parent.description: The task this one sits under. Omitted: your own session's task.

sessionId.description: Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused.

skill.description: The main skill this task runs, by name.

story.description: The story this task works. Omitted: its parent's current story, then your session's.

subject.description: A free tag refining the type, for example `code`, `design`, `doc`, `security`.

targets.description: Targets for this task, over the type's defaults, for example `{"wall_minutes": 60}`.

type.description:
The task type tag, for example `exploratory`, `feature`, `bugfix`, `review`, `routine`
or `ops`. Omitted: `unclassified`, with the reason.

tools.name: task_start

tools.description:
Update a task — refine it, record its verdict, or close it. Required: `sessionId` (your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused), `taskId` (from task_list; a launched session's task is that session's id, a story's root task is `story:<id>`). Optional, each changing only itself: `goal`, `type`, `subject`, `story` (link a task made without one; a task with no parent then goes under that story's root task), `parent` (re-attach under another task, never inside its own subtree), `targets` (set over the current ones; recorded as set by task_update), `acceptanceMet` (true or false: whether the acceptance criteria were met; the lead sets it), `label` ({verdict: good|bad, why}: a person's verdict, kept with who gave it and when, so the Steward can be calibrated against it), `status` (done, abandoned or superseded: closes the task), `links` ([{kind, target}] as in task_start). A launched session's task also closes by itself when the session calls signal_done, and a routine run's when the run ends; the first close stands. Only tasks of your own org and team can be changed. Returns the task. Nothing here scores an agent. Next: task_read for the outcome facts.
Docs: arc-e-agents/tasks.html

acceptanceMet.description: Whether the task's acceptance criteria were met.

anyOf.description: A human's verdict on a task.

label.description: A verdict to keep with the task, so the Steward can be calibrated against it.

items.description: A link a task is given: `kind` is `session`, `artifact` or `relates_to:<verb>`.

parent.description: Re-attach the task under another task, never one inside its own subtree.

sessionId.description: Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`; another session's id is refused.

story.description: Link the task to a story. A task with no parent then goes under that story's root task.

targets.description: Targets to set over the current ones. They are recorded as set by `task_update`.

tools.description:
This Mac's terminal server for this CodeSense instance (it hosts every terminal tab and agent, and outlives the app): `state` (`running`, `stopped`, `incompatible` — this build cannot use it until it is restarted —, `unreachable`, or `notApplicable` when this app hosts its terminals itself), `pid`, `version`, `startedAtMs`, `sessions` (running or exited but kept), `running`, `runningAgents`, `exitedKept`, `ends` (in words: the running sessions a stop or restart ends, the agents among them and the other instances whose tabs end too; unknown counts are said to be unknown), `connectedInstances` (CodeSense instances connected, this one included; `null` when the server cannot say), `otherInstances`, `unowned` (`[{session, command, startedAtMs, running, runningAgent}]`: sessions no app holds — opened by a CodeSense instance gone for 5 minutes or more, and shown nowhere), `expected` (what stop_terminal_server and restart_terminal_server bind to: `{serverId, epoch, pid, sessionIds, otherInstances}` — pass it back unchanged) and `detail` (why something is unknown). Never starts a server.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/terminal-servers.html

Test an explicit machine draft. Observe fingerprint first; pass trustedHostKeyFp explicitly only after trust is authorized. mode defaults to private-account, the only mode that opens terminal tabs. Does not save, except that a saved legacy machine tested with mode private-account is converted in place (same id, host key and settings) before its private setup.

tools.description:
Take a dashboard down: sets its dashboard.yml publish.state back to draft and the local record to unpublished, then blocks viewing on the share host and clears cached live answers. Unpublish deletes all hosted file versions. publish.retain in dashboard.yml keeps current or 1–5 versions (default 5), applied on the next new version commit. hostedFilesDeleted reports {versions, files}, or null when unknown. Pass dashboard as the absolute folder path. Refused unless the dashboard is published, or a takedown is still pending. hostedCopy is removed, or still_live with hostedCopyError: takedown or file deletion is unconfirmed, so call unpublish_dashboard again to retry (a build with no dashboard host cannot retry). The output's visibility is null, because unpublish does not read it. A child agent cannot unpublish a parent's dashboard, even when shared; a human can.
Docs: arc-i-dashboard-primitives/your-first-dashboard.html

dashboard.description: Absolute path of the dashboard folder on this Mac (the folder holding dashboard.yml).

Un-route file from context — the inverse of route_file_to_context. Stops managing the file and un-hides it from git (strip-exclude LAST). The team content copy is deleted only when route_file_to_context created it (and it still holds what was routed); a file that was hydrated, launched or adopted is only unmanaged, its team file kept. Each step is idempotent, so re-running after an interruption completes cleanly.
Docs: arc-k-sync/moving-between-contexts.html

logicalName.description: Repo-relative, `/`-separated path of the previously-routed file.

Move an authorized shared declaration back to personal scope.

tools.description:
Update the canonical profile's CodeSense docs to this app's bundled version, OFFLINE and independently of the caller's working directory. Explicit replacement preserves local HEAD/history, staged content, tracked edits and nonignored untracked files on a named local branch before checkout. Returns docs versions/state, root, preservationBranch and changedPaths; ignored machine state stays in place and collisions are refused. A current clean copy is a no-op. No network or remote is used.
Docs: arc-a-first-touch/identity-menu-and-switcher.html
tools.name: update_codesense_docs

tools.description:
Update terminal servers to this app's build, ending every terminal and agent each one runs (tabs reopen; agents as shells unless their Agent has resumeAfterRestart). Required: `orgSlug`, `confirmEndSessions: true`, `expected` (`{machineId: {serverId, epoch, sessionIds, pid?}}` exactly as list_out_of_date_terminal_servers returned it — `sessionIds` required), and `machineIds` or `all: true`. Refused, and nothing ends, without `confirmEndSessions`, for an unknown machine, without a machine's `expected` or its `sessionIds`, or when a server is no longer as listed (another server or lifetime, or a session not listed: list again). Each machine is checked again right before its update; one that changed by then is skipped. A machine that is not out of date is skipped, with why. Asynchronous: returns `{opId, machines, skipped}` at once; machines update remote first, This Mac after, your own machine last — your own tab may end before any reply. The outcome (each machine updated, skipped or failed, and what reopened) goes to the verified caller's inbox. A supplied `sessionId` must name that caller; an unbound MCP caller is refused. Gated by the Interactive tier.
Docs: arc-d-terminals-and-machines/terminal-servers.html

confirmEndSessions.description: Explicit authorization to end every terminal and agent each server runs.

additionalProperties.description:
What one machine's update binds to, as `list_out_of_date_terminal_servers`
returned it.

sessionIds.description:
The sessions confirmed ending (required: an update is never bound to
a count alone).

sessions.description: The confirmed session count (the length of `sessionIds` when given).

machineIds.description: Which machines; or `all: true` for every out-of-date one.

sessionId.description:
Your own `$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID`: the outcome goes to your inbox,
and your own machine is updated last.

tools.name: update_terminal_servers

tools.description:
Move a workspace that lives on a machine to the newest commit of its base. "Newest" means what baseRef (the ref it was prepared from) names in YOUR attached local clone now — fetch or pull there first if you want the provider's latest. Name the workspace by machineId + workspaceHandle, or by storyId / workspaceId of an open workspace (add teamKey if more than one team matches). Only the commits the machine lacks are sent (an incremental Git bundle; an interrupted update resumes its upload when retried). The worktree fast-forwards only when it is clean, including CodeSense-copied files nobody edited, and its branch has no commits of its own: otherwise it is refused (refusedDirty with the changes in dirty, or refusedDiverged) and nothing changes. If the new base tracks files that already exist in the workspace, the update is refused (refusedManagedOverlap): managedOverlap lists unedited CodeSense copies, modifiedManaged lists edited ones (publish or discard those first; reverse_sync_worktree previews them), unmanagedOverlap lists other ignored files. WARNING: removeManagedCopies:true deletes the unedited CodeSense copies in managedOverlap and replaces them with the repo's versions; edited copies and other files are never removed. Progress arrives as workspace-base-progress events keyed by the workspace handle. Returns status (updated, upToDate or a refusal), previousCommit, commit and bundleBytes. Re-opening a workspace never updates its base.
Docs: arc-c-workspaces-and-worktrees/workspace-and-tab-lifecycle.html

machineId.description:
The machine the workspace lives on. Optional when `storyId` or
`workspaceId` names an open workspace that lives on a machine.

removeManagedCopies.description:
When the new base tracks files CodeSense copied into the workspace,
remove those copies and update (default: refuse and list them). Only
unedited copies are ever removed; the repo's version replaces them.

storyId.description: An open story workspace's story id.

teamKey.description: The team whose open workspaces are searched, when more than one matches.

workspaceHandle.description: The managed workspace handle (`remote-workspace-…`) on the workspace record.

Supply inline content or a path (at least one); content takes precedence. Returns valid, detectedKind, findings and checked scope. Does not execute scripts or prove runtime liveness.

Validate a candidate CodeSense file BEFORE writing it. Pass `path` (preferred — anchors depends_on/supporting_docs checks) and/or inline `content`. Detects intent (plain_doc | pipeline_story | epic_main_doc) and never nags a plain doc. For a story, returns blocking + advisory findings ({code, field, severity, message, hint}) computed with the same parser + source_repo/type rules the pipeline cache uses. Never returns valid:true for a file it could not fully evaluate.

`path` from disk when provided.
